News.title: Shocking moment huge waves repeatedly slam packed ferry against pier as horrified Brit tourists watch on
News.content:
THIS is the moment massive waves slam a ferry into a pier as stunned British tourists look on in horror.

Chaos erupted at the Positano port on Italy’s Amalfi Coast as giant waves caused a dramatic mooring for one tourist ferry.



Wild footage captured by a British holidaymaker showed passengers screaming in terror as the huge waves swell causing the boat to violently smash into the dock.

One woman who experienced the ordeal said being on the boat was “100 times worse than the video shows”.



Tourists could be heard swearing as the boat’s boarding steps crashed into the edge of the dock while the vessel was battered by rough seas and strong winds.

White water surged over the pier forcing those waiting to quickly flee.

Shaken tourists aboard the ferryboat hung onto the railings as the crew struggled to execute the docking in the extreme weather.

After struggling for some time crew eventually raised the boarding ladder and pulled away from the harbour before making several more attempts to dock.



The ferry was eventually able to berth safely and no injuries were reported.

One person said: “We were struggling to get off, and people were struggling to get on.

“It was a crazy boat ride where seawater splashed on the passengers and people barely held on.

“We got off safely and everyone survived.



“But it was a crazy experience.”

The footage has reignited concerns over safety at the iconic Amalfi Coast resort during periods of severe weather, when high winds and rough seas can make docking particularly hazardous.

Famed for its luxury hotels, dramatic cliffside towns and sweeping views, tourism at the Amalfi Coast is a sore spot for many locals.

It comes as a hero 16-year-old lifeguard faces a drowing boy at a Californian beach.



Footage shows powerful waves bashing the youngster at Seabright State Beach in Santa Cruz as the teenager, named by local media as Ryder, holds on to him, without thinking of his own life.

Multiple bystanders attempt to help Ryder – first forming a human chain to pull them out – but the waves pummel them down and they are forced to abandon the mission.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A second lifeguard enters the monstrous churn and eventually the pair drag the youngster back to the beach.

Donald Trump’s son, Eric, shared the video on X, describing the lifeguard’s bravery as “truly the best of America.”

News.title: Man ‘sexually assaulted by male stranger who grabbed his hair and kissed him on the neck’ in town park
News.content:
PARK PROBE Man ‘sexually assaulted by male stranger who grabbed his hair and kissed him on the neck’ in town park

A MAN was allegedly sexually assaulted by a male stranger who grabbed his hair and kissed him on the neck in a town park.

The incident happened in the early hours of July 12 in Wellingborough, Northamptonshire, with police now appealing for witnesses.

Cops said a man was approached by an unknown male in the field and footpath area of Croyland Road between 12.45am and 1.15am.

The suspect then allegedly grabbed the man by the hair and “kissed or attempted to kiss” him on the neck before fleeing.





Northamptonshire Police are now urging anyone who may have witnessed or has information on the incident to come forward.

A force spokesperson said: “Police officers investigating a sexual assault in Wellingborough are appealing for witnesses and information.

“The incident happened between 12.45am and 1.15am on Sunday, July 12, in the field and footpath area off Croyland Road, Wellingborough.

“A man was approached by an unknown male who then allegedly grabbed him by the hair and kissed or attempted to kiss him on the neck before leaving the area.

“Officers are keen to hear from anyone who witnessed the incident, saw either man in the area at the time, or has any information which could assist their enquiries.

“Witnesses or anyone with information are asked to contact Northamptonshire Police on 101.”

They added: “Please quote incident number 26000416679 when providing any information to make sure it gets to the right person as quickly as possible.

News.title: Mum GUILTY of murdering girl, 2, sexually abused by stepdad in torture campaign that left her with 21 broken bones
News.content:
A MUM has been found guilty of murdering her two-year-old daughter who was sexually abused by her killer stepdad.

Little Isabelle Rose Welsh, two, suffered a catastrophic brain injury at the hands of Alexandra Walker and her boyfriend Harrison Simpson.



The toddler was left with 21 broken bones before her death on 14 September last year and had also been sexually assaulted.

Walker and Simpson have now been convicted of murder following a harrowing trial.



Simpson was convicted of sexual abuse of a child, while both were found guilty of child cruelty.

Teesside Crown Court was told Simpson and Walker began a relationship in the summer of 2025.

Mr Wright said the relationship was “unhealthy” and “characterised by drink on the part of Walker and drugs on the part of Simpson”.

The court heard this led to a “decline over time in the care that was being given to Isabelle”, which then “built into her being subjected to regular violence at home by these two defendants”.



Isabelle’s grandmother Claire Walker had become “seriously worried” about the youngster’s deteriorating health during the final days of her life and described her as looking “white as a sheet”.

When she messaged Walker asking whether she could pick up supplies for Isabelle from Asda, Walker replied: “Ten cans of Stella for my stress and nappies.”

The court also heard how Claire told police the toddler was chatty and intelligent and had generally been in good health up to her sustaining a broken leg for which she received hospital treatment.

After Walker and Isabelle were allowed home, the grandmother visited them and spotted a bruise on Isabelle’s back.

She told detectives she said “what the hell” when she saw it but Walker claimed Isabelle had bumped her head on the settee.



Hearbreaking footage showed the tot before she was murdered running around the garden clutching a red witch’s hat.

Just days later, Isabelle was found collapsed at the foot of the stairs covered in bruises, with “no pulse and plainly gravely ill”.

Jurors heard she had been violently shaken and slammed against a “hard, unyielding” surface on September 13 last year before passing away in hospital in the early hours of the following morning.



Richard Wright, KC, prosecuting, said: “This was no accident. It was the deliberate infliction of injury on that little girl.

”It was, say the prosecution, murder.

“Neither was the assault on Isabelle an isolated act of violence towards her.”

On the day of her daughter’s death, Walker only called 999 after being told to do so by her stepfather “long after she must have known her daughter was critically ill”, it was said.

A post mortem revealed Isabelle had suffered a catalogue of injuries – including 21 broken bones and 97 soft-tissue injuries.



She had internal tears from violent sexual assaults and there was evidence from a pathologist to say she appeared to have been swung by a limb, the court heard.

Mr Wright said: “Her death was caused by the deliberate infliction of a devastating head injury that required the application of significant force.

“Any person who violently shakes a two-year-old child before hitting there head off a hard and unyielding surface so that their skull is fractured and their heart stops beating can only intend to cause that child really serious injury or to kill her. This was an act of murder.

“But it was murder that came at the conclusion of a campaign of violence against her not over hours, or days but over weeks.

“She was beaten, her bones were broken and she was in obvious and severe pain for weeks.



“It was absolutely plain that she was being seriously abused we suggest and the only people who had access to her so as to have inflicted those injuries over that period of time were Harrison Simpson and Alexandra Walker.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Both Walker and Simpson denied murder, allowing the death of a child, sexual assault and child cruelty.

They will be sentenced on a later date.

News.title: Child, 5, seriously injured after double-decker bus crashes into house – as man in his 60s arrested
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

BUS HORROR Child, 5, seriously injured after double-decker bus crashes into house – as man in his 60s arrested

A FIVE-YEAR-OLD boy has been rushed to hospital with serious injuries after a double-decker bus ploughed into a house on a coastal road.

Emergency services were scrambled to Torquay Road, Devon, after a bus filled with passengers slammed into a home on Monday.

A five-year-old boy from Torquay, who was riding on the bus, was rushed to Bristol Children’s Hospital with serious injuries.

A man in his 60s from Torbay has been arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by careless driving.





He remains in police custody while enquiries into the horror are ongoing.

Ambulance crews assessed a further 14 passengers at the scene of the smash.

Emergency medics concluded that the other passengers did not require hospital treatment.

The road was closed in both directions for a total of seven hours in the wake of the smash.

Roads policing officers conducted a forensic examination of the scene and the bus was recovered.

Devon and Cornwall Police said: “Officers are now appealing for witnesses to come forward.

“They are keen to hear from anyone who may have relevant CCTV, doorbell, mobile phone or dashcam footage.

“Anyone with information is asked to contact police through the Force website or by telephone on 101, quoting reference 50260198141.”

News.title: Husband finds five dead babies in boxes at home he shares with pregnant wife ‘after row with her about what was in them’
News.content:
BODIES IN BOXES Husband finds five dead babies in boxes at home he shares with pregnant wife ‘after row with her about what was in them’

A HUSBAND has found the remains of five dead babies hidden in cardboard boxes following an argument with his wife soon after she gave birth.

The macabre discoveries were made at a house in Orange, in south-east France on Monday morning.



Local prosecutors opened a criminal investigation after the 32-year-old wife – who cannot be named for legal reasons – was reported to police by her husband.

An investigating source said: “The woman was complaining about abdominal pain when they argued, the day after she gave birth on Sunday.



“The husband stayed behind when she was taken to hospital, and looked inside the cardboard boxes they had been arguing over – that’s when he found the five dead babies.

“All the fetuses were decomposing, and had a been around for quite a while.”

The boxes containing the remains of the babies were all in the same plastic bag.

A source close to the investigation told Le Parisien that the man took the bag the hospital, which reported the incident to police.

The source told the outlet the woman had suffered three failed pregnancies before giving birth on Monday.

The couple have two other living children, aged eight and twelve, beyond the newborn.



They are now involved in the enquiry opened by Carpentras prosecutor’s office.

There have been no arrests in connection with the case yet.

The woman remains in the hospital and has not been taken into custody.



It comes months after the remains of two babies were discovered in the freezer of a mans home in Aillevillers-et-Lyaumont, Haute-Saône, France.

Cops launched an investigation , with officers searching for the man’s partner – both in their 50s.

The mother of nine reportedly left the home voluntarily in December 2025, according to L’Est Républicain.

She was arrested in February, in Boulogne-Billancourt, where one of her sons resides.

And five years earlier a widower found the dead bodies of three babies in a locked cupboard while cleaning his home months after his wife’s death.



The bodies – believed to be foetuses – were found in plastic bags and wrapped in clothing.

The widower ,41, who has not been named, called police after uncovering the rotting baby body in a locked cabinet in his garage, which he had forced open.

Police scrambled to the man’s property in the sleepy town of Mezeray, France only to find another two decomposing bodies in a shed nearby.

Cops said both were found in plastic bags with kitchen knives nearby, according to new website RTL.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The couple were childless while the woman had two children from a previous relationship, RTL reports.



The man and several relatives were questioned by French police.

News.title: Mum killed her son, nine, before taking her own life after finding her partner on a dating site, inquest told
News.content:
TRAGIC DEATH Mum killed her son, nine, before taking her own life after finding her partner on a dating site, inquest told

A MUM killed her nine-year-old son before taking her own life after finding her partner on a dating site, an inquest heard.

Tasmin Paterson, 31, and Hudson Paterson were found dead at home in the Fletchersbridge area of Bodmin, Cornwall, in September 2024.



A court heard Tasmin’s relationship with her partner Marcus Hughes had been on the “verge” of ending before the horror.

Marcus had discovered the mum and his stepson in a bedroom at the property they shared.



He told the inquest the relationship had become “fraught” and strained after she discovered he had been on a dating site.

Marcus added: “We’d not broken up necessarily but we were on the verge, I felt.



“She believed it was to do with her ongoing health issues, but there were more things going on than that.”

Cornwall Coroner’s Court heard Tasmin had battled with health problems after suffering a head injury.

She experienced mobility problems as a result and was also under strain from financial and housing issues.

Senior coroner Andrew Cox said: “Mr Hughes was Tasmin’s partner at the time of her death and he accepted that while their relationship had been good and healthy and strong at the outset, more recently it had run into difficulties.

News.title: Suicide drones SWARM Moscow as Trump meets Zelensky & North Korea sends 30k more troops to boost desperate Putin’s ranks
News.content:
UKRAINE unleashed a swarm of suicide drones on Moscow hours before Volodymyr Zelensky and Donald Trump are due to meet today.

Nearly 400 unmanned aircraft overwhelmed the sky over Russia’s capital and the wider region – as mayor Sergei Sobyanin claimed that “most” had been intercepted.



Flames engulfed a logistics warehouse at Podolsk, and an apartment block in Chekhov was also hit.

The strike in Podolsk on the e 3PL logistics company was close to a massive warehouse belonging to Wildberries – Russia’s version of Amazon – which appeared undamaged.



While Ukraine has stepped up attacks on Russian retail warehouses as well as large oil refineries, the war-torn country is running out of desperately-needed air defence.

The Ukrainian President is expected to use his White House visit to press his US counterpart today.



Amid improving relations with US President Donald Trump, he will seek tougher sanctions against Russian tyrant Vladimir Putin.

Zelensky is also calling for urgent anti-ballistic defence missiles to protect Ukrainians from Russian attack.



“Our top priority is anti-ballistic defence and strategic cooperation with America. Peace must come closer,” he said.

At a previous meeting in Washington in October 2025, Zelensky failed to convince Trump to provide Ukraine with Tomahawk cruise missiles.

And during heated exchanges in the Oval Office in February that year, both clashed during an argument in the full glare of television cameras.



The US leader has since changed his tone and during their last encounter in Turkey earlier this month, he said Zelensky had done “an amazing job”.

It comes as North Korea reaffirmed its support for Russia’s war on Ukraine as the nations’ foreign ministers met in Moscow.

Russia reportedly plans to enlist 30,000 North Korean soldiers for a full offensive in Ukraine, Zelesky said over the weekend.

But it is not the first time Ukrainian officials have sounded the alarm on the nations cooperation.

The US confirmed in 2024 that at least 3,000 of Kim Jong Un’s troops had entered Russian territory.



Huge numbers of North Korean forces were killed after the deployment to Russia’s Kursk region.

Pyongyang has also supplied Moscow with weapons systems, in return securing financial assistance, food, energy supplies and military technology, analysts say.

Ukraine, South Korea and the US have voiced deep concern about possible military cooperation between the two.



Kim Jong Un lords over one of the world’s largest militaries – with some 1.2 million soldiers.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Fears were sparked again earlier this year when footage showed a wave of suited North Koreans touching down in Russia.

Kim Jong Un last travelled to Russia in September 2023, and Putin made a rare visit to Pyongyang in June 2024.

News.title: Moment French warship fires ‘intimidation’ shots near top Tory MP in the Channel during migrant surge
News.content:
A FRENCH warship fired “intimidation” shots near the Shadow Home Secretary in the Channel this morning.

Tory MP Chris Philp was out at sea monitoring small boat migrant crossings when the gunboat unleashed a barrage of ammunition.



He was in the middle of filming a broadcast interview when the crack of 17 live rounds could suddenly be heard.

Mr Philp, who is contacting the ambassador about the incident, said: “On the Channel today monitoring illegal migrant crossings.



“As I was being interviewed by the BBC just now a French warship approached close and fired 17 live rounds behind us.

“There was no notice or training exercise in place. Felt like warning shots or attempted intimidation.”



The French warship was seen close to Mr Philp’s fishing boat in the international shipping lane.

The French Navy, which helps patrol the Channel, has not yet responded to Mr Philp’s allegation.

Warm weather has seen a spike in small boat crossings with more than 900 making the journey last week.

Mr Philp added: “It is extraordinary that the French navy will fire live rounds to defend their waters against a visiting British politician but cannot bear to do anything about stopping illegal Channel crossings.



“If France showed people smugglers half the seriousness they showed me, the boats would stop. Instead, the French wave them through and pass them off to the British coastguard so it’s our problem.

“I will be raising this incident with the French ambassador.”

The French Navy often escorts the crammed dinghies from the shallows into British waters where they are then picked up by Border Force.

Mr Philp’s allegations could spark a fresh diplomatic incident with France amid years of tensions in the Channel.

Britain is also paying France close to £1billion pounds for its help stopping illegal migration.



Home Office figures show 881 arrived in Dover since crossings resumed on Wednesday after days of windy conditions — including 165 on a 42ft-long mega-dinghy.

It beat the record of 128 for the most migrants getting here from France on one vessel.

The Home Office said: “We are bearing down on small boat crossings, with removals at record levels and asylum claims down by 12 per cent. We have removed or deported almost 70,000 people who were here illegally — an increase of 41 per cent.”

The attack lasted from 8.30pm last night to dawn this morning as the Ukrainian President drove home confidence that Kyiv is turning around the Russian full-scale invasion.

A logistics warehouse serving several Russian companies in the village of Koledino, 12 miles south of Moscow, was set ablaze in the attack. News.title: Trump live: Zelensky and Netanyahu at White House as Donald set to quiz Putin
News.content:
Donald Trump is set to hold important talks with Volodymyr Zelensky and Benjamin Netanyahu at the White House today, who are both in Washington for the funeral of Senator Lindsey Graham

Donald Trump is set to hold separate talks with Volodymyr Zelensky and Benjamin Netanyahu at the White House today - just days after Zelensky accused Russia of helping Iran target US troops.

Both the Ukrainian president and Israeli prime minister are in Washington DC to attend the funeral of Senator Lindsey Graham, who died earlier this month aged 71.

Zelensky has said he plans to discuss strengthening Ukraine's anti-ballistic missile defences with Trump. It comes after the Ukrainian leader said on Saturday that Kyiv has intelligence indicating Russia shared satellite imagery with Tehran, enabling Iran to target US military bases in the Middle East. Trump said that he will "find out if that's true" and "ask Putin about it".

After meeting Zelensky, Trump will hold talks with Netanyahu - his first in-person meeting with the Israeli prime minister since the US-Israeli war on Iran began on February 28.

News.title: 'Wardrobe malfunction on my wedding day sparked two-year battle with my bank'
News.content:
'Wardrobe malfunction on my wedding day sparked two-year battle with my bank'

Rachel vowed to 'not give up' after the drama on her wedding day

View 2 Images Rachel had a problem with her dress (stock image) (Image: Tony Anderson)

A bride says a wardrobe malfunction on her wedding day sparked a wrangle with her bank which lasted almost two years. Rachel, who did not give her last name, was enjoying her big day when the zip on her £1600 wedding dress broke.

‌



She waited until after the wedding to contact the shop where she had bought the dress from to notify them of the problem. She was told they would look into it but she never heard anything else.

‌



That made her apply for a chargeback. This is a rule that a number of debit, credit, and charge cards have to claim your money back when you do not receive the goods or services you paid for. It is not a legal right.

‌



Unfortunately for Rachel, her quest was denied and, for the best part of two years, she thought that was the end of the matter. However, she decided to put in a Section 75 claim, which is when your credit card company has a legal responsibility to help you with something if there is a problem with an item or service that you paid more than £100 for.

Speaking to MoneySavingExpert - the site set up by Martin Lewis - Rachel explained: "On my wedding day, the zip on my wedding dress broke. I contacted the shop after the wedding and they apologised and told me they would investigate, but I never received a response.

"I asked my bank to chargeback but it was unsuccessful and there was nothing I could do. Nearly two years later, almost on a whim, I submitted a Section 75 claim with my evidence to support my case. The bank upheld the claim in part and offered me £800 (50% of the purchase price)."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Chargeback and Section 75

If you buy something and you do not feel you have received what you have paid for, you can attempt a chargeback. This is when you ask your bank to 'reverse the transaction' and give you a refund.

Terms and conditions vary depending on your card supplier, but it is basically you bak asking the supplier's bank for a refund. It should still work even if the supplier has since gone bust as it retrieves the money from the supplier's bank and not the supplier itself - although MoneySavingExpert warns that this is not always the case.

‌



The key point is that you must be able to prove a breach of contract and the firm in question will not give you a refund. You must ask the business involved for a refund first. You are usually covered for 120 days, meaning any problem that arises after this period is usually not protected. You are also not protected when using PayPal, or when you only pay the deposit on the card.

View 2 Images Rachel's zip on her wedding dress broke on her big day

Section 75 is named after the part of the Consumer Credit Act 1974 where it can be found. This lets you raise a claim against your bank or lender for a breach of contract or misrepresentation by the supplier of goods or services.

‌



The Financial Ombudsman Service says that, to launch a Section 75 claim, you should:

explain to your bank or lender that you want them to help resolve an issue with something you paid for using a card or loan they provided

mention that you’d like them to consider the chargeback and Section 75 process

make sure you have supporting information about your dispute

The bank or lender should look at whether they can raise a chargeback or a Section 75 claim. If you are unhappy with their response, you can complain to them. If you are still not satisfied, the ombudsman may be able to help.

Article continues below

The ombudsman says: "The Consumer Rights Act 2015 is often relevant. This sets out the protection that consumers have when buying goods and services. For example, it says that goods should be of ‘satisfactory quality’ and services should be performed with ‘reasonable care and skill’.

"There are also other relevant laws that are specific to certain situations, such as purchases of package travel holidays. Your bank or lender should be able to tell you which laws apply to your situation, but if you’re unhappy with their response, you can raise a complaint."

News.title: France wildfires spark 300,000 evacuations as locals say devastation 'is like Pompeii'
News.content:
France wildfires spark 300,000 evacuations as locals say devastation 'is like Pompeii'

Images from Le Grand-Crohot campsite in Lege-Cap-Ferret in south west France showed the charred remains of cars, vans, push bikes and buildings, as locals say there were scenes reminiscent of Pompeii

BREAKING France forest fires- Thousands of tourists evacuated from campsites popular with Brits

Firefighters were racing to control wildfires in searing heat today as Bordeaux residents said the conditions were 'like Pompeii'. Stark images from Lege-Cap-Ferret in south west France showed the charred remains of cars, vans, push bikes and buildings. Locals said there were scenes reminiscent of Pompeii after the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in AD 79 as they fled to safety, the air thick with smoke.

‌



Temperatures of 39C are forecast just as the latest heatwave of the summer hits the UK. Bordeaux resident Chris de Abrea said: "It reminds me a little bit of Pompeii, especially over the weekend. The air was quite smoky; it was quite difficult to breathe. The smell of burning was pretty much all around the city."

‌



View 5 Images Blackened charred remains of bikes after the evacuation of the residents in Lege-Cap-Ferret.

‌

The wildfire has burned more than 42,000 hectares, destroying 240 homes. More than 300,000 people have been evacuated across France and Spain. French President Emmanuel Macron has said the wildfires raging near Bordeaux are the toughest since the Second World War.

He said: "We must understand we are facing a completely unprecedented wildfire. The situation we are dealing with is the most severe we have ever recorded."

"Every available resource has been deployed with more than 1,500 military personnel helping to tackle the fire." Mr Macron added that firebreaks have been dug and reinforced to stop the fire's advance.

‌



Chris said that while many in the Bordeaux were "just getting on" with their lives, others are contemplating staying with relatives elsewhere.

"The main concerns for people are, 'where do I go from here if I don’t have family?' and then, 'will I see my home again?'."

View 5 Images Burnt camping equipment at Le Grand-Crohot Ocean camping, in Lege-Cap-Ferret.

‌



He never thought things would come to the situation now unfolding near Bordeaux, describing it as "almost surreal". He added: "It's just scary to know that the fire could get this close."

Spain's national weather service warned of extreme fire risk due to intense heat and dryness across the country. Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said controlling the country's wildfires was absolutely crucial. María Eugenia Olive, the technical director of the Official Association of Forest Technical Engineers, said firefighting efforts were becoming increasingly complicated due to the high temperatures forecast this week. It was forecast to hit 39C in southern Europe. One resident was evacuated from her home in Saint-Médard-en-Jalles in south west France on Saturday morning, along with her British partner, and their son, 19.

View 5 Images Wrecked vehicles in a business park following a wildfire in Biscarrosse, southwestern France

‌



She told the Mirror: "We were evacuated on Friday night. All of us and two dogs left and escaped to Agen, where we booked into a hotel. The air quality in Bordeaux has massively improved now. Inside the ring motorway, you wouldn't really know that this disaster is happening now. There's been a huge wave of solidarity here with hundreds and hundreds of people offering a room or two to those who have had to be evacuated, and 9,000 people registered as volunteers to help with various things.

"We're all worried things could deteriorate again though, as we enter the fourth heatwave of the year, and if winds start blowing towards Bordeaux again.

"Being evacuated felt very surreal. You see it in films and in the news, but you don't really think it's going to happen to you, so you feel like you're seeing yourself from the outside, and everything happens both fast and in slow motion.

‌



View 5 Images A map showing the fires across south west France

"There was fear when we evacuated. We turned off the gas supply, closed windows and shutters and all doors.

"I couldn't help thinking that maybe this was the last time I would see my house. I was thinking of everything of sentimental value, especially precious photos of my late parents.

‌



"I picked up three or four small objects connected to my mum at the last minute. I didn't really think of expensive belongings, but just those that connected me with my loved ones.

"We left our house in the car at 1.45am. Lots of cars were coming out of private driveways, there was no sense of panic. The flames were still 14km away, and we trusted everything would be done to stop them from reaching the suburbs of Bordeaux."

View 5 Images Wildfires blaze in south-western France close to Bordeaux (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Article continues below

This latest spell of heatwave threshold-level temperatures is expected to peak in the south-east and east of England this week. The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has warned the rising temperatures could increase health risks, particularly for vulnerable groups. It has issued amber heat health alerts.

The heatwave will not be felt in all parts of the country, with clouds and outbreaks of rain continuing in Northern Ireland, Scotland and northern England. The hot weather will be focused on central, southern and eastern England on Tuesday thought it may spread slightly northwards and westwards into midweek.

Temperatures in England and Wales are forecast to rise to around 25-32C this week. They are expected to reach 30-35C across the Midlands, southern and eastern England.

News.title: 'Extra £111 cost' for UK families in new bill update
News.content:
'Extra £111 cost' for UK families in new bill update

Experts warn bills could climb even higher this winter

View 3 Images The rise comes as wholesale UK gas prices have surged 42% over the past month (Image: LordHenriVoton via Getty Images)

Households have been warned to make a crucial change now as wholesale gas prices jump 42% and experts fear another painful rise in bills this winter

‌



Families looking to shield themselves from soaring energy bills have been hit by a fresh blow after the cost of the cheapest fixed tariff rocketed by £111 in just two weeks. New analysis shows the best fixed deal on the market has climbed from £1,424 a year to £1,535 since the middle of July – an increase of almost 8%.

‌



The rise comes as wholesale UK gas prices have surged 42% over the past month, driven by renewed instability in the Middle East, raising fears that households face another expensive winter. Suppliers are already warning that Ofgem's energy price cap could rise by 5.8% in October to around £1,760, with forecasts suggesting bills could climb as high as £1,865 from January.

‌



View 3 Images Families looking to shield themselves from soaring energy bills have been hit by a fresh blow (Image: AndreyPopov via Getty Images)

Despite the recent increases, fixing is still cheaper than remaining on the current £1,663 price cap. The cheapest fixed tariff is still around £128 a year lower than the current cap, although the savings have narrowed sharply as suppliers respond to rising wholesale costs.

Cheapest fixed deals

Supplier Annual bill Saving vs price cap

‌



Outfox Energy £1,535 £128

Fuse Energy £1,594 £69

Outfox Energy £1,609 £54

‌



E.ON Next £1,612 £51

Fuse Energy £1,618 £45

*Source: Uswitch. Prices correct on July 27. Typical annual dual-fuel bills.

‌



The spike follows weeks of tension in the Gulf, which has pushed up the wholesale price suppliers pay for gas months before it reaches homes. Those higher costs are now feeding through into the retail market, with analysts warning that waiting for prices to fall could prove costly.

If October forecasts prove correct, it would mark the highest winter energy price cap since the Government's Energy Price Guarantee ended following the energy crisis. There is one piece of relief on the horizon. From October, VAT will be removed from domestic electricity bills until March, saving a typical household around £45 over a year.

View 3 Images The cheapest fixed tariff is still around £128 a year lower than the current cap (Image: Jessie Casson via Getty Images)

‌



However, the measure applies only to electricity, not gas, meaning many households that rely on gas central heating could still see overall bills rise if wholesale prices remain elevated.

Sabrina Hoque, energy expert at Uswitch, said: "Wholesale gas prices have risen sharply over the past month, and we're already seeing that filter through into the fixed tariff market – the cheapest deal available today is £111 more expensive than it was just two weeks ago.

"Suppliers are already warning there could be a bigger jump in the price cap in October, with another rise to follow in January. That's a reminder that, for those on standard tariffs, the energy market is turbulent and getting off the price cap should be a priority.

Article continues below

"Households who've been putting off switching are leaving savings on the table. Don't wait until you turn the heating on to find out what winter is going to cost you. Fixing your rates now still beats sticking on the price cap, and it's the only way to know exactly what you'll pay through the cold months. Run a comparison to see your options.”

The direction of wholesale gas prices over the coming weeks will be crucial in determining whether suppliers continue to increase the cost of fixed tariffs before winter.

News.title: Mum-of-four Michelle Donnelly dies 'unexpectedly' in her sleep after inspiring thousands through health battle
News.content:
Mum-of-four Michelle Donnelly dies 'unexpectedly' in her sleep after inspiring thousands through health battle

Michelle Donnelly was a student midwife and mother of four children

View 4 Images Michelle Donnelly shared her journey online (Image: Jam Press)

A beloved mum-of-four and student midwife who touched the hearts of thousands by chronicling her health battle has passed away unexpectedly in her sleep.

‌



Michelle Donnelly, from Glasgow, candidly shared the challenges of juggling leukaemia treatment with family life and her studies, with her videos amassing 1.3 million likes. She was remembered as an "incredible wife, mum, daughter, sister and friend" whose strength, kindness and determination resonated with people both online and within her local community.

‌



Michelle had been battling acute lymphoblastic leukaemia – known as ALL – and had recently returned to university after responding well to treatment, as reported by NeedToKnow. Tragically, she passed away peacefully in her sleep last week, leaving behind her devastated husband, Ryan, and their four children Poppy, Rosie, Benny, and Teddy.

‌



Her passing came just days after she proudly completed a six-week university placement while continuing to undergo chemotherapy. Her family described the loss as a "complete shock" as Michelle had been doing so well and had so much to look forward to. Just weeks before her death, Michelle had joyfully announced that she had finished her placement and passed the first year of her midwifery degree.

View 4 Images Michelle with her family (Image: Jam Press)

She wrote: "Six weeks of placement done. Honestly can't believe I have made it through the last six weeks while still having chemotherapy.

‌



"I won't lie, I underestimated just how challenging it would be but I've done it and I am proud to say I have passed and finally completed 1st year of my Midwifery degree. This was me my first day back, very nervous and anxious but I can't honestly say I have loved this placement and everyone made me feel so welcomed."

Michelle studied at the University of the West of Scotland and described herself online as a "busy working mum and student midwife". Her videos racked up 1.3 million likes as she openly shared family life, her studies and cancer treatment. Ryan broke the heartbreaking news in an emotional tribute to his wife.

He wrote: "Woke up this morning hoping it was all just a nightmare but my beautiful wife and the most incredible mum to our four amazing children passed away peacefully and unexpectedly in her sleep yesterday morning. Words can't describe how heartbroken we all are as a family.

‌



"Michelle was the rock to the full family. She was such a warrior to go through what she did. We had so many plans for the future with our amazing kids and now our hearts are all in pieces."

View 4 Images Michelle with husband Ryan (Image: Jam Press)

Ryan said he took comfort from believing Michelle had been reunited with their late baby son, Archie.

‌



He added: "My comfort is she will be up in heaven looking after our baby boy Archie."

A tribute from Glasgow photography business K&K Studio & Events described Michelle as "so young" and "so strong". It said: "Our hearts are aching at the tragic loss of beautiful Michelle Donnelly."

A GoFundMe has been launched on behalf of Michelle's family to support Ryan and the children.

‌



Organisers said: "As many of you know, Michelle fought leukaemia with unbelievable strength and determination. She had been doing so well and had recently returned to university, proudly completing her last placement.

View 4 Images Michelle was open about her cancer battle (Image: Jam Press)

"She had so much to look forward to, which makes this loss even more heartbreaking. Sadly, Michelle passed away peacefully in her sleep on Wednesday night.

‌



"Her passing has come as a complete shock and her family, friends and everyone who knew and loved her are absolutely devastated."

The appeal has raised more than £28,000 of its £40,000 target through around 1,100 donations. Michelle's TikTok followers also paid tribute to Michelle.

One person said: "Absolutely heartbreaking, I watched her videos all the time and was in awe of her strength, what a wonderful woman she was, I know she will be so terribly missed by you all."

Article continues below

In a response posted through Michelle's account, her family said: "We have read everyone's kind comments, we are just so overwhelmed to write back. Everyone is truly so kind.

"Keep us in your thoughts, stay strong for her. Lots of love from Ryan and the kids, and family."

News.title: Love Island final LIVE: Jasmine addresses speculation she was fuming over Julia's win
News.content:
Tonight's final of Love Island will crown the 13th season's winners as Priya responds to 'job-shaming' allegations after Elicia comment

The Love Island has officially ended with Lorenzo Alessi and Julia Majchrzak announced as winners, beating out stiff competition from Kavan Murphy and Jasmine Muller.

News.title: Donald Trump ordered to hand over financial records in £7.5 billion BBC lawsuit setback
News.content:
Donald Trump ordered to hand over financial records in £7.5 billion BBC lawsuit setback

A judge has ordered Donald Trump to disclose years of closely guarded financial records to the BBC after he claimed its Panorama documentary caused up to £7.5billion in damage to his businesses and brand

View 4 Images Donald Trump has been ordered by a judge to hand over financial records (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Donald Trump has suffered a damning setback in his defamation case against the BBC after a judge ordered him to hand the broadcaster years of closely guarded financial records.

The ruling means the US President, who has fought for decades to keep the details of his business empire secret, must disclose documents showing the value and financial performance of his companies.

The BBC demanded the records as part of its defence against Trump’s $10 billion - £7.5 billion - lawsuit over a misleadingly edited Panorama documentary covering the January 6 riots.

US Magistrate Judge Enjoliqué Lett indicated this would be her ruling last week - and it has now been made formal. She has ruled that the US leader could not claim the programme had caused massive damage to his businesses and personal brand while refusing to provide the evidence needed to test his allegations.

The Donald J. Trump Revocable Trust, which owns virtually all his properties and businesses, has been ordered to begin handing over financial documents within ten days.

View 4 Images The BBC is fighting Trump’s £7.5billion defamation claim over a misleadingly edited Panorama documentary. (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

It must then continue producing records every week until the process is complete. The Florida judge restricted the disclosure to documents dating from January 1, 2023, to the present, rejecting Trump’s attempt to block the BBC’s subpoena.

The order represents a huge victory for the corporation, which apologised for the Panorama edit but refused to pay compensation. It also creates the prospect of intense scrutiny of financial information that the President has spent much of his public life trying to shield from rivals, investigators and the American public.

Trump’s lawyers argued that the trust was not a party to the lawsuit and claimed the BBC’s requests were unreasonable, disproportionate and excessively burdensome. But Judge Lett said the scale of the disclosure sought by the broadcaster reflected the sweeping nature of Trump’s own claims.

The president has alleged the programme caused “extensive economic harms,” “injury to [his] business and personal reputation”, and “massive economic damage to his brand value and significant damage and injury to his future financial prospects.”

His lawsuit also claims there was “direct harm to his professional and occupational interests, including, without limitation, the value of his brand, properties, and businesses, and severe diminishment and tarnishing of his reputation as a politician, leader, and businessman in the eyes of the American public and around the world.”

View 4 Images Trump supporters clash with police as they force their way into the US Capitol on January 6, 2021. (Image: Zuma Press/PA Images)

The judge said that because virtually all the properties and businesses Trump claimed had been damaged were held by the trust, its records were directly relevant to the case.

She also said the BBC’s ability to examine the financial evidence was especially important because Trump was demanding damages of up to $10 billion.

The dispute began with a 2024 Panorama documentary about Trump’s speech before his supporters attacked the US Capitol on January 6, 2021, in an attempt to stop the certification of Joe Biden’s election victory.

The programme showed Trump saying: “We’re gonna walk down to the Capitol and I’ll be there with you and we fight. We fight like hell, and if you don’t fight like hell, you’re not gonna have a country anymore.”

However, the passage had been created by joining remarks made at different points in the speech. Near the beginning, Trump said: “We’re gonna walk down, and I’ll be there with you, we’re gonna walk down, we’re gonna walk down any one you want, but I think right here, we’re gonna walk down to the Capitol, and we’re gonna cheer on our brave senators and congressmen.”

His statement, “And we fight. We fight like hell. And if you don’t fight like hell, you’re not going to have a country anymore,” came towards the end of the address.

The BBC accepted that the edit had created a misleading impression, apologised and said the documentary would not be broadcast again.

But it refused to pay Trump compensation and maintains that the programme did not meet the legal threshold for defamation. The BBC’s decision to fight the case contrasts with the approach taken by several major American media companies which settled lawsuits brought by Trump rather than face a lengthy court battle.

Disney, the owner of ABC News, agreed to pay £11.3million towards Trump’s future presidential library after presenter George Stephanopoulos wrongly said he had been found liable for rape. The company also agreed to pay £750,000 towards Trump’s legal costs.

‌



Paramount later agreed to pay £12million to settle Trump’s lawsuit over the editing of a CBS interview with his 2024 presidential election opponent, Kamala Harris.

Paramount denied wrongdoing, but the settlements prompted warnings that large media companies were capitulating to legal and political pressure from Trump.

View 4 Images Rioters flood the Capitol building in an attempt to stop the certification of Joe Biden’s election victory. (Image: AP)

Article continues below

The BBC has refused to take the same course and is instead contesting his allegations in court. Trump could appeal the disclosure order or reduce his claims of damage to his businesses to limit the financial evidence he must produce.

The case is due to go before a jury in Miami in February 2027.

News.title: French patrol boat appears to fire gunshots in the Channel during MP's BBC interview
News.content:
A French patrol boat has appeared to fire a round of gunshots in the English Channel during a BBC interview with an MP.

Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp MP was being interviewed about small boat crossings by BBC journalist Michael Keohan as a French warship passed by at 09:15 BST (10:15 CET), about three miles from the French coast.

Noises which sounded like 17 gunshots fired in succession were heard in the background and an officer on the boat was seen pointing a pistol at the sea.

The BBC has approached the French coastguard for comment, while the UK government said it was in contact with the French authorities to understand the full context of the incident.

News.title: Schools to offer technical subjects from age 14 in England, Burnham says
News.content:
Secondary school pupils in England will be able to study subjects like manufacturing and AI in addition to core academic learning under reforms outlined by Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

The government said the courses, which would be available from Year 10, would be linked to local industries and designed to give children a clearer pathway into work.

Data published this year showed more than one million young people across the UK were not in education, employment or training, the highest level in more than 12 years.

Few details have been published about how the new vocational courses would work in practice and it is not clear how they would operate in areas with low industrial activity.

The BBC understands that the government expects the new pathways into work to be up and running in some areas by 2028.

Speaking at a train manufacturing site in Derby, Burnham said: "We've had a system built for too long around the university route and it sends a message to some young people that they're some kind of second-class citizens, and it's just not right.

"They need an education system that works for them as well, that offers a path to all young people, that's balanced between academic and technical."

The prime minister said he was "on a mission" to reduce the number of young people not in education, employment or training - known as "Neet" - but declined to put a target date on his ambition.

"The trend is rising at the moment, so the first thing I've got to do is to stop that rise," he said.

"It's hard to put a firm date on the moment when you can say there are fewer than now."

However, shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately said while there was a "broad consensus" on improving vocational education, it was "not a big bold announcement".

She told BBC Breakfast: "What's going on there is a drastic shortage of jobs because Labour's policies over the last couple of years have killed job opportunities for young people. This announcement will not solve that."

News.title: Naga Munchetty to leave BBC Breakfast after 17 years
News.content:
Munchetty is among the best-paid presenters on the BBC's star salaries list, earning about Â£360,000 a year, according to the latest accounts.

She has interviewed major celebrities and politicians on the programme over the years ranging from Hillary Clinton and Michelle Obama to Sir Keir Starmer, Sir David Attenborough and Sir Rod Stewart.

In 2016, she appeared on the BBC's Strictly Come Dancing.

She has also been at the centre of some controversies during her time on BBC Breakfast.

In 2019, she was initially found to have breached the BBC's guidelines over comments she made about a social media post from Donald Trump about four female politicians of colour.

However, the BBC's director general then reversed that finding after deciding her words were not "sufficient to merit" upholding part of the complaint.

In 2021, Munchetty and co-presenter Charlie Stayt were "spoken to and reminded of their responsibilities" after complaints about their reaction to a government minister's flag. Munchetty apologised for liking "offensive" tweets about the exchange.

In June 2025, the Sun reported details of two alleged incidents which the paper said caused BBC bosses to speak to Munchetty about her conduct.

That came amid reports of behind-the-scenes tensions on the show, and at the same time as the programme's editor Richard Frediani took extended leave following allegations about his behaviour.

The BBC said it did not comment on individual cases but took all complaints about conduct at work extremely seriously.

Munchetty and Frediani did not comment on the reports.

News.title: Mother and boyfriend guilty of girl's murder
News.content:
Warning: This story contains distressing details

A mother and her new boyfriend have been found guilty of murdering her two-year-old daughter, with the man also convicted of sexually abusing the girl.

Isabelle Welsh suffered multiple injuries in the weeks before she collapsed with a fractured skull at her home in Thornaby in September 2025, Teesside Crown Court had heard.

Alexandra Walker, 25, and her partner Harrison Simpson, 22, were both found guilty of murder and child cruelty, with Simpson also convicted of sexual abuse of a child.

They will be sentenced on Thursday. Isabelle's family said she had her "whole life ahead of her" but it was "taken in the most heartbreaking way".

Prosecutors previously said the couple, who began a relationship in June 2025, were both responsible for a "wicked" campaign of sexual abuse and violence against Isabelle.

Walker and Simpson blamed each other for the girl's injuries and suffering.

News.title: Fourth heatwave grips parts of UK with 35C forecast
News.content:
A fourth heatwave of the year is now under way for parts of the UK, with temperatures expected to climb into the mid-30s Celsius later this week.

This latest spell of heatwave threshold-level temperatures is expected to peak on Wednesday in the south-east and east of England.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has warned the rising temperatures could increase health risks, particularly for vulnerable groups.

It has issued amber heat health alerts, external for much of eastern England that come into force on Wednesday.

News.title: House of the Dragon star Bethany Antonia joins Strictly line-up
News.content:
House of the Dragon star Bethany Antonia is the latest celebrity to join this year's line-up for Strictly Come Dancing.

Antonia has portrayed dragon-rider Lady Baela Targaryen in HBO's Game of Thrones prequel since 2022. She is currently starring as Eurydice in the Tony Award-winning musical Hadestown in London's West End.

The singer and actress has also appeared in series including Nolly, Stay Close, Stath Lets Flats, and Doctor Who.

In a statement, Antonia said: "I can't quite believe that I will be heading to the Strictly ballroom this September! I have grown up watching Strictly, and I am so excited to take the challenge on and (hopefully!) learn a new skill. See you on the dancefloor!"

She is the ninth celebrity to be confirmed for this year's series, joining stars including Delta Goodrem, Lacey Turner, Dani Dyer and Jaime Winstone.

More celebrities are set to be announced in the coming weeks, with 15 expected in the final line-up.

News.title: 'It's a hell of a situation': Spain grapples with destructive wildfires
News.content:
Temperatures are expected to approach 40C in some regions in the coming days, with the heatwave forecast to last at least until Sunday.

Spain's state meteorological agency Aemet has warned the "fire danger level will continue to rise to extreme levels, hindering firefighting efforts".

Ayuso confirmed that four municipalities remained under lockdown orders while another 12 were evacuated. She had earlier described the wildfires as "the biggest natural catastrophe in the history of Spain" and of flames turning the area into a "war zone".

In the Madrid region alone, more than 56,500 people have been evacuated since the fires broke out last week. A further 27,797 people have been ordered to stay at home.

Further evacuations have taken place in Ãvila, Toledo and Valencia.

Ayuso wrote on X that the situation was now "improving little by little" and some residents may soon be allowed to return home.

Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska told Spain's La 1 TV channel that firefighting efforts on Monday night had resulted in "relatively positive progress".

"This morning, we are very satisfied with the work done. We are going to consolidate the work that has been done," he said.

He maintained that "we must be positive; we have the emergency under control" but conceded that "weather conditions are not helping us at all".

News.title: Is it safe to travel to Spain and France right now?
News.content:
The UK government has not specifically warned against travel to anywhere in France or Spain, but it does advise caution.

In France, it says access to affected areas may be restricted and roads may close at short notice. It adds that further evacuations may take place.

It has also issued a general warning about the high risk of wildfires in France during the summer season from April to October.

For those in an affected area in France or Spain or planning to travel there, the UK government recommends following instructions and updates from local authorities and emergency services at all times.

Those needing emergency help in France or Spain can call 112.

Travellers should also bear in mind the UK government's advice can and does change in response to moving events.

Anna-Marie Duthie, travel insurance expert at financial rating firm Defaqto, says that if this happens after you have booked your trip, "you may be covered for cancellation or curtailment".

"You may also be covered for additional travel and accommodation costs should your trip be disrupted due to a catastrophic event, if your insurer offers this cover or you've paid to include it," she adds.

To know if this applies to you, check your policy.

News.title: Unsolved Suzy Lamplugh case 'haunts' detectives
News.content:
Police officers investigating the disappearance of estate agent Suzy Lamplugh in west London say they remain "haunted" by the case, four decades after she went missing.

Lamplugh, 25, vanished after leaving her Fulham office to meet a client on the afternoon of 28 July 1986. She never returned and her body has never been found.

As the Metropolitan Police investigation is due to be mothballed next year, cold case detectives say they are troubled by the continuing mystery.

To mark the 40th anniversary of her disappearance, the Lamplugh family has released previously unseen photographs featuring her siblings Lizzie, Tamsin and Richard and her parents Paul and Diana.

In releasing the intimate family images, her siblings described her as "a truly beautiful person inside and out".

News.title: Hundreds of thousands of women get morning-after pill via free pharmacy service
News.content:
The morning-after pill, known as emergency contraception, external, is medication designed to prevent unwanted pregnancies. It usually has to be taken within three to five days of having unprotected sex. The sooner it is taken, the more effective it is.

It works by delaying or preventing the release of an egg, but will only prevent pregnancy if ovulation has not already happened.

Alternatively, women can visit a doctor or nurse to have a coil or intrauterine device (IUD) fitted to prevent pregnancy at any time during their menstrual cycle. To be effective, it needs to be fitted within 120 hours or five days of unprotected sex.

The government said making the morning-after pill available free from pharmacies would end the "unfair" barriers and postcode lottery some women faced - with access varying dramatically depending on where they live.

Under the scheme, women can visit their local pharmacy and have a confidential consultation with a pharmacist or trained pharmacy technician, before receiving the medication on the same day.

Prior to this, women had to book an appointment with their GP, sexual health clinic or pharmacy to get the morning-after pill. Women could also access it privately, as they still can now.

In 2024/25, there were around 150,000 NHS prescriptions for the morning-after pill - far fewer than under the new service.

Dr Sue Mann, NHS National Clinical Director for Women's Health, said the pharmacy service was a "major step forward for women's health", with "no appointment, no waiting and no judgement".

"This service is already making a real impact, particularly for women living in more deprived communities, by making contraception easier to access closer to home," she added.

Women can check online, external to find their nearest participating pharmacy. All pharmacists and pharmacy technicians delivering the service have received specialist training to provide emergency contraception and wider contraceptive care.

News.title: Love Island UK crowns winners of twist-filled series
News.content:
This article contains spoilers for the Love Island final.

Julia Majchrzak and Lorenzo Alessi have been crowned the winners of Love Island UK 2026.

The pair beat runners-up Jasmine Muller and Kavan Murphy, and Angelista Gunda and Simba Kudyiwa, who came in third, to take home the Â£50,000 prize.

A shocked Julia thanked all those who had voted for them, saying: "I just didn't think coming into Casa [Amor] I'd be stood here."

When host Maya Jama asked what they would spend the money on, Julia revealed she wanted Lorenzo, who appeared too stunned to speak, to move in with her after leaving the villa.

Talking to Maya ahead of the reveal during the live final, 28-year-old Lorenzo said he had "never met someone who feels so well matched to me" when reflecting on his relationship with Julia.

Business owner Lorenzo, who entered the villa on day one, said he felt like he "manifested" meeting Julia, 26, in Casa Amor, the alternate villa where relationships are tested by new arrivals.

Julia said she felt an "instant spark" when meeting Lorenzo and described their relationship as "seriously unserious".

The final drew in an average audience of 1.1m viewers across all devices, according to ITV.

This is a notable drop from last year's finale, which reportedly , externalbrought in 1.3m viewers.

News.title: Former boxing world champion denies assaulting man, court hears
News.content:
Former boxing world champion Joe Cordina has denied assaulting a man outside a petrol station, a court has heard.

Cordina, 34, was one of two men charged in connection with an incident in the Cardiff suburb of Pentwyn in February.

He appeared at Cardiff Magistrates' Court on Tuesday and pleaded not guilty to two charges of assault by beating.

Cordina appeared in the dock alongside Jamie O'Brien, 32, from Pentwyn, who has also been charged with assault in connection with the incident.

O'Brien did not enter a plea during the short hearing.

The court previously heard the offences the two men are charged with are alleged to be "against each other".

Nadeem Majid, representing Cordina, said the second charge of assault he faces "emanates from one continued incident".

District Judge Charlotte Murphy granted Cordina unconditional bail until a trial, which was set for 13 October this year.

O'Brien's case was adjourned until 26 August.

Cordina is a former super-featherweight world champion and was due to fight for the WBO lightweight title in the United States on July 4.

However, he revealed in a social media post that his application for a US visa was refused.

News.title: Man admits taking ambulance with patient inside
News.content:
A man who stole an ambulance with a patient and paramedic inside has admitted false imprisonment and aggravated vehicle taking.

Marshall Leese, 32, took the vehicle from outside the Royal Stoke University Hospital in Stoke-on-Trent at about 20:15 GMT on 25 March.

Police pursued him until he stopped at a petrol station on the A34 in Newcastle-under-Lyme, Staffordshire. A second ambulance was sent to recover the patient.

Leese, of Hanley, Stoke-on-Trent, also pleaded guilty to failing to provide a specimen and driving without insurance at Stoke-on-Trent Crown Court. He was remanded into custody and the case adjourned for sentencing on a date yet to be fixed.

Judge Sally Hancox described the incident as "unusual".

West Midlands Ambulance Service previously said a second ambulance was sent to where Leese stopped to recover the patient and take them back to hospital.

A welfare check was also carried out on the staff member to "maintain their wellbeing", a spokesperson added.

News.title: Second home owners 'feel unwelcome' while locals struggle to buy
News.content:
Rhodri Lewis is desperate to buy a house in his home county of Pembrokeshire, an area in which the Welsh government estimated 6.5%, external of all properties were second homes in 2023-24.

"When I did have a look around, there was no chance I was going to be able to afford a house," the 23-year-old said.

"So, yeah, I had to move back in with mum and dad, unfortunately."

Rhodri is a Welsh speaker and like many other people, he said he worries that a lack of affordable housing for local people can affect the language.

"Tourism is fantastic for us for three months of the year in the summer," he said.

"But then the other eight, nine months, where a lot of the second homes, for example, don't have people in them, it just kills the community for the rest of the year."

Rhodri is planning to travel in the near future and hopes he'll be able to afford his first home upon his return.

Carol Peet, who sells properties in Pembrokeshire, said she believed in some areas there are two housing markets: one for locals and one for second homes.

"The obvious answer to it, I think, which I've been selling for the last 25 years is to stop houses under the average price of a property in this area, which at the moment is about Â£250,000, being sold as second homes," she said.

"Those are the properties that young local families can afford, not the million-pound houses that second homers buy."

She added that a number of "chocolate box pretty cottages" are great for holidays but are "totally impractical" for full-time living as "they're cold, damp and dark in the winter".

She said that while second homes were "absolutely vital" to her local economy in Narberth, she understood the need for affordable housing for local people.

News.title: 'We lost all of our morning trade' - businesses fearful after more break-ins
News.content:
Pride weekend is one of the busiest of the year for many city centre businesses, but for one chip shop owner Saturday morning was spent filing police reports after his shop became the latest to be targeted in Belfast.

Gareth McKinstry, who owns Simply Fish & Chips, said it was a costly incident.

Last week another cafÃ© owner warned the situation was at a "tipping point" after his premises were targeted.

Since then, three more city centre businesses have been broken into and money stolen, including McKinstry's restaurant on Oxford Street.

"Saturday was Pride day and it was meant to be one of our busiest days of the year and we lost all of our morning trade because we couldn't open the shop until the police had finished with their investigation," McKinstry said.

The break-in happened at about 02:00 BST on Saturday.

News.title: Reform UK reports Zack Polanski to police over guillotine T-shirt post
News.content:
Reform UK have reported Green Party leader Zack Polanski to the police, after he shared an Instagram post including a photo of a man wearing a top featuring the name "Nigel" alongside an image of a guillotine.

One of several images showed a man in a black t-shirt with a large guillotine below the words "We're only making plans for Nigel".

Sharing a screenshot on X, Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said: "If I was to post anything as inciteful then I would expect to be arrested, and so should Polanski."

A Green Party spokesperson said: "Once this image was brought to [Zack's] attention he immediately unshared the post. He unequivocally does not support this type of dangerous message."

Polanski had shared the photo with his 713,000 followers in a post containing several pictures of a Green Party event on Sunday, having accepted a request to collaborate with another account.

In a post on X, the Metropolitan Police said: "We received a third-party report relating to an image shared on social media. We take reports of this nature extremely seriously, and officers are conducting enquiries into the matter."

The words "We're only making plans for Nigel" are the same as the lyrics of a 1979 song by band XTC, external.

The Green Party spokesperson said: "Zack condemns the image on the T-shirt. He was tagged in a post with 20 images and clicked accept without realising there was more to it than he had seen.

"The T-shirt is clearly in poor taste, especially at a time of heightened fears for the security of public figures, having experienced multiple threats himself.

"He and the Green Party call on everyone involved in public discourse to show kindness and not encourage more division."

The BBC understands Polanski has not been contacted by police.

Reform UK say Polanski has not been in touch with Farage to privately apologise for sharing the post. The Greens have been approached for comment in relation to this.

Train drivers are calling on British rail companies to provide “decent” toilet facilities and breaks, a year after the UK’s rail regulator told operators to improve conditions for staff.

Aslef, the train drivers’ union, said it has put the industry “on notice” after companies including Network Rail failed to deliver decent facilities for drivers on Britain’s railways.

In November 2024, Aslef’s Dignity for Drivers report found a lack of adequate toilet facilities and time to access them for drivers during the working day.

The Office of Rail and Road (ORR) called for passenger and freight companies to provide proper facilities for staff on the rail network as a “matter of human dignity, health, safety and respect to our people” in July 2025.

According to Aslef, the welfare charter drawn up by the Rail Safety and Standards Board has not been delivered across the network.

Dave Calfe, Aslef general secretary, said: “We need action, not broken promises, to improve toilet facilities for drivers and to reduce the time drivers are expected to go without being able to take a toilet break.

“The health and wellbeing of our members is not a price we are prepared to pay for the inaction of the industry. That’s why we are calling them out publicly and telling them – in no uncertain terms – that it is time for them to deliver, to do what they promised. And, if they don’t, there will be consequences.”

The ORR’s annual report published this month said that “progress has been uneven and industry momentum has slowed” with key barriers around “coordination, shared access to facilities, and consistent delivery”.

It said: “We will continue to assess welfare provision through inspections and engagement, while encouraging wider adoption of the Charter. Sustained focus is needed to translate commitment into practical improvements and ensure workers have consistent access to appropriate facilities.”

Calfe added: “20 months after we exposed this scandal, and a year after the train companies promised to do the right thing, drivers are still paying with their health for industry inaction.

“We are putting the rail industry on notice that we have had enough of their excuses. The industry and the government cannot continue failing the workforce on the most basic level, and we need action now.”

News.title: Victim of ‘evil’ funeral director says she has nightmares of ‘bodies found in Auschwitz’
News.content:
For free real time breaking news alerts sent straight to your inbox sign up to our breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

A grieving daughter said the horrors at Robert Bush’s funeral home made her think of “bodies found in Auschwitz”, while another described him as a “cruel conman” who had destroyed families.

The disgraced funeral director had kept 31 decomposing bodies at the site in Hull, and had falsely told their families that they had been cremated before giving them to ashes of a stranger.

Bush, 48, was found with half a tonne of ashes, with some families forced to wait seven weeks for DNA tests to identify their loved ones.

Tina Thomas, whose father Jim Porter, 80, was recovered from Legacy Independent Funeral Directors with his hospital identification bands still on, had noticed at his funeral that his coffin did not look big enough.

She said: “When the police told me there was a possibility that Dad was still at Legacy, I was devastated.

“I had nightmares and thoughts of bodies just piled up came into my mind.

“The only way I can describe it is like seeing images of the bodies found in Auschwitz during the war.”

open image in gallery Robert Bush pictured arriving at Hull Crown Court for his five-day sentencing ( AFP/Getty )

Another woman described Bush as “pure evil” after he gave her the wrong ashes of her brother Paul Hemingway, which her children then had made into jewellery.

Valerie Coates described to Hull Crown Court her devastation at realising she had not been given her husband Ron’s ashes, despite holding a celebration attended by more than 100 people.

She said: “I try to wear a brave smile, but my close friends and family know that I am tortured by thoughts of how Ron’s poor body was mistreated – and the cruel realisation that the beautiful urn I cherished, and talked to every day, did not contain his ashes after all.”

She said: “We had made a pact, Ron and I, a promise to each other, that our ashes would eventually be together.

“Robert Bush has made that impossible and I shall never know what actually happened to Ron’s ashes.”

Terry White’s daughter Angela Scottow also said that she was handed the wrong ashes, and that her family had lit candles around them on his birthday to celebrate his life.

“Dad was such a lovely man and Rob Bush treated him like a piece of meat,” she said. “I feel only anger, hatred and disgust for the man that I trusted to treat my dad with dignity and respect.”

She added: “He has absolutely broken me. How will I trust anyone again?”

The grandson of Susan Stone, 77, whose body was also found at Legacy, said that his grandfather was “destroyed” by the discovery.

Hull Crown Court heard over 12 years, Bush breached the trust placed in him by grieving families “on an almost industrial scale”, by keeping bodies for months after they should have been cremated, giving out the wrong ashes, taking money for funeral plans without making any of the arrangements and stealing charity donations collected at services.

open image in gallery Bush had kept 35 bodies at his funeral home in Hull ( PA )

One woman said she feels she has let her mother down after her ashes “can’t be located anywhere”.

In a victim personal statement, Claire Edwards said: “I am so angry that I placed trust in Bush from the start, and that he has let us down as a family, and I feel that I personally have let my mum down.

“I feel guilty about what happened with my mum’s funeral arrangements and that I am unable to place my mum’s ashes with my late dad’s ashes – which were hers/our wishes.”

His crimes were discovered by chance, when he was on holiday in Arizona and contacted Gary Pickering and Steve Emmerson, directors of Evergreen Funeral Directors, asking them to assist with a body recovery while he was away.

Patrick Moore – a casual worker for Legacy – helped the two men collect the body from the care home, but said Bush had told him “not to bring anyone back to Legacy or help put a body into the fridge area”.

After becoming suspicious that operations at Legacy were not as they should be, the two men persuaded Mr Moore to let them into Legacy’s site on Hessle Road, which was described as a “horror scene”.

open image in gallery The bodies were discovered by chance while Bush was on holiday in Arizona ( PA )

They flagged down a passing police car after discovering bodies “uncovered and in varying states of decomposition”, with the funeral home described as “dirty and unkempt” and a human foetus discovered in a brown bag.

Robert Bush committed fraud concerning the ashes of 57 people between 2017 and 2024, Hull Crown Court has heard.

The total value of this fraud is around £86,868 with 46 victims identified where ashes have been wrongly returned to families, and an additional 11 families where no ashes have ever been returned, prosecutor Chris Paxton KC said.

He added that the “lack of book keeping” by Bush was “quite profound”, making it “very difficult to follow” the number of funerals overseen by the him during this time.

Bush has admitted 67 offences, including preventing a lawful and decent burial, fraudulent trading, fraud by false representation and theft from well-known charities.

This includes four “foetus allegations” of fraud where he presented ashes to women, falsely saying they were “the remains of their unborn”.

News.title: Transfer news LIVE: Vinicius Jr hands Arsenal boost with new decision, Liverpool get £140m Barcola green light
News.content:
Chelsea appear set to strike a surprise double deal for England veterans Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson as Xabi Alonso seeks to add experience to his squad. The Brighton striker, 35, and Brentford midfielder, 36, could continue an intriguing summer of incomings at Stamford Bridge after the marquee addition of Morgan Rogers earlier in the window.

Arsenal, meanwhile, are plotting an audacious move for Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Jr and want to sign the Brazil winger this summer. The Premier League champions are preparing to offer the 26-year-old the biggest contract in their history but Real Madrid may yet offer the Brazilian fresh terms.

It could be a busy few weeks for Mikel Arteta’s side as they also look to sign Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes and add another centre-back, with England internationals Ezri Konsa and John Stones both of interest – though the latter appears bound for Italy. Newcastle manager Eddie Howe confirmed that he wants to keep Guimaraes, but added that his future at the club is out of his control.

Elsewhere, Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has set out his targets for the transfer window and has confirmed the Reds “definitely need to sign a winger”, while France international Bradley Barcola is reportedly open to leaving Paris Saint-Germain this summer. PSG, who are set to miss out on the signing Yan Diomande to Real Madrid, would demand a record fee, however.

Manchester United are still interested in adding another midfielder and have “reached an agreement in principle” with France international Manu Kone, according to reports in Italy. Aurelien Tchouameni remains a target, too.

The U.N.'s migration agency is warning that criminal networks have been trafficking hundreds of thousands of people — many of them educated English speakers — to work in online scam centers, and the caseload is growing.

The International Organization for Migration says victims are often lured by fake job s — mostly through social media — promising work abroad, only to get locked up, have their identity documents seized, and forced through violence, threats and “debt bondage” to participate in the online scams.

“We’re seeing so many more of these cases emerge right now," IOM Director-General Amy Pope told reporters in Geneva on Tuesday. “We’re seeing victims from over 80 different countries being trafficked into the scams.”

'They’re recruiting people who often speak English very well, who often have graduate degrees, some level of education," Pope said, adding that the cases are “specifically playing out across Asia.”

The migration agency cited estimates from the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime that losses across east Asia, Australia, and New Zealand reached as much as $114 billion last year, and “scam compounds” across the region could hold hundreds of thousands of trafficked workers.

IOM said it had assisted over 3,500 such victims of forced criminality between 2022 and 2025, people who originated from nearly 40 countries: people from Indonesia, India, Sri Lanka, Ethiopia, Kenya, and Bangladesh were most affected.
