SUNDAY: Liverpool seek compromise on Bradley Barcola

SATURDAY: Tottenham continue push for Man City winger Savinho

FRIDAY: Real open talks for Yan Diomande, Chelsea go back to Villa to poach set-piece coach Austin MacPhee... and Brentford bid for West Ham wing back

THURSDAY: Arsenal sign Christos Tzolis in £34million move from Club Brugge as Leeds ramp up talks with Man City's James Trafford

WEDNESDAY: West Ham star Crysencio Summerville set for £60m Saudi Arabia move despite Roma's late attempt to hijack deal

Sports.title: Zinedine Zidane is announced as France's new manager on a four-year-deal - as football icon succeeds former team-mate Didier Deschamps
Sports.content:
Zinedine Zidane has been announced as France's new manager, with the long-expected announcement having finally been delivered.

The 54-year-old has signed a four-year deal with Les Bleus as he succeeds his former Juventus and France team-mate Didier Deschamps.

Deschamps left his 14-year tenure as France manager at the end of the World Cup, with his side losing 2-0 to eventual champions Spain in the semi-finals. They finished fourth after a 6-4 defeat by England in the third-place play-off.

Zidane's unveiling took place on Tuesday morning at the French Football Federation's (FFF) headquarters in Paris, alongside FFF president Philippe Diallo.

It is Zidane's first foray back into management since leaving Real Madrid in 2021, revealing he has rejected offers in the meantime as he waited for his 'dream' to become France boss.

'The French team was the only thing I wanted to do,' Zidane told reporters.

Zinedine Zidane has been announced as France's new manager on a four-year contract

He revealed he has rejected club management roles as he waited for his 'dream' job instead

Zidane succeeds Didier Deschamps (centre) who bowed out at the end of the World Cup

'I've always looked at this team through the eyes of a future manager. I didn't take a club job for that reason. The only thing I wanted to do after Madrid was manage the French national team.

'I could have taken on a three-year role because Deschamps was there. He made that decision in January 2025, and the very next day I knew I wanted to be the next one. We met with the president and the deal was sealed.'

Deschamps oversaw 185 matches and 120 victories, guiding France to the 2018 World Cup title, the 2020-21 Nations League trophy, and the Euro 2016 and 2022 World Cup finals.

He and Zidane share a long association, having been team-mates in France's 1998 World Cup-winning side on home soil.

Zidane played a pivotal role in that triumph and won the Ballon d'Or that year. He made 108 appearances for the national side, scoring 31 goals and contributing 29 assists.

'You'll see my [team's] style soon,' Zidane said. 'I'm driven by the game. I was a No 10, and what drives me is scoring goals.

'I lived in Spain for 25 years, you know what that means. On the pitch, I was a leader. Now I'm becoming a leader through my experience.

'Winning in '98 is the best thing that's ever happened to me, winning with my team-mates. I spent those four or five years waiting for that day. I'm emotional; you can't see it, but I'm so excited. I'm happy.'

The pair were team-mates at Juventus and France as players (pictured for Les Bleus in 2000)

Speaking about Zidane's arrival, Diallo revealed that negotiations with the 1998 World Cup and Euro 2000 winner began in February 2025 after Deschamps said he would stand down after the 2026 World Cup.

'This is an exceptional moment, exceptional because of the person sat next to me,' Diallo said. 'Zinedine is one of the legends of French soccer and for many years he said one of his dreams was to take charge of the France team.'

'I would like to thank Didier Deschamps and his staff for their work. For 14 years he led the France team to the top.'

The length of the deal means Zidane will work through until at least the 2030 World Cup, incorporating two Nations Leagues (2026-27 and 2028-29) as well as Euro 2028 before the major showpiece.

His first match in the hotseat will be away to Türkiye in the Nations League on September 25. After that comes a trip to local rivals Belgium on September 28 with a clash against Italy on October 2 sparking his first game in charge on home soil.

Sports.title: Milos Kerkez reveals why Andoni Iraola is the 'perfect fit' for Liverpool, how he's stepped up as a leader during pre-season and driving trucks with his dad - aged 10!
Sports.content:
When Milos Kerkez signed for Liverpool last summer, an old colleague from his days in Hungary told Daily Mail Sport he was ‘like a young horse’.

Kicking everybody, a hive of energy unable to sit still, a relentless running – but, as former Hungary No 1 Adam Bogdan added at the time, it was always obvious this eccentric individual would make it to the top.

After spending time with Kerkez in a swanky rooftop bar in Chicago, it was hard not to let that verdict pop back to mind.

In an engaging and at times hilarious chat with the Liverpool left back, Kerkez is here to discuss all things from driving Serbian trucks at age 10, getting a ‘smack’ from his dad when he does not play well and his friendship with UFC fighter Paddy ‘The Baddy’ Pimblett.

But first, Kerkez is the best-placed player to offer insight on the new regime. Having signed from Bournemouth for £40m last summer, the Serbian-born Hungary international knows Andoni Iraola and his backroom staff better than any player at Anfield.

‘I was delighted, honestly,’ says the 22-year-old when asked how he reacted to Iraola’s appointment. ‘I worked for him before and he helped me and improved me a lot in the two years that I spent with him.

Kerkez signed for Liverpool from Bournemouth for £40m last summer - and knows Andoni Iraola and his backroom staff better than any player at Anfield

'If you see footage of how we all are after training – all lying down! – then you can see what he is preparing us for,' Kerkez says of Iraola

‘I was really happy, obviously for myself but also for the team. Everyone knows what type of football he plays, I think he is the perfect fit for us.

‘It’s the intensity. He’s not scared to play one-on-one all over the pitch, to press high and to be on the front foot always. If you see footage of how we all are after training – all lying down! – then you can see what he is preparing us for.

‘He is very professional. He likes to talk sometimes but not a lot. Maybe he doesn’t want to get too close to some players and wants to show that everyone is the same in the team and doesn't want to get too close to anyone in particular. He keeps it professional with a lot of hard work.’

At this point, Kerkez puffs out his cheeks and wipes a bead of sweat from his brow. He has just returned from a training session at the HQ of MLS side, Chicago Fire, where the squad have been put through their paces in the searing Illinois heat.

It is understood the left-back has taken it upon himself to step up as a leader on this pre-season tour noting that senior stars such as Virgil van Dijk and Alisson will not partake in the trip. Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate have all departed the club.

But at heart, Kerkez feels like a kid with the innocence of youth, loving every day living out his dream as a top-level footballer.

It was a journey that started on the streets of Serbia, which he believed left him in good stead to make it, following a similar journey to one of the biggest names in the NBA, Denver Nuggets centre Nikola Jokic, nicknamed ‘The Joker’.

‘I grew up a bit different in Serbia,’ says Kerkez, who says he was bored of the summer holidays after 10 days that he spent in Serbia, Spain and Montenegro. ‘We grew up different. It's just your job, do your own damn job.

‘For example, I started to drive a truck when I was 10 years old. I don't know if it's legal or not! It's just a bit different. We're more on the street. I don't know. I can say 10 other things that I did when I was younger… I won't. I gave you this example!’

It is worth pointing out that Kerkez’s father, Sebastijan, was also present – ‘he was doing the pedals, I was quite small so couldn’t catch them – and the youngster was merely sitting on his lap while steering the big-wheeler down the dirt tracks.

When Kerkez signed for Liverpool last summer, an old colleague from his days in Hungary told Daily Mail Sport he was ‘like a young horse’, a hive of energy unable to sit still

Kerkez Snr lives with his son now alongside mother Tijana and gives him lifts to training most days.

The Kerkezes are a tight-knit family. Brother Marko, 26, plays for Aris in the Greek league, while the eldest of the trio is Rade, who worked in a chemical factory. Rade got married this year, which led to some confusion when Milos posted a picture on Instagram with the bride.

‘Everyone gets this wrong!’ beams the left back when asked if he got married. ‘It was my oldest brother. In Serbia it is normal for the younger brothers to take the bride to the church. That’s what I did and now everyone thinks I got married.

‘I keep having to explain to a lot of people that I never got married. It was my oldest brother, not me. I was going around the club and people started to congratulate me. I’m like, “No, I’m not ready for this yet!” It was not me, it was Rade.’

As for his father, Kerkez adds: ‘Paddy the Baddie! My dad met a friend, who is close with Paddy. Then my Dad met Paddy and I came and I met him. I follow UFC a lot. Nice guy… A Scouser. Crazy!

‘My family are very important. My brothers have their own lives now but my parents are with me and I am much happier they are with me, my mum and dad.

‘He is here to smack me sometimes on the top of the head to remind me! Sometimes you play a few good games and you maybe start to get a bit carried away. But my dad is here to smack me, I come straight back down and I switch straight back on. They are very important.’

Kerkez, as is becoming clear, is different to most footballers and his turn of phrase could set him up for a post-playing career as a stand-up comedian.

There is quite a Hungarian community building in Liverpool. Dominik Szoboszlai captained the Reds in their first pre-season friendly, while a back-up goalkeeper Armin Pecsi is impressing team-mates with his calmness on the ball, though he will be loaned out this term.

Academy sources also rave about teenager Erik Farkas, born in Hungary but is eligible to play for England if he makes it. He has trained with the first team.

At one point last season, Slot joked that he thought Mohamed Salah was Hungarian as he spent so much time with Szoboszlai and Kerkez. The trio were good pals and Kerkez says: ‘We speak often. I don't know who he is signing for! We just talk about vacations.’

Kerkez has learned a lot from him and Robertson and adds: ‘Andy helped me a lot. Like I said many times, he's a legend. He did a lot of big things, won everything. He's someone I look up to. Obviously, I'm here. I want to make my own thing.

‘We all know what Andy (Robertson) did for the club, I'm not running away from that. I want to make my own way. I'm going to work hard. I know what it means to play for Liverpool. I showed it a bit last year and I am going to show it more this year.

‘As for Mo, I saw on the TV before we left the AXA (training centre), how many goals and assists Mo had, it was 300 and something. I just walked out! What is this?!

‘Time flies, a new generation comes with new players and hopefully everything will be good.’

Sports.title: Inside Arsenal's Hale End academy battles: Why two wonderkids left, how Gunners missed out on Jeremy Monga, and why Spurs and Man City are beating them to targets
Sports.content:
Inside Arsenal's Hale End academy battles: Why two wonderkids left, how Gunners missed out on Jeremy Monga, and why Spurs and Man City are beating them to targets

Unlock more from Isaan Khan inside the Arsenal camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Arsenal's rather unexciting first-team recruitment has dominated the summer chat in the pubs of north London. Their Hale End academy, however, has quietly endured its own transfer misery.

Despite being Premier League champions and boasting one of England's most celebrated youth setups, Arsenal have lost a string of key recruitment battles - from being beaten to top targets to seeing their own highly-rated prospects reject new deals.

First, Manchester City hijacked a move for promising Leicester City winger Jeremy Monga, whom Arsenal had been close to signing. Second, Tottenham are poised to beat the Gunners to West Ham’s Under 15s midfield star Isaac Allen.

And then internally, talented youngsters such as Kyran Thompson and Mishel Nduka have chosen to continue their careers elsewhere.

Behind the setbacks lies a changing academy market in which rival clubs are prepared to offer eye-watering salaries to 16-year-olds, while Arsenal remain reluctant to match those figures. Combined with an increasingly difficult pathway into Mikel Arteta's title-winning first team, it has created a perfect storm that is testing the club's renowned youth system.

Missing out on Monga first drew attention to this academy malaise. The 17-year-old Leicester star was on track to join the Gunners after the club registered their firm interest for weeks and put in the groundwork. Yet, City stole in amid Arsenal’s reluctance to meet Leicester’s £10million valuation. City paid £12.5m for the youngster.

Arsenal's academy players are put through their paces - but it has been a frustrating summer at Hale End

Arsenal missed out to Manchester City for the services of Jeremy Monga, with City agreeing to pay Leicester a higher fee

That hasn't been the only attempted transfer not to come to fruition.

As Daily Mail Sport reported last week, Tottenham are close to beating Arsenal to signing West Ham’s 15-year-old Allen. Again, the Gunners were keen on the player - but Spurs are now confident they will land him.

There are, meanwhile, a number of prospects Arsenal wanted to keep and have sign scholarship terms - with a view to a professional contract aged 17 - who have turned down deals. They include Thompson, the highly-rated 16-year-old winger who joined in 2024 after the club paid West Ham £1.1m.

Last season, Thompson was fast-tracked into the Under 18s, while also featuring for the Under 19s in UEFA’s Youth League - an academy version of the Champions League - and making his Under-21 debut in Premier League 2.

The Gunners saw a pathway for the teenager and were keen to tie him down to a new extended contract. Yet, as Daily Mail Sport reported, he turned it down and pursued a move to Spurs - before pivoting to join Newcastle.

Nduka falls into the same category. He joined the Arsenal academy in September 2025 after eight years at Charlton. The skilful midfielder, who turned 16 in April, made the Under 21s squad twice last season and also featured in a UEFA Youth League Under 19s match against Club Bruges in December.

He regularly appeared for the Under 18s, playing 10 games in a group above his own age, and shone. But he has now joined City.

Some young players cannot see a way into Arsenal's first team now that they are successful on the pitch

Myles Lewis-Skelly (left) and Bukayo Saka have helped build Hale End's reputation as a production line of elite talent

There are two factors influencing Arsenal’s predicament. The first is money. The likes of City are willing to pay way beyond the Gunners in wages for academy players. And that outlay does not count towards the Premier League's financial rules so clubs can, to a degree, throw what they want at these youngsters.

Daily Mail Sport understands Nduka’s City deal includes a salary of £20,000 a week, which puts the 16-year-old on around £1m a year. Monga, meanwhile, is understood to be on a much more lucrative wage.

Arsenal’s stance is that they are unwilling to pay salaries they believe are disproportionate for players yet to play senior top-flight football. Their focus is on development, building a genuine career pathway and potential re-sale value. But in reality, the academy landscape has changed.

The other element is a pathway to the first team. Some young players can’t see a way to the senior squad because of how well Arsenal have done on the pitch.

As reigning champions with a squad so strong the likes of Christian Norgaard played only a handful of games last season, earning a place in the set-up is extremely hard. This makes other clubs, like Tottenham for example, an attractive proposition.

Some players believe the pathway to first-team football is clearer at a club that narrowly avoided relegation in the last two seasons.

There have been some wins, though, in this window under new academy director Pascal De Maesschalck who was appointed earlier in the month. His arrival has helped steady the ship after uncertainty following Per Mertesacker’s departure, the club actively operating in the market.

Arsenal are close to completing the signing of Cardiff City teenager Axel Donczew.

The 16-year-old attacking midfielder made headlines last October when he became Cardiff’s youngest-ever senior player, aged just 15 years and 234 days old when he came on as a substitute in the Welsh club’s EFL Trophy game against Newport County.

Elijah Upson, the 18-year-old son of Matthew, last week signed for Arsenal from Spurs and has joined up with the Under 21s.

The Gunners are also pushing hard to acquire Crystal Palace striker Mylo Bernard, 16.

But the whole academy market is in a state of flux, turbo-charged by eye-watering sums and a desire by top clubs to seize the country’s best talents before they turn professional at 17.

Kyran Thompson, the highly-rated 16-year-old winger who joined the Gunners in 2024 from West Ham, turned down a new Arsenal contract to join Newcastle

Mishel Nduka joined the Arsenal academy in September 2025 after eight years at Charlton but has now moved to Manchester City, where his salary is £20,000 a week

For Arsenal, the challenge is complicated. Hale End has built a reputation for producing elite talent, with Bukayo Saka, Ethan Nwaneri and Myles Lewis-Skelly among the graduates to break into the first team in recent years.

The Gunners can point to their record of promoting youth, but the battle for the best young players is no longer simply about reputation or coaching. It is about money and opportunity.

For years, Hale End was viewed as one of Arsenal's greatest competitive advantages.

Now, as the club sits at the summit of English football, protecting that advantage is proving to be its next great challenge.

Sports.title: 'It was a s***show': Sean Dyche hits out at Everton's transfer strategy and says he was 'constantly putting out fires' before he was axed - and reveals why Andoni Iraola's 'lower league style' has landed him the Liverpool job
Sports.content:
'It was a s***show': Sean Dyche hits out at Everton's transfer strategy and says he was 'constantly putting out fires' before he was axed - and reveals why Andoni Iraola's 'lower league style' has landed him the Liverpool job

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Sean Dyche has labelled Everton's transfer strategy during his time at the club as a 's***show', while he has lauded new Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola's management skills.

Dyche, speaking on The Good, the Bad and The Football podcast - in partnership with Midnite, reflected on his near two-year spell at Everton when discussing transfer windows.

The 55-year-old highlighted the difference between his long spell at Burnley where he was able to delegate recruitment with staff aware of his priorities and demands.

By contrast, Dyche explained he needed to become more involved in the recruitment process during his time at Everton, where the Toffees had been in the midst of a financial crisis as the club battled to stay in the Premier League.

'When you are at somewhere a longer period like I was at Burnley, after year three or four we have got it up and running, it is working, everyone knows their roles,' Dyche told Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt.

'You can delegate better, once that trust builds and you are onto something, the CEO, data analysts and sports science knows what you are thinking, then it is really easy.

Sean Dyche claimed he was 'constantly putting out fires' at Everton with the club a 's***show' during his time in charge

'It is not so easy going to Everton, where it is like a f***ing s***show you know and it is constant putting out fires.

'It was a whole different ball game, brilliant in a weird way, rewarding when you get it done.

'There was a reward because you get the feeling of "I've played that little part in a really important time" and Evertonians now treat me way different than at the time.

'When I came out they were ready for me to go, but when I meet fans now they are like "thanks for helping us through it".'

Beto and Youssef Chermiti were Everton's only signings in the summer of 2023 where the club paid a fee, with Ashley Young joining on a free transfer and Arnaut Danjuma and Jack Harrison joining on loan.

Moise Kean and Alex Iwobi were among players to generate sizeable fees after being sold the same summer.

The following summer saw Everton sign Iliman Ndiaye, Jake O'Brien and Tim Iroegbunam in fee-paying moves, with Harrison, Jesper Lindstrom, Orel Mangala and Armando Broja joining on loan.

Amadou Onana was a significant summer departure with the midfielder joining Aston Villa in a £50m move.

Dyche has lauded new Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola as he complemented him for adapting his tactics to fit the Premier League

Dyche was sacked a month after the Friedkin Group completed their takeover of the club, with David Moyes appointed as his successor in January 2025.

This was followed by an overhaul of Everton's recruitment staff in June, with the appointments of a technical director, director of scouting and recruitment, a head of football strategy and analytics, and head of player trading.

After his success in guiding Burnley into Europe was compared by Scholes to Iraola's achievement last season at Bournemouth, Dyche revealed what impressed him about the Spaniard since moving to the Premier League.

Dyche highlighted how Iraola had adapted to the Premier League after a slow start, with the new Liverpool boss having quickly realised his intended style of play at Bournemouth was unlikely to yield results.

Iraola had seen his Bournemouth side thrashed 3-0 by Everton in October 2023, with his team failing to win any of his opening eight matches in charge.

Dyche pinpointed a major shift from Iraola towards 'lower league football' with higher quality players after that initial spell, with the Spaniard overseeing three impressive seasons at the club.

Dyche suggested Iraola had played 'lower league football at a high level' during his time at Bournemouth

'Iraola basically plays lower league football, but at a high level. They turn you and turn you, and force you into submission,' Dyche said.

'High quality and high energy version.

'I marvelled at it because we ran all over them at Everton when he was trying to play what you would imagine is the Spanish way.

'I think he is brilliant at managing, as you could tell he went "this ain't going to work".

'The next time we played them, he is bombing it down our throats, getting us turned, full backs keep turning and having to run back towards their own goal, centre halves thinking that they never get a break.

'They looked a different outfit and he's done a brilliant job.'

Sports.title: Sorry Morgan Rogers, you're wrong. Here's the definitive proof that Arsenal are the BIGGEST team in London as James Sharpe gives Chelsea's record signing a history lesson
Sports.content:
Thanks a bunch, Morgan. Kick the hornets’ nest, why don’t you.

‘I am joining the biggest club in London,’ declared Morgan Rogers after completing his £117million British record transfer to Chelsea from Aston Villa. Perhaps he genuinely means it. Perhaps you’re contractually obliged to say it when your new club fork out quite so much for you.

Elliot Anderson did his bit after his £116m move to Manchester City, too. ‘For as long as I’ve known, Manchester City have been the Kings of Manchester,’ said the lad born in 2002.

Anyway, back to London. Rogers’ bold claim about a club that finished 33 points behind actual Premier League champions Arsenal last season stoked up all the old feelings and arguments. So, who are the biggest club in London?

Daily Mail Sport have donned a tin hat and bravely taken it upon ourselves to provide the definitive answer to the most divisive of questions…

Morgan Rogers boldly declared he had joined London's biggest club after completing a £117m move to Chelsea, but Arsenal will also stake their claim for that title

Trophies

What do the biggest clubs do? They win stuff. And the more you win, the more your reputation grows, as do your coffers, and your size.

But it also depends on what you win. A case full of League Cups and Community Shields is far less impressive than one of Premier League trophies and European Cups.

Arsenal have more than double the league titles of Chelsea, won over a far longer period of time, and almost twice as many FA Cups. Domestically, there is only one winner.

HONOURS Competition Arsenal Chelsea Premier League/First Division 14 6 Champions League/European Cup 0 2 FA Cup 14 8 League Cup 2 5 Europa League 0 2 UEFA Conference League 0 1 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup 1 2 Club World Cup 0 2 UEFA Super Cup 0 2 Full Members' Cup 0 2 Inter Cities' Fairs Cup 1 0 Community Shield 17 4

Only, isn’t being champions of Europe (or the world) bigger than being champions of England? Arsenal’s continental shortcoming is their glaring weak spot. The biggest clubs have won the European Cup. Arsenal haven’t.

A penalty shootout against Paris Saint-Germain away from glory, of course, but Tottenham have won a European trophy more recently, so have West Ham, so have Crystal Palace.

Chelsea have two Champions Leagues, two Europa Leagues, even a Conference League.

They boasted that they are the only club in history to win every major European trophy, which, more than anything, made you spare a thought for fans of the Inter Cities Fairs Cup.

As soon as Gabriel sent his penalty high into the stands, Chelsea posted an invitation to book a stadium tour at ‘London’s Home of Trophies’, with Big Ears front and centre.

They are two-time Club World Cup winners, too, which sounds cool but is only starting to feel important now that there’s £100m to win.

Verdict: Tie

Arsenal have more than double the league titles of Chelsea and almost twice as many FA Cups

Chelsea, however, have won the Champions League twice with Arsenal's contiential shortcomings their glaring weak spot

League position

Gravitas comes with a weight of history, too. That all but one of Chelsea’s league titles have been since 2005, with a Russian oligarch signing bigger cheques than anyone else, will tell you that time is on Arsenal’s side.

Since Arsenal joined the Football League in 1893, their average league position is 8.3. Across Chelsea’s history, theirs is 12.7. Tottenham’s is 11.7.

Across the 110 seasons in which both clubs have existed, Arsenal have finished higher in 77 of them.

Even in the Premier League era, when Chelsea stormed to power, the two clubs have split a higher finish 17 times apiece, though 16 of those for the Blues’ came across an 18-season period from 2004-05 to 2022-23.

However, Arsenal’s average position of 3.8 across the entire Premier League era still betters Chelsea’s of 5.

And even now Arsenal are current champions, after finishing second three times, during which time Chelsea finished 10th and 12th.

Verdict: Arsenal

Stadium and crowd

There’s simply no comparison between the Emirates Stadium, which Arsenal moved into in 2006, and Stamford Bridge. Bigger, better, fuller.

There was a brief five-year period before Arsenal’s move during which Chelsea boasted the marginally bigger crowds but, across history, the Gunners have had the greater attendances.

Chelsea’s average crowd even dropped below 13,000 in the early 1980s. Until Chelsea get an extension, or move, they cannot compete with Arsenal. Or Tottenham.

Yes, you can suggest, as the club’s supporters’ trust did during the malaise of Wenger’s final years, that Arsenal have not always been completely honest with their attendance figures — filled seats or tickets sold — but when the club’s fans come out they do so in force. Islington Council estimated more than a million people turned up for their Premier League title bus parade.

When Chelsea had theirs in 2015, official numbers were around 70,000. Around 200,000 turned up for their first under Jose Mourinho in 2005.

Verdict: Arsenal

There is no comparison between Arsenal's Emirates Stadium and Stamford Bridge

Over a million people reportedly attended Arsenal's Premier League title parade in May

Spending Power

The biggest clubs splash the biggest cash, right? Few spend it like Chelsea.

What began under Abramovich has continued into the BlueCo years. Chelsea’s net spend — that’s NET spend — over the past five years is more than £800m, nearly £150m more than any other Premier League side and £262m more than Arsenal.

Chelsea announced a Premier League-record pre-tax loss of £262.4m earlier this year for the 2024-25 season. They have spent well over a billion but not much of it well.

BIGGEST SIGNINGS Arsenal Fee Chelsea Fee Declan Rice £105m Morgan Rogers £117m Nicolas Pepe £72m Moises Caicedo £115m Eberechi Eze £67.5m Enzo Fernandez £106.8m Kai Havertz £65m Romelu Lukaku £97.5m Viktor Gyokeres £64m Mykhaylo Mudryk £88.5m Martin Zubimendi £60m Kai Havertz £75.8m Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang £55.4m Wesley Fofana £75m Noni Madueke £52m Kepa £71.6m

Kieran Maguire, the football finance expert, recently listed the biggest wage bills in Premier League history, adjusted for football inflation and the spending power clubs had at the time.

Chelsea made up eight of the top 10 with all their seasons from 2003-04 to 2010-11 at the height of their Abramovich era.

Arsenal’s first appearance on the list, their 2011-12 season, is in 51st place. Ahead of them are 16 different Chelsea seasons, 17 Manchester United seasons, 12 Manchester City seasons and five Liverpool seasons.

And yet over previous two sets of results, Arsenal have blown Chelsea out of the water in terms of their revenue: £691m to £491m.

Declan Rice is the only Arsenal signing of more than £100m.

Chelsea now have three: Rogers, Moises Caicedo and Enzo Fernandez. Their top seven all come in higher than Arsenal’s second most expensive arrival in £72m Nicolas Pepe.

Verdict: Chelsea

Chelsea showed their financial power by signing Rogers from right under Arsenal nose

Rogers is one of three Chelsea players to cost over £100m, while Rice is Arsenal's only one

Star Power

Big spending brings big names and big managers. In the Premier League era, Arsenal have had Wenger, Unai Emery and Mikel Arteta in the dugout. Chelsea have had Mourinho (twice), Carlo Ancelotti, Rafa Benitez, Antonio Conte and Thomas Tuchel. The biggest names in the game. But then they have also had Graham Potter and Liam Rosenior.

On the pitch, few have ever had the aura of Thierry Henry, Dennis Bergkamp or Patrick Vieira. Bukayo Saka will be next. Chelsea will point to Didier Drogba and Eden Hazard. And Cole Palmer, perhaps?

Arsenal have taken a couple of Chelsea’s cast-offs in recent years, too, with Kai Havertz and Noni Madueke, and yet they are both now champions.

Arsenal lead the way, too, when it comes to producing England stars. Rice, Madueke, Saka and Eberechi Eze’s involvement in the World Cup quarter-final against Norway, took the club past 1,000 caps for Arsenal players.

Chelsea, the first club to field an all-foreign team, in 1999, stand at fewer than 750.

Verdict: Tie

Jose Mourinho is among a host of big name managers to have taken charge of Chelsea

Few can match the aura of former Arsenal stars Thierry Henry (pictured), Dennis Bergkamp and Patrick Vieira

Social Media

The true test of how big a club is in the modern era is, surely, how many followers they have on social media.

I would have staked everything on Arsenal winning this. Few supporter groups make their voices quite so piercingly heard than the Gunners’, and certainly when they feel, as they often do, that they have been wronged or robbed.

And, yet, Chelsea win on all counts. They have more followers on X, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and YouTube, to the combined tune of more than 33 million.

Verdict: Chelsea

Insider’s view

It’s clear they both crave the title. Chelsea previously trademarked their ‘CFC LDN’ branding — what better way to prove you’re London’s big dogs? ‘There’s only one answer,’ replied one Arsenal source when posed the question.

‘The way Arsenal conduct themselves comes from a place of prestige,’ a prominent agent who has dealt with both clubs tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘Chelsea have more of a big-club approach in the way they get things done. They are very much: if we want the player, we will do what it takes to get them. Put our cards on the table. That is a big-club mentality.

‘There’s definitely two different cultures, through which both see themselves as the biggest club in London but go about it in a different way. Arsenal are like your old money, slightly entitled aristocrat who can fall back on title and family history. Chelsea are the nouveau riche, super successful city worker who isn’t shy about showing off how much money they have and uses that to drive more success.’

Elon Musk might be the richest man in the world and Tesla the largest automobile company by market capitalisation, but good luck convincing anyone they are really bigger than Mercedes or Ferrari.

Verdict: Arsenal

Sorry Morgan, your new club may be big spenders but most metrics confirm the Gunners are the capital’s major players.

Overall verdict: Arsenal

Sports.title: First Danny Welbeck, now Jordan Henderson! Chelsea plot deal for England veteran, 36 - with Blues also closing in on move for Brighton star, 35, after he scored 13 Premier League goals last season
Sports.content:
First Danny Welbeck, now Jordan Henderson! Chelsea plot deal for England veteran, 36 - with Blues also closing in on move for Brighton star, 35, after he scored 13 Premier League goals last season

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Chelsea are working on a deal to sign Jordan Henderson on a free transfer from Brentford.

After missing out on Sunderland’s Granit Xhaka, the Stamford Bridge club have moved for 36-year-old Henderson to fulfil a role on the pitch and crucially in the dressing room.

As Daily Mail Sport exclusively revealed, Chelsea are already closing on a move for Danny Welbeck as manager Xabi Alonso looks to add older heads to a young squad.

Alonso has determined that the squad dynamic needs to change to help Chelsea achieve their goals and maintain a successful challenge to rivals.

There are a number of clubs interested in Henderson, who is still recovering from a fractured arm suffered during the World Cup, including two other Premier League sides, but Chelsea are favourites to sign him.

Chelsea are working on a deal to sign Brentford veteran Jordan Henderson

It comes after Daily Mail Sport exclusively revealed talks with Brighton's Danny Welbeck

New Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso (left) is keen to add experience to his squad, with 35-year-old Welbeck (right) a contender

Earlier on Monday, Daily Mail Sport revealed how 35-year-old Brighton striker Welbeck has emerged as a player of interest within Stamford Bridge, and is now a contender to join the Blues squad under Alonso.

Welbeck has scored 46 goals in 176 games in the Premier League for the Seagulls, having previously played for Manchester United and Arsenal, among others.

Chelsea currently have five strikers on their books in Joao Pedro, who is considered untouchable, Emmanuel Emegha, Liam Delap, Nicolas Jackson and Marc Guiu.

The Blues have been looking at sales or loans to trim down their options up front.

Welbeck scored 13 times in the league for Brighton in 2025-26, and was considered unfortunate not to make the England squad under Thomas Tuchel.

Joao Pedro and Delap are currently on Chelsea’s pre-season tour of Australia and Asia, with Emegha absent due to injury. Jackson is not involved due to his run at the World Cup with Senegal and Guiu has not been selected.

Welbeck joined Brighton in 2020 and triggered a one-year contract extension in March. If he moves to Stamford Bridge he would add to the lengthy list of signings Chelsea have made from Brighton in recent years - including Marc Cucurella, Moises Caicedo, Robert Sanchez and Joao Pedro.

Sports.title: Royal Ascot record-breaker who shone while trainer was battling serious illness, dies aged 20
Sports.content:
Royal Ascot record-breaker who shone while trainer was battling serious illness, dies aged 20

Ghanaati won the 2009 1,000 Guineas and Coronation Stakes during a five week period when Barry Hills was being treated for blood poisoning

View 2 Images Jockey Richard Hills celebrates as he comes home to win the Coronation Stakes on Ghanaati (Image: PA)

Brilliant filly Ghanaati, the last Classic winner trained by the late Barry Hills, has died at the age of 20, her owners Shadwell announced on Tuesday.

‌



Ghanaati was at her peak in 2009 when she captured 1,000 Guineas and the Coronation Stakes at Royal Ascot before becoming a successful broodmare. The daughter of Giant’s Causeway triumphed at Newmarket under the trainer’s son Richard Hills on her first start of the year and she remains the fastest winner in history of either the 1000 or 2000 Guineas.

‌



She confirmed her status as one of the leading fillies of her generation when following up in the Coronation Stakes, quickening clear of a high-class field to win by two lengths again in a course-record time, the second fastest running of the race.

‌



Eastender Kaiya Fraser hoping to star on the big stage at Goodwood READ MORE :

That success came on the day Barry Hills was released from hospital, where he had spent five weeks being treated for blood poisoning. Charlie Hills was running the stable during his absence.

Ghanaati went on to finish third in the Sussex Stakes and second in the Sun Chariot Stakes before she retired.

‌



She joined owners Shadwell’s broodmare band with her notable progeny including multiple Group 2 winner Mutasaabeq, Group 3 winner Wafy and Royal Hunt Cup winner Afaak.

View 2 Images Barry Hills: trainer of Ghanaati (Image: Getty Images)

Shadwell Racing Manager Angus Gold said: “Ghanaati was a fabulous race mare who gave us two special days in the spring and summer of 2009, winning the 1000 Guineas in impressive fashion on her first start and then going on to Royal Ascot where she showed she had improved by blitzing the Coronation Stakes on the day that Barry Hills was released from hospital after a lengthy spell of illness.

Article continues below

“As a granddaughter of Height Of Fashion she was particularly close to Sheikh Hamdan’s heart, and his family were very sad to hear of her death, and we will always remember her as a top class miler and an outstanding Guineas winner.”

Sports.title: Worrying Anthony Joshua footage emerges from dramatic KO win
Sports.content:
Worrying Anthony Joshua footage emerges from dramatic KO win

Anthony Joshua nearly saw his fight with Tyson Fury fall apart after he was knocked down twice by Kristian Prenga before rallying to a KO win in the second round

View Image Worrying footage has emerged following Anthony Joshua's stunning KO victory

Anthony Joshua has been told he no longer has the killer instinct to be a fighter, while his cornermen also took some shots in the Brit's win over Kristian Prenga on Saturday night.

‌



The former two-time heavyweight is due to fight long-time rival Tyson Fury later this year, but nearly saw the fight slip away from him after being knocked down twice in the opening round by Prenga. 'AJ' managed to survive the round and turned the tide in the second before eventually knocking the Albanian out.

‌



Recent footage has emerged of what was said to Joshua after the chaotic opening three minutes. A dejected 'AJ' can be seen sat firmly in his stool, while his corner were barking instructions at him. The Brit teamed up with Oleksandr Usyk's team in the build-up to his fight with Jake Paul, and had the Ukrainian's team-members again this past weekend.

‌



Despite telling his cornermen he felt 'good,' Joshua was slammed for not 'listening' to the corner, before being begged to 'stay in the ring' and to 'not go down'. The 36-year-old was then told to 'fire'. The advice seemed to pay off after he scored a second round KO, but fans were left rather concerned by the footage.

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Kristian Prenga's team addresses conspiracy theories after Anthony Joshua loss READ MORE :

Despite rallying to a famous knockout victory, one fan believes Joshua is completely spent, posting: "I just don’t think the fight is in him no more. You need killer instinct to be a fighter and you can see it’s gone." The Brit's team was also at the heart of some harsh criticism for the advice they gave their star man at the end of the opening stanza.

"'You don’t listen'. 'You need to stay.' 'Don’t go down.' Great advice," wrote one sarcastic fan. Another posted: "Looks like AJ's corner was auditioning for a drama series, next thing you know they'll need popcorn," while a third commented: "Absolutely terrible corner advice here." Another fan replied: "Absolute amateurs." One user agreed, writing: "Ridiculous cornering."

Anthony Joshua sends violent message to Tyson Fury after brutal comeback KO READ MORE :

Many were quick to weigh in and offer their verdict on the fight, including boxing coach Dave Coldwell - who offered a rather brutal take on the fight, posting: "Joshua is without a doubt shot to bits. Punch resistance looks completely gone. Last thing a fighter loses is his punch and that’s what got him out of jail tonight."

Article continues below

Nevertheless, a date with Fury awaits, and Joshua was eager to send a direct message to his foe after the fight. “Wait a minute - have we got Tyson Fury in the room? Wait, wait, wait, to more important matters - is he here or not? Fair do’s. Imma rip his heart out. I'm the meanest and vicious champion's ever been," he said.

“Listen, all jokes aside, you see, there’s two sides of this thing. One is fire. You have to have that vim, that grrr. But also respect. I respect everything he has done. And everything that he has achieved. As someone who who has been calling for the fight for a long time, we're here now. Shout out to his Excellency. Shout to Eddie Hearn for making these opportunities possible, and I hope the fans will be in for a lovely treat.”

Sports.title: Man Utd stance on hijacking Chelsea's Danny Welbeck transfer after secret talks
Sports.content:
Man Utd stance on hijacking Chelsea's Danny Welbeck transfer after secret talks

Danny Welbeck is in talks to join Chelsea from Brighton in a shock move and Manchester United have also previously considered re-signing their former academy striker

View 2 Images Manchester United have previously made moves to re-sign Danny Welbeck (Image: GLYN KIRK, AFP via Getty Images)

Manchester United have given no indication that they are considering a fresh attempt to re-sign Danny Welbeck, who is in talks to sign for Chelsea.

‌



The 35-year-old striker is a United academy graduate who went on to represent the club in the Premier League before joining Arsenal in 2014 for £16million. Welbeck has spent the last six years at Brighton, scoring 23 league goals in the last two seasons for the Seagulls.

‌



Welbeck's fine form last season, plus his wealth of top-flight experience and leadership qualities, has seen him emerge as a surprise transfer target for Chelsea, who are looking to bolster their squad ahead of the new season.

‌



The Blues and Brighton are currently in talks over a deal for Welbeck, whose contract on the south coast expires next year.

Chelsea line up shock Danny Welbeck swoop after Xabi Alonso green lights transfer READ MORE :

Intriguingly, Manchester United are also in the market for a striker this summer. However, there is nothing to currently suggest they have designs on hijacking Chelsea's move for Welbeck, according to The Athletic.

United have, though, held discussions with Welbeck about a romantic return to Old Traffic in both 2024 and 2025. It's even claimed that talks to bring the veteran back home got 'quite far' last year, with United eventually signing Benjamin Sesko to bolster their attack.

‌



View 2 Images Chelsea are currently in talks to sign Welbeck from Brighton (Image: Izzy Poles/AMA)

Interest in Welbeck comes off the back of his impact since joining Brighton, who qualified for the Europa Conference League last season. Welbeck was their top scorer in the Premier League, plundering 13 goals.

After narrowly missing out on a place in England's World Cup squad, Welbeck is viewed by Chelsea as a quality support option for their first-choice striker, Joao Pedro. Welbeck played with the Brazilian previously at Brighton and would become the eighth player to move between the clubs in recent years if a transfer is finalised.

Article continues below

As well as their pursuit of Welbeck, Chelsea are also working on a deal to sign the veteran midfielder, Jordan Henderson, from Brentford on a free transfer. The 36-year-old still has a year left on the contract he signed when he joined the Bees last summer.

Sports.title: Liverpool given free run at Bradley Barcola as Arsenal make transfer decision
Sports.content:
Liverpool given free run at Bradley Barcola as Arsenal make transfer decision

Paris Saint-Germain are open to selling Bradley Barcola and Liverpool's chances of signing him have received a boost thanks to Arsenal's fresh stance on the player

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola is a top target for Liverpool (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

Arsenal are not actively pursuing Bradley Barcola, giving Liverpool a free run at signing him. Barcola, 23, has been of interest to both Premier League clubs throughout the summer transfer window, with Paris Saint-Germain open to a sale.

‌



PSG would demand an eye-watering £145million for the winger, who was in and out of France's starting line-up at the World Cup. Liverpool made him a top target and have now been boosted in their pursuit after Arsenal decided to prioritise a stunning move for Vinicius Junior.

‌



The Athletic report that Arsenal's focus is firmly on Real Madrid star, who has one year left on his £400,000-a-week contract. A deal for Barcola is therefore unlikely unless Vinicius snubs the Gunners.

‌



But even with Arsenal out of the picture, Liverpool appear to be reluctant to shell out a club-record fee for Barcola. PSG's argument is that Barcola is worth considerably more than Elliot Anderson and Morgan Rogers, who Manchester City and Chelsea respectively have paid £116m and £117m for this summer.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Federico Chiesa confirms Liverpool future stance and reveals new role under Andoni Iraola READ MORE :

The Frenchman's stock is also high thanks to helping Luis Enrique's side win back-to-back Champions Leagus and having come through Barcelona's famous academy. Enrique is said to only want players who are committed to PSG, plunging Barcola's future into uncertainty.

‌



Barcola himself doesn't know the answer, having been asked about the prospect of a transfer earlier this month. "I'm focused on the World Cup," the 23-year-old said. "What happens after that, I don't know."

Should Liverpool pay £145million for Bradley Barcola? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola's future at Paris Saint-Germain is uncertain (Image: Franco Arland/Getty Images)

‌



New manager Andoni Iraola has admitted that Liverpool 'definitely need to sign a winger', having been asked about the Reds' transfer plans last week. "When the market is open, you have to be always open to new options to improve the squad," Iraola explained.

"There are obvious situations where we need to sign players. Winger for example, we definitely need to sign a winger, but there are other situations where we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what is the cost, how we also see the players we have."

Liverpool will kick-off their Premier League campaign and new era under Iraola away to Newcastle on Sunday, August 23. The Reds have played one pre-season friendly so far, beating Sunderland 4-2.

Sports.title: Mohamed Salah transfer at risk of collapse as new club enters race for Liverpool legend
Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah transfer at risk of collapse as new club enters race for Liverpool legend

Mohamed Salah had been in talks with Besiktas over a move to the Turkish club but one of their senior figures has delivered a damning update on his potential transfer move

View 2 Images Mohamed Salah was planning to leave last summer before signing a new deal (Image: Liverpool FC/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Besiktas have claimed they've walked away from talks to sign Mohamed Salah despite several meetings with the former Liverpool man.

‌



The Egyptian is a free agent after being allowed to leave Anfield a year before the end of his contract and, now 34, the forward is looking for a new club, with the Turkish side believing they were leading the race.

‌



Salah had been the subject of approach from Besiktas with the club's president Serdal Adali telling Turkish media they were awaiting a final decision, but director Onder Ozen has claimed they have hit a roadblock with communications coming to a stand still.

‌



He believes Salah's representatives are in talks with another club but insists their final offer remains on the table if they want to make the move happen.

Free agent XI including Man Utd flop, Liverpool legend and current England star READ MORE :

PSG tell Liverpool outrageous Bradley Barcola transfer price as Chelsea cause problems READ MORE :

Ozen told Turkish media: "We contacted Salah, this also involved a financing model. Salah is a global star, a respected athlete. We met with Salah three times before the financial part of the negotiations was discussed.

"Up to this point, everything was smooth. When the financial side began, the initial smoothness slowed down from July 21st onwards. Requests began to arrive that would both disrupt the flow of information and create a deadlock in the financial process. I can assume that a respected athlete like Salah was unaware of this.

‌



"The club has a policy, and it cannot deviate from that policy, our President has very clearly identified his position and has stayed there. I don't have a chance to say yes or no, Besiktas's offer, made under its own terms, is clear. If a response comes to this offer, it can be evaluated.

View 2 Images Mohamed Salah left Liverpool at the end of last season (Image: Getty Images)

"But Besiktas will not make another offer. They said they are also in talks with another club, maybe they will get a result from there. The last offer we made to Salah is the final point that does not harm Besiktas's club identity."

Article continues below

Besiktas have just signed Leandro Trossard from Arsenal as they look to bolster their ranks ahead of the upcoming season. Whilst being competitive they've not claimed the Turkish title since 2021 with Galatasaray the dominant force currently.

Salah will not be without options has long been linked with a move to Saudi Arabia with Liverpool turning down lucrative offers in the past whilst the MLS also remains a possibility if the ex-Red wants to see out his playing days in the United States.

Sports.title: Kristian Prenga's team addresses conspiracy theories after Anthony Joshua loss
Sports.content:
Kristian Prenga's team addresses conspiracy theories after Anthony Joshua loss

Anthony Joshua was knocked down twice in the opening round by Kristian Prenga before rallying back to knock his rival out in the second stanza

View Image Kristian Prenga knocked Anthony Joshua down twice in the first round before suffering a brutal second round KO defeat (Image: Getty Images)

Kristian Prenga's manager has downplayed talk of foul play in the Albanian's defeat to Anthony Joshua, but claims his star client was ill two weeks before the Saudi showdown.

‌



Joshua was back in action this past weekend for the first time since being involved in a tragic car crash which resulted in the death of close friends Latif Ayodele and Sina Ghami. A win in Jeddah for the former two-time heavyweight champion would finally earn him a date with Tyson Fury - after the 'Gypsy King' won his warm-up fight against Mariusz Wach

‌



'AJ' nearly saw a fight with Fury snatched away from him after he was dropped twice in the opening round by Prenga, before rallying back in the second to stop his Albanian rival in Jeddah. Fans immediately started to scratch their heads as Prenga looked a completely different fighter in the second round.

‌



There have since been whispers of outside influences, but Prenga's manager Keith Sullivan has denied all the conspiracy theories, and revealed the heavyweight scrapper was ill in the build-up to the clash. Speaking to talkSPORT, presenter Ade Oladipo asked Sullivan to adress all the theories - to which he answered: "We can clear those up very easily in one word, impossible. There were two conspiracies. One was that Turki (Alalshikh) had come over to our corner...

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

Tearful Anthony Joshua can’t get words out as he pays tribute to late friends READ MORE :

"You were there, Ade, Turki was not even in Jeddah, so that never happened. That's gone, throw it away. The other conspiracy was that somebody from Sela or Matchroom had come and whispered in our corner. Look at the footage, that never happened. I'll tell you what happened, and this is the first time I'm mentioning this, this is the first time anybody from Team Prenga is mentioning this, and we had no intention of ever discussing this.

‌



"I had a little team meeting on a conference call this morning and I felt that, because of the conspiracy theories that were floating, I had to go down this road and I didn't want to go down this round because... Everybody I deal with in boxing, I'm a person that believes in responsibility and accountability, and accept the outcome of things, and we do."

It was at this point that Sullivan made a rather stunning revelation that Prenga was ill and unable to spar in the weeks leading up to the Joshua fight. "But, what happened here was Kristian had gotten very sick leading up to the fight. He didn't spar or train for two weeks before he got to Jeddah," he continued.

"He had a 102 (degrees Fahrenheit) fever and he was in bed for eight days straight... he moved camp over to Dubai, he brought a doctor in, drew some blood to make sure there wasn't something more serious going on.

‌



Anthony Joshua sends violent message to Tyson Fury after brutal comeback KO READ MORE :

"They said he was just run down and they thought it was a flu or cold, or something, and he would get over it. It took 14 days, so we had the last seven days before we went to Jeddah for training. We had a sparring partner there in Dubai who we didn't use at all... we couldn't get him out of bed to go for a walk.

"In the first round, he came out and just gassed himself out. The instructions in the corner for the second round were, 'Continue what you're doing, keep the pressure on, keep pumping the jab and when you have the opportunities, take him'. Kristian stood up off the stool to start, when that bell rang for the second round, and he said to me he felt like he was back in that bed that he was in for eight days, when he was gasping for air and had no energy."

He concluded: "But, there was no... again, I'm not making excuses, I think it was the most exciting five-and-a-half minutes of boxing that I've witnessed in a very long time."

Sports.title: Ronnie O'Sullivan sets retirement deadline and makes Crucible vow - 'Have to be realistic'
Sports.content:
Ronnie O'Sullivan sets retirement deadline and makes Crucible vow - 'Have to be realistic'

Snooker legend Ronnie O'Sullivan feels he is unlikely to continue playing beyond 2028, meaning he may have just two more attempts to win an eighth world title at the Crucible

View 3 Images Ronnie O'Sullivan has suggested he will not play beyond 2028

Ronnie O'Sullivan has conceded that he is unlikely to continue playing snooker beyond 2028, leaving him with just two more opportunities to land an unprecedented eighth world championship at the Crucible.

‌



'The Rocket', 50, is widely recognised as the sport's greatest player and has a glittering CV brimming with trophies and accolades. But O'Sullivan has slowed down in recent years and is currently ranked 14th in the world.

‌



He is currently participating in the Shanghai Masters: a lucrative but non-ranking event. O'Sullivan's current ranking would guarantee him a spot at the World Championships next April, though dropping out of the top 16 would force him into qualification.

‌



But O'Sullivan insists he will NOT play qualifiers — and while he is desperate to win another world title in Sheffield, he is unlikely to play for longer than the next two seasons.

Snooker star Kyren Wilson's house burgled as watches worth thousands stolen READ MORE :

O’Sullivan said: “I’m glad I’m at the end of my career and I don’t have to face these young Chinese talents much. Because they’re just like machines. They’re just phenomenal.

“I have to be realistic. I’m 50 now. I play for two hours and I need to lay down for two or three hours. It’s very hard for me to get going again. This game, alright, you don’t have to run around on a pitch. Mentally, you have to concentrate. It’s draining.

‌



“When you’re young, you can just keep going for an hour and not get tired. Now, I need to have a lie down. You see your grandparents, sleeping in their chairs. You get a little bit tired.

“I have to be realistic about what’s possible. Just have to accept it. Especially when you see talent like that, you can’t fight it.

View 3 Images O'Sullivan is still chasing an eighth world title (Image: Getty)

‌



“I’d love to win another World Championship. I’ve got two attempts at it. For three years previous I wasn’t cueing well enough. So I feel like if I can find a bit of cueing and some form in Sheffield, then who knows?

“If I don’t do it this year or the next year, then it’ll definitely never happen. I’m pleased with my career. I’m happy with how things have gone.”

O'Sullivan went on to confirm that he plans to take stock of his remarkable career in two years time with a view to calling it quits - and that he definitely will not be resorting to playing qualifiers to keep himself in the game for another Crucible triumph.

‌



View 3 Images O'Sullivan won his last World Championship title in 2022 (Image: VCG/VCG via Getty Images)

“I will try to enjoy these next two years,” he continued. “I’ll reassess it in 2028. If things are going really well and I surprise myself, then maybe you can extend it.

“You have to be realistic. I am definitely not going to be playing qualifiers, put it that way.

Article continues below

“You won’t see me go down to Barnsley, trying to win qualifier matches and all that sort of stuff.

“I have to be realistic, if that happens, then obviously that’s the end of my career. Hopefully I can go for at least another two seasons.”

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
