A festival born from a historic moment

The Festival Internacional de Música Sacra de Bogotá (FIMSAC) was founded in 2012 to commemorate the 50th anniversary of the Second Vatican Council. It has since grown into one of Latin America’s most distinctive cultural gatherings, held every year between September and October.

The 2026 edition marks a decade and a half of uninterrupted programming. What began as a modest ecclesiastical music series now commands national and international recognition, including designation by Colombia’s government as one of the country’s 100 events of national interest.

The festival has also been named a Metropolitan Project of Bogotá. In a rare honour, it received the Honorary Plaque of the Order of Isabella the Catholic from King Felipe VI of Spain, underscoring its cultural diplomacy credentials.

Grand concerts define the anniversary era

Recent editions illustrate the scale that now characterises the Bogotá Sacred Music Festival. The 2024 edition, themed “La Consagración” (The Consecration), brought together more than 750 artists from 14 countries across 40 events in 20 venues, with an estimated 10,000 attendees.

The grand opening featured Mahler’s Symphony No. 2 “Resurrection” at the Teatro Mayor Julio Mario Santo Domingo.

The National Symphony Orchestra of Colombia and the National Choir performed alongside international soloists under conductor Arthur Fagen.

The closing concert presented Beethoven’s Mass in D major with the Women’s Philharmonic Orchestra of Bogotá and the Youth Choir of the Bogotá Philharmonic Orchestra. Admission was free, reflecting the festival’s core commitment to accessibility.

The 2025 edition raised the bar further

The XIV Festival in 2025, under the theme “La Gloria” (The Glory), expanded the international footprint to roughly 750 artists from 16 countries. It maintained the same 40-event, 20-venue structure over four weeks.

The Teatro Mayor again anchored the programming, opening with Verdi’s Nabucco and closing with Brahms’s German Requiem. Both featured the National Choir and National Symphony Orchestra of Colombia, reinforcing the festival’s symphonic-choral identity.

Programming stretched well beyond the European canon. Audiences heard medieval chant, Latin American baroque, Vivaldi and Purcell, gospel from Colombia’s Caribbean coast, and sacred music from Iran, Turkey and Israel, alongside new commissions such as Diego Vega’s Gloria.

Venues that bridge the sacred and the civic

The Bogotá Sacred Music Festival uses a dual-venue strategy that sets it apart. Historic churches such as the Catedral Primada, San Ignacio, San José, San Agustín, Santa Bárbara, and La Candelaria host intimate performances in their original acoustic and spiritual settings.

Modern cultural spaces run in parallel: the Museo Nacional, Teatro Mayor, Auditorio Fabio Lozano, universities, hospitals, and even prisons. This deliberate mix takes sacred music out of the sanctuary and into the broader civic life of the city.

The result is a festival that feels simultaneously rooted in Bogotá’s colonial religious architecture and forward-looking in its reach. For visiting audiences, it offers a rare chance to experience the city’s built heritage while hearing world-class performances.

What the 15-year milestone means for Bogotá

Fifteen years of uninterrupted annual programming signals institutional maturity. The festival has moved from a niche ecclesiastical event to a metropolitan project with national-interest designation, royal honours, and a reliably international artist roster.

For Bogotá’s cultural brand, the festival provides a counter-narrative to headlines about security or politics. It positions the city as a regional capital of sacred music, capable of mounting Mahler, Beethoven, Brahms, and Verdi with its own national orchestras and choirs.

The economic read-through is tangible. A month-long festival with thousands of attendees, international artists, and free admission drives footfall to neighbourhoods, restaurants, and hotels.

Cultural tourism of this kind builds the soft infrastructure that makes Bogotá attractive to expats and long-term investors.

Why the Bogotá Sacred Music Festival matters for investors and expats

A city that sustains a free, large-scale, internationally recognised cultural event for 15 years is signalling something about its institutional capacity and quality of life. For professionals considering relocation or investment, cultural infrastructure of this calibre is a meaningful data point.

The festival’s interreligious mission also speaks to Bogotá’s social fabric. Programming that brings together Catholic, Protestant, Jewish, Muslim, and indigenous sacred traditions in a single curated season reflects a city managing pluralism through culture rather than conflict.

The 2026 edition will be closely watched for any expansion in scale, new commissions, or diplomatic presence. Organisers publish detailed schedules each year on the official FIMSAC site and through Bogotá’s cultural agencies, typically in the months leading up to the September opening.

Frequently Asked Questions

When does the Bogotá Sacred Music Festival take place?

The festival runs annually between September and October. The 2026 edition marks its 15th anniversary, with exact dates typically announced by organisers several months in advance on the official FIMSAC website and through Bogotá’s cultural agencies.

Are the concerts at the Bogotá Sacred Music Festival free?

Yes, between 70 and 80 percent of all events are free to the public. This includes major symphonic-choral works at the Teatro Mayor, making world-class sacred music accessible to broad audiences across Bogotá.

What kind of music is performed at the Bogotá Sacred Music Festival?

Programming spans large symphonic-choral works by composers such as Mahler, Beethoven, Brahms, and Verdi, alongside medieval chant, Latin American baroque, gospel from Colombia’s Caribbean coast, and sacred music from Iran, Turkey, Israel, and indigenous traditions. Recent editions have also included new commissioned works.

World.title: Costa Rica Moves to Widen Extradition of Its Own Citizens
World.content:
President Laura Fernández asked lawmakers on Monday to widen the narrow list of crimes for which Costa Rica may hand its own citizens over to foreign courts, proposing a constitutional amendment that would add money laundering, human trafficking, arms trafficking, contract killing and cybercrime to the two grounds that exist today.

The president arrived at the Legislative Assembly mid-morning accompanied by her cabinet, police directors and members of the unit the government calls Fuerza Élite, and delivered a second package of six security bills. The extradition proposal was the centerpiece of her presentation but was not among the files formally handed over, because legislative procedure does not allow constitutional reforms to be processed during extraordinary sessions. The government said it will file that text on Monday, August 3.

Costa Rica has permitted the extradition of its nationals only since 2025, and only for international drug trafficking and terrorism. Fernández wants to add seven further categories: money laundering; human trafficking and migrant smuggling; illegal arms trafficking; trafficking in organs, tissues and human stem cells; contract killing and homicides linked to organized criminal structures; participation in transnational criminal organizations; and cybercrime, cyberterrorism and cyberfraud that compromise national security or the critical infrastructure of the Costa Rican state.

Fernández framed the proposal as a move against criminal structures rather than a general loosening of protections for citizens, telling lawmakers that Costa Rican nationality is a right and a source of pride for millions of honest citizens and <cite index=”1-1″>not a shield for members of transnational criminal organizations.

She said the mechanism would remain exceptional and would require a final ruling from Costa Rican courts in every case, describing it as not an automatic or generalized extradition of nationals. The proposal also preserves the dual criminality requirement, meaning the conduct must be a crime both in Costa Rica and in the country requesting the person.

The prohibition Fernández is seeking to narrow further dates to the aftermath of the 1948 civil war, when the drafters of the current constitution barred the forced removal of citizens from national territory. That ban held for more than seven decades. The Legislative Assembly approved the amendment to Article 32 unanimously in its final debate on May 15, 2025, and the reform was promulgated as Law 10730 and published on May 28 of that year. A companion reform harmonizing the 1971 Extradition Law with the new constitutional text cleared Congress the following November.

On March 20 of this year, former Supreme Court magistrate and former security minister Celso Gamboa Sánchez and Edwin Danney López Vega were handed to United States agents at the San Jose Airport and flown to Texas aboard a DEA aircraft, the first extraditions of Costa Rican nationals in our history.

Both face cocaine conspiracy charges in the Eastern District of Texas. The appeals court that authorized the transfer required written assurances from Washington that neither man would face life imprisonment or a sentence longer than 50 years, the ceiling permitted under Costa Rican law, and that time served in pretrial detention here would be credited against any sentence.

That same ruling exposed a question the courts have not settled. Judges accepted a defense argument on non-retroactivity in the case of a third man, Álvarez Alfaro, declining to apply the 2025 reform to conduct predating it. Whether nationals can be extradited for acts committed before May 2025 remains contested, and any expansion of the grounds would inherit the same dispute.

Constitutional amendments move slowly in Costa Rica by design. The text must win a two-thirds majority in three debates, then be taken up again and approved in three more debates after the Assembly’s annual turnover, meaning no reform filed in August could take effect before the second half of the current legislative period at the earliest.

The five bills Fernández did file on Monday address the ordinary criminal system. One would replace the preliminary hearing in the Criminal Procedure Code with a single pre-trial hearing before the same court that will hear the case, which the president said would cut duplicated steps that delay resolutions. Another would require electronic ankle monitoring for anyone granted an alternative to prison after a final sentence, replacing arrangements such as signing in every fifteen days.

A third would classify illegal mining as organized crime and raise penalties for extraction, processing, financing, transport or storage to between six and ten years, with confiscation of machinery and registry freezes on linked properties. A fourth would allow parents jailed over unpaid child support to serve under electronic monitoring instead, on the reasoning that a father in prison cannot earn the money he owes.

The fifth restores older police rank titles and requires a university degree and fifteen years of service for senior command posts. A planned reform of the Dirección de Inteligencia y Seguridad Nacional was pulled from the package and deferred to a third round of bills.

The government has now sent twelve security bills to Congress since mid-June. Homicides, meanwhile, are running below last year’s pace. The Judicial Investigation Agency counted 401 killings through July 6, fifty-two fewer than the same point in 2025, with settling of scores recorded as the leading motive and San José, Limón and Puntarenas the most affected provinces.

World.title: Costa Rica Reworks $400 Million Limón Hospital Tender After Failed Bid
World.content:
Costa Rica’s public health system is preparing to relaunch the tender for a new hospital in Limón during the final week of July, seven months after the first competition for the roughly $400 million project closed without a single company submitting an offer.

The Caja Costarricense de Seguro Social (CCSS) has rewritten the terms of the competition to address the objection contractors raised most consistently the first time around. Under the original terms, the winning firm would have been locked into its quoted price for the full life of a project expected to run several years, with no mechanism to recover cost increases if the exchange rate moved, if steel and cement rose, or if freight became more expensive. Jorge Granados, the CCSS manager of infrastructure and technology, confirmed that the institution has secured a change to that provision for the new tender.

The absence of a price-adjustment clause was not an oversight. The first competition was structured as a turnkey contract covering design, construction and equipment in a single award, and the regulations accompanying the General Public Contracting Law bar price readjustment mechanisms in contracts of that type. Granados told the CCSS board earlier this year that when the institution surveyed the companies that had declined to bid, the inability to adjust prices was the reason they named most often. On a project of this size and duration, he said, ordinary movement in input costs becomes a risk the bidder alone would have to absorb.

Construction firms cited additional concerns. Security conditions in the province and the repeated closures of Route 32, the highway that connects the Caribbean coast to the Central Valley, both came up in the CCSS survey, along with uncertainty over the colón’s behavior against the dollar. The institution has characterized those as secondary to the pricing question, though they help explain why a project in Limón in particular drew no takers.

The second change to the tender is structural. The first competition was open only to companies that had cleared an earlier international prequalification round, which in practice narrowed the field to five Costa Rican firms. Representatives of all five visited the 19-hectare (47-acre) site in June of last year, and none of them bid when the window closed in December. The new process discards prequalification entirely and will be run as an open public tender, which allows companies beyond that original group, including foreign firms, to compete alongside them. Mónica Taylor, the CCSS executive president, has said the institution intends to draw bidders from abroad.

The financial figures attached to the project have shifted with the currency. The tender declared unsuccessful was valued at approximately ¢208.78 billion, a figure set when the colón stood considerably weaker against the dollar than it does now. The CCSS currently describes the project as costing close to $400 million, which at the Banco Central de Costa Rica reference rate of ¢455.40 to the dollar would translate to roughly ¢182 billion. The gap between those two numbers over a period of months is a fair illustration of the exposure contractors said they were unwilling to carry.

How quickly the relaunch translates into visible work on the ground is the open question. Taylor has previously indicated that awarding a contract of this scale would take about a year. Granados has since offered a longer estimate, warning that even with the tender published in the coming days, the contracting and award process for a project of this magnitude can run up to two years before construction begins. Once building starts, he has estimated roughly two and a half years to completion, with late 2029 as a tentative date for the hospital to open its doors.

That timeline sits well beyond what the institution promised the province. In a 2023 press statement the CCSS said the facility would be ready by the end of 2027. President Laura Fernández has asked whether groundbreaking could be scheduled for August 31, 2027, the Day of the Black Person and Afro-Costa Rican Culture, a date that would now mark the start of construction rather than the opening the province was originally told to expect.

The failed tender has drawn official scrutiny. The Defensoría de los Habitantes opened an investigation into the process, requesting that the CCSS submit an improvement plan for the project along with the specific adjustments planned to the tender terms, the contracting model and the participation conditions, and the corrective measures it intends to take in the short, medium and long term. The ombudsman’s office framed the review as a matter of verifying efficiency, reasonableness and transparency in a project it described as essential to the right to health for the population of Limón.

The current Hospital Tony Facio Castro serves the entire Caribbean province, including the cruise port at Limón, the beach communities of Cahuita and Puerto Viejo, and the agricultural districts along Route 32. Its physical condition has been the central argument for replacement for years, and every month the new tender does not produce a contract is another month the province waits on a building the CCSS itself has called urgent.

Whether the revised terms are enough to attract offers will be visible within weeks of publication. If the second competition also closes without bids, the institution will be back at a starting point it has now reached twice.

World.title: Bail denied for Manuel De Jesus Flores, accused of sexually assaulting 10-year-old girl
World.content:
Bail denied for Manuel De Jesus Flores, accused of sexually assaulting 10-year-old girl

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A resident of the Lords Bank area, Ladyville, was remanded to the Belize Central Prison on Monday morning after appearing in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on sexual assault charges involving a 10-year-old minor.

Manuel De Jesus Flores appeared in Court #5 before a Senior Magistrate to answer to two counts of sexual assault. Allegations are that on July 18, 2026, Flores intentionally and unlawfully touched the female minor, who is 10 years and 5 months old, without her consent.

Court details reveal that Flores allegedly pressed his body against the child before grabbing her with his right hand, pulling down her blouse, and touching her breast.

Flores was represented by attorney Sharon Pitts-Robateau, who submitted a strong application for bail. Pitts-Robateau argued that her client is gainfully employed as a mason and emphasized that he remains presumed innocent until proven guilty, as the charges against him are currently allegations. She argued that the functional purpose of bail is to ensure a defendant’s attendance in court, which could be managed through strictly enforced court conditions.

Police Prosecutor Sergeant Ayala vigorously objected to bail, urging the court to consider the extreme vulnerability of the young victim, the serious nature and prevalence of sexual offenses, and the risk that Flores might reoffend or interfere with the victim or the ongoing police investigation, given that the alleged incident took place at around 12:30 a.m.

After weighing submissions from both the defense and prosecution, the sitting Senior Magistrate denied bail due to the severity of the charges. Flores has been remanded to prison until his next court appearance scheduled for September 17, 2026.

World.title: Police officer pleads guilty to having sex multiple times with 13-year-old girl; Had sex with her in her mother’s house – showed up in police uniform
World.content:
Police officer pleads guilty to having sex multiple times with 13-year-old girl; Had sex with her in her mother’s house – showed up in police uniform

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 29-year-old police officer is behind bars tonight after pleading guilty in the High Court to four counts of Unlawful Sexual Intercourse (USI) involving a minor.

Police Constable Dexter Diego admitted to the charges on Monday morning before Justice Nigel Pilgrim. The trial was expected to begin on Monday but concluded in less than an hour when Diego entered guilty pleas on all counts. Diego had sex with the victim once when she was 13 years old and three times when she was 14 years old.

According to the agreed facts presented in court, Diego was a family friend who first became acquainted with the victim in 2022. Over a 10-month period, the two maintained regular communication and developed a close relationship in secret without the knowledge of the child’s mother.

The incidents took place between late 2022 and early 2023. The first instance occurred between late December 2022 and January 2023, when the 13-year-old victim was babysitting a relative’s children. Diego visited the home and engaged in sexual acts and repeated intercourse with the minor throughout the night, leading to a single charge for that date.

The remaining charges stem from three separate incidents in early 2023. Between mid-February and March 2023, Diego visited the victim’s home uninvited while her mother was away and had sexual intercourse with her. On February 27, 2023, Diego again visited the minor at her home around 9:00 a.m. and engaged in sexual intercourse. The final incident took place on March 26, 2023, when Diego visited the victim’s house while dressed in his police uniform and had sexual intercourse with her.

Diego was represented in court by attorney Hurl Hamilton.

Justice Pilgrim has deferred sentencing until September 8, 2026. Before delivering the sentence, the court has ordered the preparation of a Prison Report, a Social Inquiry Report, and a Victim Impact Statement. Diego remains in custody pending his sentencing hearing.

World.title: Gunman fires at GI3 officers during Belize City pursuit
World.content:
Gunman fires at GI3 officers during Belize City pursuit

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating an armed confrontation in which a gunman allegedly opened fire on members of the Gang Intelligence, Investigation and Interdiction Unit, commonly known as GI3.

The incident occurred on July 23, 2026, while GI3 officers were conducting mobile operations in the Saint Martin’s and Port Loyola areas of Belize City.

Police say officers attempted to intercept a vehicle of interest, but its driver refused to stop, prompting a pursuit. The fleeing vehicle eventually crashed into a lamp post, after which three people exited and ran.

Investigators allege that the front-seat passenger fired at the officers, who returned fire. All three occupants managed to escape, but no police officers were injured.

The vehicle was subsequently impounded, and police say significant progress has been made in the investigation. Separate reporting placed the incident in the Police Street area behind the Foam Factory and indicated that it occurred during the early-morning hours.

World.title: Baby placed in Human Services care after mother allegedly failed to return for the infant
World.content:
Baby placed in Human Services care after mother allegedly failed to return for the infant

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A baby has been placed in the care of the Human Services Department after the child’s mother allegedly left the infant with a woman in Belize City and failed to return.

Police became involved after responding to a report of a small fire on the stairway of a residence. After extinguishing the fire, the occupant found a birth document near the area where the blaze had occurred.

The document was eventually linked to a baby who had been left at another nearby residence. The caretaker told investigators that a woman she knew only by her first name had visited and asked her to call a taxi. While they waited, the child fell asleep and was placed inside the home.

The mother reportedly left the premises and did not return for the child. Police have since located her, while the baby has been handed over to Human Services.

Authorities say a welfare assessment and consultation are being conducted to determine what caused the mother to leave the child. Police have not established that the stairway fire was intended to harm the baby.

World.title: Fire contained at downtown Belize City’s Abdo Building
World.content:
Fire contained at downtown Belize City’s Abdo Building

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Fire officials are investigating a fire that broke out inside the Abdo Building at the corner of Albert and Orange streets in downtown Belize City.

Police were alerted to the blaze at approximately 12:44 a.m. on Sunday, July 26, 2026. Criminal Investigation Branch personnel responded and found National Fire Service officers already working to extinguish the flames.

The businessman occupying the affected ground-floor premises told police that he had left the property and was later alerted to the fire. He reportedly rents the building, while the contents of the store belong to him and are insured.

The quick response prevented the blaze from spreading extensively to the building’s upper level. Police are awaiting an official report from the National Fire Service to determine whether the fire was caused by an electrical fault or was deliberately set.

World.title: Police investigate break-in at Atlantic Bank’s Ladyville branch
World.content:
Police investigate break-in at Atlantic Bank’s Ladyville branch

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating a burglary at the Atlantic Bank branch in Ladyville that caused damage to the building and its automated teller machine.

Investigators were called to the branch on Thursday, July 23, 2026, after signs of forced entry were discovered. Police say nothing of significance appears to have been stolen.

The ATM was damaged, apparently after the intruder or intruders had already gained entry to the building. Police have declined to reveal how the building was entered.

Scenes of Crime technicians processed the location and lifted several fingerprints that investigators hope will help identify those responsible. Atlantic Bank subsequently advised customers that the Ladyville branch was open and its ATM service had been restored.

World.title: Mexican motorcyclist Nidia Hernandez killed in collision near Belize–Mexico border
World.content:
Mexican motorcyclist Nidia Hernandez killed in collision near Belize–Mexico border

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police have issued notices of intended prosecution following a traffic accident that claimed the life of 31-year-old Mexican national Nidia Hernandez near Belize’s northern border.

The accident occurred at approximately 9 p.m. on Sunday, July 26, 2026, as Hernandez was riding a motorcycle toward the Mexican border.

Investigators say a green Chevrolet was travelling behind Hernandez when she allegedly swerved into the opposite lane and collided with a Dodge Attitude travelling from the direction of Mexico toward Belize.

Hernandez sustained fatal injuries in the collision. Police say urine samples were obtained from the drivers of both motor vehicles as the investigation continues.

World.title: Notice of intended prosecution issued to driver after Tatiana Alvarado’s fatal crash
World.content:
Notice of intended prosecution issued to driver after Tatiana Alvarado’s fatal crash

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police have issued a notice of intended prosecution as investigations continue into the road traffic accident that claimed the life of 39-year-old Tatiana Alvarado of Bella Vista Village.

The collision occurred at approximately 4:35 p.m. on Saturday, July 25, 2026, near the Independence Junction on the Thomas Vincent Ramos Highway.

Police say Alvarado was riding a motorcycle toward Punta Gorda when the driver of a Ford Escape travelling behind her allegedly attempted to overtake. Investigators now allege that Alvarado suddenly turned left during the overtaking manoeuvre, resulting in the collision.

Earlier reports identified the driver of the Ford Escape as 26-year-old Daunte Oliver Eden Noralez of a Belmopan address. Alvarado’s motorcycle caught fire following the collision, and she was pronounced dead after being transported to the Southern Regional Hospital.

Police say the driver has been cooperating with investigators. Authorities have not yet confirmed whether a urine sample was obtained from him.

World.title: Conflict shift
World.content:
Superintendent Mark Harris, commanding officer for the St Andrew Central Police Division, speaks about the division’s changing crime landscape during an episode of the Jamaica Constabulary Force’s Force4Good podcast. x

THE St Andrew Central Police Division, which is the commercial heartbeat of the Corporate Area, where thousands of Jamaicans live and work daily, is confronting a changing crime landscape, with police saying interpersonal and domestic conflicts have become a greater concern than organised gang violence.

Commanding officer for the St Andrew Central Police Division Superintendent Mark Harris said the division has largely brought organised gang activity under control, but is now grappling with murders arising from personal disputes, many of which occur without warning and in communities not traditionally associated with violent crime. He said this shift has presented a more complex policing challenge because, unlike gang conflicts, interpersonal disputes are far less predictable.

Speaking on the Jamaica Constabulary Force’s (JCF) Force4Good podcast, Harris said the division recorded the largest reduction in murders across the Jamaica Constabulary Force last year and even went an entire month without a murder this February. However, he noted that while gang-related killings have declined significantly, police are increasingly being challenged by crimes rooted in personal and domestic disputes.

“Last year, I had gang issues, [but] this year, we don’t have a gang issue, we have criminals committing crimes, but it’s not associated with gangs, like 2024 and part of 2025, and believe it or not, gang conflict is easier to police than the interpersonal and the domestic issues,” he noted.

The St Andrew Central Police Division encompasses some of Jamaica’s busiest commercial, educational and transport hubs, including Half-Way-Tree, New Kingston, Cross Roads and Papine. It is also responsible for policing major national events, entertainment activities and sporting fixtures that are often held at the National Stadium, making it one of the JCF’s most demanding divisions.

The division also includes communities such as August Town and Nannyville, both of which have experienced persistent gang activity and periodic security operations over the years. August Town was placed under a Zone of Special Operations in 2020 following years of deadly gang violence, while Nannyville has repeatedly featured in anti-gang and anti-gun operations as police sought to dismantle organised criminal networks operating across Kingston and St Andrew.

Despite that history, Harris said the division’s greatest challenge is no longer organised gangs but the rise in deadly interpersonal conflicts.

“We know where the gangs are and where they operate and who they’re in conflict with, and we put police right there…but for the interpersonal things, even in Jack’s Hill we have murders [and] that is not normally a place where we have murders… and these are interpersonal, rather than gang conflict,” he explained.

He said the division is relying not only on intelligence-led operations but also stronger community partnerships to prevent personal disputes from escalating into violence.

“We go out there and do the hard policing, we still have our community engagement. We had to do those meetings at the Transport Centre to speak to students and parents and stakeholders,” Harris noted.

Meanwhile, Area Four Commander Assistant Commissioner of Police Michael Phipps said St Andrew Central remains critical to crime management across Kingston and St Andrew because of its concentration of commercial activity, major institutions and daily commuter traffic.

He noted that the division has also experienced a significant number of fatal attacks involving weapons other than firearms, reflecting the growing challenge posed by interpersonal violence.

“I can tell you here and now that St Andrew Central has had a very high number of murders resulting from the use of knives and other blunt-force trauma injuries that have resulted in death. So we see St Andrew Central as one of the most important divisions if we are to maintain control of crime across Area Four,” Phipps said.

World.title: Upper St Andrew residents ready to protest
World.content:
The residents of Kingston 8 claim that a lot of the problems they face stem from an increase in large real estate projects in the area, as when projects are being executed, roads are dug up and not repaired properly. (Photo: Naphtali Junior)

SOME residents of upper St Andrew have threatened to take up placards to protest poor road infrastructure and unrestricted real estate developments, as they say they are tired of their cries falling on deaf ears.

The Jamaica Observer was taken on a tour of Waterworks Road and adjoining thoroughfares in Kingston 8, starting from the Manor Park area, where various roadways that were recently patched have already started disintegrating.

The residents claim that a lot of the problems they face stem from an increase in large real estate projects in the area, as when projects are being executed, roads are dug up and not repaired properly. They also suspect that unregulated construction is a main factor in roads being damaged frequently even after being fixed.

“We are planning a protest, if nothing happens,” one resident threatened.

That resident, who withheld his name, pointed to a spot where water was spouting through a break in the asphalt on Waterworks Road. “They don’t use shingles or anything like that when they are fixing the roads, so the road is being eaten out from underneath,” he said.

As it relates to apartment projects being undertaken in the area, the resident said the road infrastructure can’t support the developments.

Pointing to premises on Waterworks Road where heavy-duty trucks used in construction were parked, the resident said the community has no idea what the plans for the location are, and is opposed to any more major construction projects at this time. Attempts have been made by members of the community to acquire information from the authorities about the developers’ plans, but they have hit a roadblock, having been told by authorities that they can get a copy of the documents in 60 days. However, this time frame poses a problem for the residents who said they are aware that under the law, they have a limited period in which to file an objection to any proposed construction projects.

In a letter recently penned by residents, which the

Observer saw, the residents said, “For nearly two years, residents of Broadway Close, Broadway Road, Sharrow Drive, and Waterworks Road in Kingston 8 have endured a slow-motion disaster. A developer dug up their roads to lay sewer pipes, left the reinstatement in a dangerously substandard condition, and vanished — while the authorities responsible for enforcing the law have failed to act. The result is that a car recently hit a sinkhole in a patched section and got stuck. Inferior patching work has crumbled under the weight of daily traffic. And residents are left asking a question that echoes across Jamaica: why are the laws on the books not being enforced?”

It continued: “The Parochial Roads Act gives the Kingston and St Andrew Municipal Corporation (KSAMC) clear and unequivocal authority over parochial roads like Broadway Road and Waterworks Road. It requires any developer digging up a public road to obtain a road-opening permit and provide a refundable security deposit — money held by the KSAMC to ensure that if the developer fails to properly restore the road, the corporation can do the job using those funds,” the letter stated.

“…On Broadway Road and Waterworks Road, the developer dug up the roads, laid pipes, and left behind inferior patching that has deteriorated into sinkholes and dangerous driving conditions. The KSAMC’s preliminary finding, confirmed by Member of Parliament for the area Delano Seiveright, is clear.

“But where is the accountability? If [a security deposit] was obtained [from the developer], why hasn’t it been used to fix the roads? If none was obtained, why was the developer allowed to dig up public roads without providing the required guarantee?“

Seiveright, meanwhile, said he shared the frustration of residents, stating that their concerns are legitimate and that he has been lobbying on their behalf for a remedy.

“It is important to note that the Waterworks issue pre-dates my election as Member of Parliament [for St Andrew North Central],“ he pointed out. ”Since taking office, I have met repeatedly with officials at the highest levels of the Ministry of Water, the National Water Commission (NWC), KSAMC, and the National Environment and Planning Agency, carried out several site visits and technical walk-throughs, and spoken directly with many affected residents. I also escalated the matter to Minister [of Water] Matthew Samuda.“

He said the situation in Waterworks centres on corrective works following a private developer’s sewer project in the area. He added that while the developer is at the heart of this debacle, he is pleased that KSAMC and the NWC are now working assiduously to deliver a proper resolution.

Seiveright said his advocacy has also helped to prompt a broader review of how these projects are supervised, with stronger oversight and policy improvements now being actively pursued.

“I am aware of similar issues in other communities. More broadly, residents have raised concerns about overdevelopment, infrastructure capacity and protecting community character. I share those concerns. Development must be responsible, properly planned and supported by adequate infrastructure. I have consistently conveyed residents’ views to the relevant authorities and have encouraged stronger community organisation,“ he explained.

“The Orange Grove/Bridgemount Citizens’ Association is an excellent example of the kind of united, constructive leadership that helps communities achieve results. I will continue to press vigorously for better communication with residents, stronger enforcement where necessary, and practical solutions that protect both our communities and their quality of life,” he said.

World.title: Saint International’s Fashion Face of the Caribbean set for August 29
World.content:
From left: Deiwight Peters, founder, CEO of Saint International; model Kai Newman; Member of Parliament for St Andrew Eastern and Minister of Finance Fayval Williams, and Saint International model Carolyn Sangster.Samuel Edie

For 26 years Saint International has been the leading model agency across the region, unearthing new talent each year who have gone on to achieve success on the international fashion scene.

A new set of model hopefuls are poised for international success after more than 30 were selected on Sunday, July 26 during a Saint International Community Model Search, which took place at Jamaica College.

This was the fifth model search to have taken place this year and, according to Saint International boss Deiwight Peters, this one was the biggest thus far.

“This model search is the last in the series, and we’ve had five so far. I do believe this was the biggest one; not only in terms of the size of the turnout, but certainly the faces that turned out, they were remarkable. I do feel strongly that on August 29, when we have the finals of the Fashion Face of the Caribbean competition (for both male and female), several of these new discoveries will go on to bigger things,” Peters told the Jamaica Observer shortly after the model search ended.

“We have several top agencies who will be coming in for the event, who are representing the major fashion markets in New York, London, Milan, Paris, Germany, and even Spain and they are just excited to be coming to Jamaica,” shared Peters.

Member of Parliament for St Andrew Eastern and Minister of Finance and the Public Service Fayval Williams, who was in attendance at the model search, heaped praises on Peters.

“Well, I was impressed to see the young people come out for the model search because I know there is still talent all over Jamaica. Deiwight is a very reputable person, his agency has an impressive track record, and I have no doubt that several of these model hopefuls here today will become stars of tomorrow under Deiwight’s guidance,” Williams told the Observer.

Peters shared that the minister’s presence validated the work that the agency has been doing over the years.

“I think that her turning up validated what we do and the purpose of the model search. She knows the success stories of Saint International. A big thank you to the Jamaica College family for hosting us, Mr Wayne Robinson, the principal, and the team,” he said.

Kai Newman, one of Saint International’s successful models, was in attendance at the model search to encourage the newbies.

“I just flew back to Jamaica so I said why not come here and meet some of the future stars and give them some advice, a little inspiration, and motivation. I just want them to believe in Deiwight, believe in Saint International, and to just be their authentic self,” Newman, who was discovered by Peters the age of 14 while walking on the street.

Newman has walked for designers including Burberry, Tommy Hilfiger, Chanel, Gucci, Calvin Klein, Prada, Bottega, among others.

Speaking on the Fashion Face of the Caribbean competition in August, Peters shared that more than 150 models from Jamaica, Canada, United States, Europe, several Caribbean countries including Guyana, will participate.

“We have roughly 150 models who will be participating in the Fashion Face of the Caribbean and they are coming from all over the world. It’s going to be awesome,” he said.

World.title: ‘Thrilled’ 76ers confirm James signing, eye NBA title run
World.content:
Lebron James Photo: AFP

NEW YORK, United States (AFP) — LeBron James has signed a contract to play for the Philadelphia 76ers, the team announced Monday, with managing owner Josh Harris “thrilled” about chances for their first NBA title since 1983.

James announced on Friday he would play for the Sixers on a two-year deal worth US$8 million, ending a weeks-long mystery over the 41-year-old superstar’s future, but the 76ers had no comment throughout the weekend.

“I am thrilled to welcome LeBron James to the Philadelphia 76ers,” ownership managing partner Harris said in a statement. “One of the greatest players in NBA history and one of the best athletes ever, his accomplishments are iconic.”

James, the NBA’s all-time scoring leader set to begin his record 24th campaign in October, is a four-time NBA champion and four-time NBA Most Valuable Player.

After winning two titles with Miami, another with hometown club Cleveland and his most recent with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2020, James could become the first NBA player to win crowns with four different teams.

James, a three-time Olympic champion and 22-time NBA All-Star, joins a Sixers roster filled with NBA stars in hopes of bringing Philadelphia an NBA title for the first time since Julius Erving led the club to the crown 43 years ago.

“I cannot wait to see LeBron alongside Jaylen Brown, VJ Edgecombe, Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, and our talented roster as we work to deliver a championship for Philly,” Harris said.

“To LeBron and his family: we are grateful you chose the 76ers, and look forward to this next chapter of your legendary career. Welcome to the 76ers!”

James has career averages of 26.8 points, 7.5 rebounds, 7.4 assists and 1.5 steals over 1,622 games.

Philadelphia 76ers president of basketball operations Mike Gansey, an Ohio high school rival of James on the court, expects the legend will boost the club and the community.

“There’s no doubt LeBron is one of the greatest players to ever play the game of basketball and there are no words to measure the impact he’ll have on this organisation,” Gansey said.

“I’ve had the pleasure of knowing LeBron since high school and have seen the high-level impact he has produced at every stop of his basketball journey. He is a consummate professional, the ultimate competitor, and a tireless worker.

“But he’s also an incredible person with natural leadership traits, a family man, and someone who possesses unwavering commitment to community and those around him. We couldn’t be happier that he’s officially here.”

The 76ers posted a photo on social media of a James jersey, keeping his tradition number 23 with his new club, hanging in a locker with a crown on a shelf inside it, a nod toward “King James” being with the Sixers.

James has taken teams into the NBA play-offs 19 times, matching a league record, with post-season averages of 28.2 points, 8.9 rebounds, 7.2 assists, 1.7 steals and 1.0 blocked shots over 302 games.

In June, James announced he was leaving the Lakers and numerous clubs were seen as contenders to become his new home, including Miami, Cleveland, Golden State and Minnesota as well as the 76ers.

Philadelphia swung a deal with Boston three weeks ago for Brown, sending Paul George to the Celtics, and together with centre Embiid and top guards Maxey and Edgecombe they provided a line-up too good for James to pass up in his quest for a fifth NBA title.

“I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energise a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time,” James posted on X Friday.

World.title: DOUBLE JOY!
World.content:
DEMARIO Prince says a talk with his coach after the first round got his mind back where it was supposed to be, leading him to win the gold medal in the 110m hurdles on Monday’s first day of track and field at the Commonwealth Games at Scotstoun Stadium in Glasgow, Scotland.

Jamaica won two gold medals on the day as, minutes before Prince’s run, Romaine Beckford won the men’s high jump. Beckford’s leap to clear 2.25m brought Jamaica’s second gold in the event at the games and first in 68 years.

Prince, the fourth-straight Jamaican and fifth in the last six editions to win the 110m gold medal, ran 13.17 seconds (0.4m/s) to claim his first major global medal.

Prince, who was fourth in the 60m hurdles at the World Athletics Indoor Championships in March, was delighted with the win. “This means a lot. You know, that was the aim coming into the Commonwealth Games. You know, just to get the gold medal, do it for myself, my family, and the fans. So yeah, I’m very, very pleased, very happy with the win,” Prince told the Jamaica Observer.

The sprint hurdler said he believes this is the start of good things to come.

“I feel like I can still give more and still wrap up more gold medals,” he said, noting that he had not been happy with his first round race in which he placed second.

“I was more confident going into the final, I just had to go back in the mindset to know that I can go out there and execute as I was not pleased with the prelims. I spoke to coach Ben (Dalton) and he told me not to worry about anything, he told me that I can do this. It is a regular thing for me to go out and execute and go get the medal for Jamaica,” Prince said.

England’s Samuel Bennett ran a personal best 13.30 for the silver medal and Milan Trajkvoc clocked a season’s best 12.32 to deliver Cyprus’ first medal in the event. Jamaica’s Jerome Campbell was sixth in 13.86.

Beckford, who was eighth in 2022 and failed to clear the first height at last year’s World Athletics Championships, became the first Jamaican man to win the event since 1958 when Ernle Haisley set a then Commonwealth Games record 2.06m to capture gold.

India’s Sarvesh Anil Kushare, who also cleared 2.25m, took the silver medal. England’s NCAA champion Kimani Jack was third with 2.20m.

Two-time World Indoor bronze medallist Raymond Richards just missed a medal, placing fourth also with 2.20m.

Jamaica will hope to add more medals today with athletes qualified for several finals, including in the men’s and women’s 100m.

Women’s high jump defending champion Lamara Distin, former men’s 400m world champion Antonio Watson and 800m national champion Navasky Anderson are among those set to their first entry at the 2026 Commonwealth Games.

Former national champion Rohan Watson advanced to Tuesday’s semi-final of the men’s 100m after he won his first round race in 10.13 (1.5m/s).

In the semi-final he is to be joined by Ackeem Blake who drew a bye.

Also advancing were the Ghanaian pair of Benjamin Azamati and Abdul-Rasheed Saminu, as well as Jeremiah Azu of Wales and Favour Ashe of Nigeria.

Both Jamaican entries in the female 100m, Jonielle Smith and Jodean Williams, both of whom had byes, will join the action in the semi-finals.

Former World Athletics champion Tajay Gayle led the qualifying for Wednesday’s final of the men’s long jump with 8.10m (0.1m/s). He is to be joined by Jordan Turner who had a wind-aided 7.84m (4.2m/s).

Gayle, who have won medals at the last two major global championships, had a wind-aided 7.73m (3.3m/s) and 7.40m (1.0m/s) before his big mark.

Turner was was third in his group, behind Indian Sreeshankar’s effort of 8.01m (2.0m/s) and Australian Christopher Mitrevski’s mark of 7.89m (1.8m/s).

National champion Kelly Ann Beckford (2:01.63 minutes) and Adelle Tracey (2:02.58) advanced to Wednesday’s semi-finals of the women’s 800m.

Beckford booked an automatic spot after placing third in her first-round heat behind pre-championships favourite Lillian Odira of Kenya who ran 2:01.05. Isabelle Boffey of Wales clocked 2:01.53.

Tracey advanced on time after she was fourth in her first round race, just outside the automatic qualifying places. Australia’s Sarah Billings won with 2:01.51, followed by Botswana’s Oratile Nowe (2:02.11) and Kenya’s Janet Jepkemoi (2:02.30).

Nayoka Clunis qualified for Tuesday’s women’s hammer throw final, her first major global final. She threw 64.84m in the third round, eighth best of the day.

Distin could be pushed hard in her title defence with the likes of the in-form Australian pair of Eleanor Patterson and Nicola Olyslagers, as well as former NCAA champion Temitope Simbiat Adeshina of Nigeria all ranked ahead of her going into the championships.

The Sweden-based Distin has had a season’s best 1.96m, set indoors in February and has cleared 1.94m outdoors.

Navasky Anderson will be hoping to get back to the final of the men’s 800m after he finished fifth four years ago in Birmingham, England.

Since shocking the track and field world with his gold medal in the men’s 400m in Hungary in 2023, Watson has been through some lean years, failing to get past the semis in Tokyo, Japan, last year. But he has been improving through this season.

Watson will be accompanied by Delano Kennedy and Zandrion Barnes as they seek places in the men’s 400m semi-finals.

Leah Anderson and Shana Kaye Anderson are to line up in the women’s 400m first round.

World.title: Wedding Content Creators
World.content:
A wedding content creator documents your day as it unfolds, using a smartphone to capture raw, candid moments.

Not long ago, every wedding media team consisted of a photographer and videographer. Today, there’s a new professional joining the line-up — the wedding content creator.

If you’ve spent any time on Instagram or TikTok, you’ve probably seen the rise of behind-the-scenes wedding clips, emotional first looks, candid bridal party moments, and beautifully edited reels appearing within hours of the celebration. That’s the work of a wedding content creator.

This person is responsible for capturing authentic, real-time moments throughout the day, usually using a smartphone. The focus isn’t producing a cinematic wedding film or a gallery of professionally edited images. Instead, the wedding content creator documents the experience as it unfolds, creating vertical videos, candid clips, and social-ready content that couples can relive and share almost immediately.

So how are they different from a videographer? A videographer tells the story of your wedding through carefully planned shots, professional cameras, audio equipment, lighting, and expert editing. The result is a timeless wedding film that beautifully documents your ceremony, speeches, and celebration.

A content creator, on the other hand, captures the moments in-between — the laughter while getting ready, your mother’s emotional reaction as she helps you into your dress, the bridesmaids dancing in the suite, your guests’ excitement before the ceremony, or your partner’s nervous smile just before walking down the aisle. These are often the unscripted moments that couples cherish most because they reflect how the day actually felt.

Each has its advantages. A videographer delivers polished, high-quality storytelling that you’ll treasure for decades. The downside is that editing takes time, so your finished film may not arrive for several weeks or even months.

A content creator provides immediate gratification. Many deliver raw footage within 24 hours and edited reels shortly after, allowing couples to relive their day while the emotions are still fresh. However, smartphone footage is not intended to replace the production quality of professional videography.

If your budget allows, having both is the ideal combination.

The videographer preserves your wedding as a timeless film, while the content creator documents the emotion, spontaneity, and behind-the-scenes memories that often never make it into the final edit. Together, they create a complete story — one that is beautifully produced and deeply personal.

If you must choose one, let your priorities guide the decision. If preserving your vows, speeches, and ceremony in cinematic quality is more important, invest in a professional videographer. If you value candid moments, quick delivery, and social-media-ready memories, a content creator may be the better fit.

Whichever you choose, remember that great wedding content isn’t about following trends or chasing viral moments. The best professionals take the time to understand your personalities, your priorities, and the atmosphere you want to create. They know when to step in for a memorable shot and, just as importantly, when to step back and quietly capture the genuine interactions unfolding around them.

Because the most meaningful wedding memories aren’t always the ones you planned. They’re the fleeting glances, unexpected laughter, happy tears, and quiet moments that happen in-between.

At the end of the day, strong wedding content isn’t simply about documenting what happened, it’s about preserving how your wedding day felt — and that’s a memory worth investing in.

World.title: Public Advisory: Fraudulent Website Alert
World.content:
Jamaica Observer Limited is advising the public of an unauthorised and deceptive website that is unlawfully using our name, logo, and other brand elements to imitate our official platform and mislead individuals.

We are aware that a fabricated article is being circulated on social media claiming to originate from the Jamaica Observer.

The article references former Cabinet minister Lisa Hanna and a purported investment platform, and it improperly uses the image and likeness of the public figure, purporting to create the appearance of an endorsement or affiliation with the platform described in the article. No such article was published by the Jamaica Observer, and no such association exists.

These claims are entirely false. The website and related social media posts are fraudulent and have no connection to the Jamaica Observer. Such platforms may attempt to collect personal information, solicit payments, or otherwise misrepresent our services. We urge the public to remain vigilant and ensure they are engaging only with our legitimate channels.

How to Protect Yourself

• Access our official website only: https://www.jamaicaobserver.com/

• Follow our verified social media accounts: https://www.instagram.com/jamaicaobserver/; https://x.com/JamaicaObserver; https://www.youtube.com/@JamaicaObserverJa

• Be cautious of pages or profiles requesting personal information, payments, or unusual engagement

• Report suspicious websites or accounts to the relevant platform and notify us at abuse@jamaicaobserver.com

Jamaica Observer takes the misuse of our brand and intellectual property seriously. We are actively collaborating with the appropriate authorities and digital platforms to remove these fraudulent pages and safeguard the public.

World.title: Charleroi airport to halt flights in 2028 for over 2 months
World.content:
Brussels South Charleroi Airport , pictured here in March, 2023, is set to be closed for 11 weeks. | Virginie Lefour/Belga Mag/AFP via Getty Images

The suspension is necessary to allow major reconstruction works on the hub’s only runway.

BRUSSELS — Brussels South Charleroi Airport will suspend all flight operations in the second half of 2028 to allow a major reconstruction of its only runway and other infrastructure upgrades.

Belgium's second-busiest airport is expected to halt air traffic for 11 weeks, from Aug. 15 to Oct. 31.

“A complete refurbishment of Charleroi airport's sole runway (which has an estimated lifespan of 25 years), together with other major infrastructure modernisation works, has been scheduled by [airport infrastructure company] SOWAER for the second half of 2028,” the airport said in an email.

World.title: UK Green leader reported to police over Farage guillotine post
World.content:
In a statement, Zia Yusuf, Reform UK’s home affairs spokesperson, said: “Zack Polanski has posted to his 713k Instagram followers a photo of a man in a T-shirt depicting the beheading of Nigel Farage.

“To do this just 2 weeks after our friend Ann was murdered is staggering. This is incitement to murder. It should be treated as such by the police,” he said.

Ann Widdecombe, a former Tory minister who was Reform UK’s justice spokesperson, was found dead in her home in Devon earlier this month. Joshua Kerry, a 28-year-old man, was charged with her murder last week.

Sharing a screenshot, Nigel Farage wrote on X: “If I was to post anything as inciteful then I would expect to be arrested, and so should Polanski.”

A Green spokesperson said: “Zack condemns the image on the T-shirt. He was tagged in a post with 20 images and clicked accept without realizing there was more to it than he had seen.”

The spokesperson added that the t-shirt is in poor taste, and said the Greens call on everyone involved in public discourse “to show kindness and not encourage more division.”

The Met Police said Monday they had received a third-party report relating to an image shared on social media.

“We take reports of this nature extremely seriously, and officers are conducting enquiries into the matter.”

World.title: US kicks off review of its force posture in Europe
World.content:
U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth arrives to welcome defense ministers from the Baltic states at the Pentagon on July 25, 2025. | Win McNamee/Getty Images

The six-month review was first announced by U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in June during a NATO ministerial meeting.

The United States on Tuesday launched the country's Europe posture review that will determine the number of American troops and military assets on the continent, a top U.S. defense official said.

"This will be a real review, designed to ensure that NATO is moving fast and irreversibly toward Europe taking primary responsibility for its conventional defense," U.S. Undersecretary for Defense Elbridge Colby posted on X.

The six-month review was first announced by U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in June during a NATO ministerial meeting.

World.title: Can Europe fight fires this big?
World.content:
Wildfires raging across France and Spain have forced more than 300,000 people from their homes and stretched national firefighting services to their limits. Zoya Sheftalovich and Ian Wishart look at how the EU is helping through its Civil Protection Mechanism and rescEU emergency reserve — and why Brussels says that even dozens more firefighting planes would not be enough without much greater investment in prevention.

Then, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy heads to Washington amid signs that U.S. President Donald Trump and parts of the MAGA movement may be warming towards Kyiv. But will the apparent change of heart translate into sanctions against Russia and concrete military support?

Plus: Could antibodies produced by llamas provide farmers with a safer alternative to chemical pesticides?

World.title: Polanski’s Greens brace for the ‘Burnham bounce’
World.content:
An opinion poll by More in Common published Monday put Labour on top for the first time since March 2025, with its surge coming at the expense of the Greens, who recorded their lowest share of the vote since October last year when Polanski became leader. A separate YouGov poll also released Monday showed no change from last week, though it noted the party is down eight points from a February peak.

Polanski insists he is the “opposite of worried about Andy Burnham,” predicting Labour MPs’ “last roll of the dice” in switching leader won’t improve things.

But a senior Green Party local politician, granted anonymity to speak frankly, acknowledged: “It’s going to be difficult, there is going to be a Burnham bounce,” warning the party needs to “sharpen those key lines that give us differentiation.”

The party is already attacking Burnham for employing corporate lobbyists like his chief of staff James Purnell, and claiming the new prime minister’s rhetoric on Gaza, public ownership and homelessness is hollow, and does not represent a change from Starmer.

It is also on a drive to find more polished spokespeople to hit the airwaves.

Drawing the battle lines

One area where the Greens see a dividing line with Burnham is over Gaza.

World.title: Spain’s biggest blaze risks scorching conservatives ahead of key election year
World.content:
At a national level, the PP is still topping the polls and is on track to take power in 2027, profiting from the web of corruption scandals ensnaring Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's ruling Socialist Party.

But the fires threaten to expose vulnerabilities. The conservatives are not only being criticized for failing to invest in firefighters, but also risk looking out of step with the severity of the challenge posed by climate change, in part thanks to regional alliances with the far-right Vox party that are steering the PP toward increasingly anti-ecological positions.

Madrid Regional President Isabel Díaz Ayuso, a conservative heavyweight, has felt the sting of public anger over her political priorities. On Sunday, she said she'd come under fire from constituents accusing her of prioritizing investment in fighting bulls — a vote winner with a right-wing base — rather than firefighters.

From left: Madrid Regional President Isabel Díaz Ayuso, Villamanta Mayor Mariano Núñez Muñoz, King Felipe VI, Queen Letizia and Lt. Gen. Francisco Javier Marcos. They are pictured visiting wildfire evacuees on July 26, 2026. | Javier Soriano/AFP via Getty Images

"In two or three municipalities, they were talking about bullfighters," a palpably irritated Ayuso complained. “What do bullfighters have to do with all this?”

The populist Madrid president accused her political opponents of stirring up grievances to “divide” her constituents, adding that the bullfighting sector had been especially impacted by the wildfires. “We must remember that they are the first ones who have lost livestock and land,” she added.

But political opponents like Manuela Bergerot, spokesperson for the left-wing Más Madrid party, argued that once the fires are extinguished, it would be time to probe "the precarious situation of firefighters, cuts in prevention and climate change denial."

World.title: Japan: Strong earthquake hits Kumamoto, many deaths feared
World.content:
Dozens of people were hospitalized after the earthquake hit southern Japan. According to media reports, many deaths are feared after a shopping mall partially collapsed in Kahima Town.

A powerful 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck Kumamoto Prefecture on Japan's southern island of Kyushu on Tuesday afternoon, triggering emergency warnings and prompting authorities to assess the extent of the damage.

Japan's public broadcaster, NHK, reported that "many people" were trapped inside an Aeon shopping mall damaged by the earthquake. Earlier, local police reported an explosion at the mall in Kashima Town.

According to local broadcaster TBS, police said "quite a few" were presumed dead in the incident.

Meanwhile, NHK reported that at least 50 people were hospitalized after the earthquake.

Authorities assess damage as tsunami threat eases

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi also said initial reports indicated multiple injuries, damage to civilian infrastructure, and fires in several affected areas.

"We are still assessing the extent of injuries and property damage, but I have been informed that there have already been several injuries," Takaichi said.

"Power outages and fires are happening in some areas, and roads and bridges have been damaged and buildings collapsed," she added.

Although the earthquake caused widespread disruption and temporarily raised fears of a tsunami, officials later confirmed that the threat had subsided and that Japan's coastline was no longer in danger.

"This earthquake occurred inland, and no tsunami activity has been observed so far," a spokesperson for the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) said. "For this reason, we hope to lift the tsunami advisory at a relatively early stage, depending on future sea level conditions."

The earthquake struck at 4:27 p.m. local time and registered the highest possible level of seven on Japan's Shindo intensity scale, which measures ground shaking Image: Kyodo/REUTERS

Power and nuclear facilities remain safe

Japan's Nuclear Regulation Authority reported that no abnormalities were detected at three nearby nuclear power plants, providing reassurance in a country still sensitive to nuclear safety concerns following the 2011 Fukushima disaster.

However, the earthquake disrupted electricity supplies across the region. According to Kyushu Electric Power, approximately 45,000 households and facilities in Kumamoto temporarily lost power following the tremor.

Several major industrial facilities are located near the earthquake zone, including operations belonging to Sony and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), the world's largest contract chipmaker. Sony stated that it was evaluating conditions at its facilities, while TSMC did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Japan's long history of major earthquakes

Kumamoto is no stranger to devastating seismic events.

In 2016, the region was struck by two major earthquakes, first a magnitude 6.5 quake and then a magnitude 7.3 tremor two days later. The disaster claimed 273 lives, injured more than 2,800 people. Thousands of buildings were either damaged or destroyed, making it one of Japan's most destructive recent earthquake disasters.

More recently, a magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck northern Japan on June 25, causing little damage and no fatalities. Earlier this year, on April 20, a magnitude 7.7 earthquake in northern Japan injured at least ten people and shook high-rise buildings as far away as Tokyo, prompting authorities to issue a temporary advisory warning of an increased risk of even stronger earthquakes. That advisory was lifted a week later.

One of the world's most earthquake-prone nations

Japan sits along the western edge of the Pacific "Ring of Fire," one of the most active seismic zones on Earth where four major tectonic plates meet.

Home to approximately 125 million people, the country experiences hundreds of earthquakes every year and accounts for roughly 18% of the world's seismic activity.

While most tremors are relatively minor, Japan remains haunted by memories of the catastrophic magnitude 9.0 earthquake and tsunami that struck the country's northeast coast in March 2011. The disaster killed or left missing around 18,500 people and triggered the Fukushima nuclear crisis.

Tuesday's earthquake demonstrated the country's preparedness systems, emergency response capabilities, and monitoring of critical infrastructure. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi office also posted a safety guideline on X, assuring that their safety remains their top priority.

As authorities continue to assess the impact of the Kumamoto quake, residents are being urged to stay alert for potential aftershocks and follow official safety guidance.

World.title: Will Pakistan intervene amid Houthi attacks on Saudi ships?
World.content:
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia are strategic defense partners, but experts say there are limits to how far Islamabad can go in opposing Iran-backed Houthis.

Pakistan condemned attacks on Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea by Iran-backed Yemeni Houthi militia last week as the conflict in the Middle East threatens to expand.

In a statement, the Pakistani Foreign Ministry warned that any Houthi threat to Pakistani maritime interests in the Red Sea could be met with the "lawful use of force."

Pakistan enjoys a trade and security relationship with Saudi Arabia, and Pakistani-flagged vessels frequent Saudi ports in the Red Sea. Last September, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed a mutual defense agreement that contains a "collective security" clause, meaning attack on one country is considered an attack on both.

After the Houthis launched missiles at southern Saudi Arabia last week, Pakistan's Foreign Ministry expressed its "unwavering commitment" to the security pact.

At the same time, Pakistan also has ties with Iran, and has been a key mediator between Tehran and Washington to end the Iran war.

Any military act against the Iran-backed Houthis could place Islamabad in one of the most complicated foreign policy situations it has faced in years.

Houthis claim attacks on Saudi tankers in Red Sea To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Pakistan's tightrope between Saudis and Iran

Historically, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan have long shared close military and strategic relations. Pakistani military generals and advisers have aided the Kingdom for decades.

Farea Al-Muslimi, a Yemen expert at London-based think tank Chatham House, told DW that Pakistani troops are already inside Yemen in support of the Saudis, "carrying out security and training-related duties alongside Saudi forces." A Pakistani official DW spoke to categorically denied this claim.

Nevertheless, if Houthi attacks on oil tankers and commercial shipping escalate in the Red Sea, Saudi Arabia could turn to Pakistan for help.

"Pakistan is one of Riyadh's closest defense partners, and their mutual defense pact makes such a request plausible. Having also come under Iranian attack, Saudi Arabia may increasingly look to Islamabad for military assistance if it feels under growing security pressure," Michael Kugelman, senior fellow at the Washington-based Atlantic Council, told DW.

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif embrace after signing a defense agreement last September Image: Saudi Press Agency/REUTERS

However, Pakistan's improving ties with Iran and its mediation to end the US-Iran conflict could complicate any Pakistani military role on Saudi Arabia's behalf.

"Pakistan and Iran have a complicated relationship based on the calculation of tactical gains by either side. In any case, Pakistan has warned Iran several times that in case of conflict it will support Saudi Arabia," Ayesha Siddiqa, a Pakistani military analyst and senior fellow at King's College London, told DW.

After a period of unprecedented tensions in 2024, when Iran and Pakistan exchanged cross-border missile strikes, the neighbors have since rebuilt diplomatic relations and strengthened cooperation against militant groups operating along their shared border.

"Limited military support for Saudi Arabia would not necessarily rupture Pakistan's ties with Iran. But at a time when Islamabad is trying to present itself as a neutral mediator, expanding arms support to Riyadh could deepen Tehran's suspicions and undermine Pakistan's diplomatic role," Kugelman said.

How much support can Pakistan give?

If Saudi Arabia seeks assistance, analysts say Pakistan's contribution would most likely focus on protecting Saudi interests rather than joining offensive operations.

"The preference would be for defensive engagement, as expanding operations in the Red Sea may prove too risky," said Siddiqa.

Such an approach could include intelligence sharing, air-defense cooperation, maritime surveillance, and protecting critical Saudi infrastructure, allowing Pakistan to support Riyadh without joining offensive operations.

"Despite its deep military ties and mutual defense pact with Saudi Arabia, Pakistan is unlikely to provide arms or troops. Islamabad is focused on preventing regional escalation and preserving its role as a mediator in the Iran conflict, making any military support for Riyadh politically risky and potentially damaging to its ties with Tehran," said Kugelman.

Iran war: Analyzing the Houthi blockade against Saudi Arabia To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Will Saudi Arabia escalate?

Saudi Arabia has exercised considerable restraint since winding down its large-scale military campaign in Yemen. However, repeated attacks on oil infrastructure and commercial shipping may eventually force Riyadh to respond more aggressively.

"Continued Houthi attacks on Saudi vessels could prompt Riyadh to abandon its restraint and launch a military response," said Al-Muslimi.

King's College analyst Siddiqa said it is not clear that Saudi Arabia currently has the capacity to fight a prolonged sub-conventional war against the Houthis.

"While it may intensify air strikes, more bombardment alone is unlikely to achieve the objective of making the Kingdom more secure," she said.

The analysts agreed Islamabad will likely back maritime security and freedom of navigation while avoiding direct strikes on Houthi targets amid the looming US-Iran conflict. But if the Red Sea conflict escalates, staying neutral may become increasingly difficult as pressure from Riyadh and Tehran grows.

"The trajectory of the conflict with Iran will shape Saudi Arabia's tolerance for Houthi attacks," said Kugelman.

"If the current pause between the US and Iran holds, Riyadh is likely to wait out the attacks rather than escalate. But Saudi Arabia will continue to view Pakistan as a key security partner because Houthi attacks are unlikely to stop, even if the Iran conflict ends," he added.

World.title: Germany: Online tourist accommodation bookings hit new peak
World.content:
Vacation rental bookings through online platforms have climbed to a new record in Germany. The figures reveal major regional differences in where certain tourists like to go.

Bookings for tourist accommodation in Germany through major online platforms have reached a record high.

The figure rose sharply above both last year's level and figures seen before the COVID-19 pandemic.

Why are tourist rental bookings rising in Germany?

Travellers booked 68.3 million overnight stays through Airbnb, Booking.com and Expedia in 2025, the Federal Statistical Office said on Tuesday, citing data from EU statistics agency Eurostat.

That was an increase of 13% compared with 2024 and more than 83% above the level recorded in 2019.

The rise came despite TripAdvisor no longer being included in the data after it left the short-term accommodation booking market.

Strong domestic demand was the main driver of growth. German travellers booked 48.5 million overnight stays, an increase of more than 15% from the previous year.

The number of domestic bookings has more than doubled since 2019.

Foreign visitors booked 19.8 million overnight stays, almost 8% more than in 2024.

Who is visiting Germany's tourist spots?

Travellers from the Netherlands accounted for the largest number of international bookings, with 2.9 million overnight stays, followed by Poland with 2.1 million and the US with 1.3 million.

Can tourism and nature coexist on Germany's Rügen island? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The figures largely reflect the market for smaller and privately operated accommodation.

Around 94% of booked nights were spent at properties with fewer than 10 beds, which are not included in Germany's official monthly tourism statistics.

The platform data therefore provide a broader picture of the country's short-term accommodation market.

Bavaria recorded the highest number of overnight stays, with 10.6 million. Baden-Württemberg and North Rhine-Westphalia followed with 8.1 million each.

Travel patterns varied considerably between Germany's states.

Around 90% of guests in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Schleswig-Holstein came from within Germany, while city-states and western regions attracted a larger share of international visitors.

Foreign guests accounted for more than two-thirds of bookings in Berlin, at 67.7%.

Their share was also above average in North Rhine-Westphalia, at 42.3%, and Baden-Württemberg, at 40.8%.
