World.title: Study: Underground loan business survives through fear of public shaming
World.content:
Researchers at the University of Tartu have mapped Estonia's social‑media‑based loan market, which operates outside state regulation. The study shows that this uncontrolled market survives thanks to illegal contracts and harsh debt‑collection methods.

When people hear the word "loan shark", many imagine a dark underworld and burly mafiosi with menacing faces. As is typical today, however, the underground loan business has transformed into a very different, digital and more systematized ecosystem that operates completely openly on familiar social‑media platforms.

Kristjan Pulk and Laura Inno from the University of Tartu analyzed posts in Estonian Facebook loan groups and interviewed borrowers, lenders, and debt counselors. As expected, collecting data for the study was difficult, as neither side wanted to talk about their activities. The researchers contacted 125 borrowers, of whom only 12 agreed to speak. Out of 24 lenders, five gave interviews. In addition, they spoke with a handful of debt counselors.

Some of the Estonian‑language private loan groups on Facebook. Source: Screenshot

During the observation period, the loan market was significant — Estonian loan groups had a total of 45,000 members. The largest group had 14,000 members, but only about 25–30 actively offered loans.

Interviews revealed that most people borrow from social media to cover basic needs, because they can no longer get an appointment with a bank. Lenders often justified their activities on ethical grounds, claiming they provide essential funds to those excluded from the official credit system. Other borrowers were attracted by the quick and easy access to credit, even though the average interest rate reached nearly 600 percent. For comparison, Estonia's legally permitted maximum annual percentage rate for consumer loans is 45 percent.

Interviews also showed that a large share of loans go bad. Some lenders have to write off every third loan. In one extreme case, a full 75 percent of borrowers failed to repay their loans.

How does such a risky and illegal market survive? Through thorough background checks and harsh collection methods. Lenders try to assess borrowers' solvency and identity carefully using photos and bank statements, but the system has gaps. The researchers encountered examples of identity theft and cases where loans were issued to people lacking legal capacity.

When a client is late with a payment, lenders do not initiate official proceedings. Instead, they usually post the debtor's photo and private messages publicly to shame them. The fear of this is so great that people agree to pay the demanded sums. Often borrowers are not even aware that they have no legal obligation to pay usurious fees. Lenders themselves avoid going to court, because official intervention would invalidate their contracts and expose the hidden business.

The researchers published their findings in the journal Trends in Organized Crime.

World.title: Iraqi PM arrives in Turkey on an official visit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi arrived in the Turkish capital, Ankara, on Tuesday, for an official visit following an invitation from President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

Al-Zaidi said in a statement on X that his trip to Turkey will focus on investments, water, and development projects, as well as efforts to enhance stability in the region.

World.title: Ukraine rejects Iraqi official’s claims of Ukrainian cell operating in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Ukraine’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Tuesday dismissed statements by Iraq’s National Security Adviser Qasim Al-Aboudi, who claimed that Iraqi authorities had arrested a Ukrainian-linked cell responsible for carrying out attacks inside the country.

In an official statement, the ministry said the allegations were “groundless” and noted that no evidence had been presented to support the claims. It also pointed out that Al-Aboudi himself acknowledged during a televised interview that investigations into the matter were still ongoing.

According to the Ukrainian Foreign Ministry, Iraqi authorities did not communicate any information or concerns through diplomatic channels before the allegations were made publicly.

The ministry said that if Iraqi officials possessed credible evidence, the issue should have been raised through official diplomatic mechanisms rather than announced during a television interview. Instead, Kyiv said it first learned of the accusations through media reports.

Furthermore, Ukraine described the public remarks by a senior Iraqi official as “unacceptable and irresponsible” in the absence of supporting evidence. The ministry stressed that such statements contradict the principles of mutual respect between friendly nations and risk undermining relations between Iraq and Ukraine.

At the same time, Kyiv reaffirmed that it considers Iraq an important partner in the Middle East and remains committed to strengthening political, economic, and humanitarian cooperation between the two countries.

The Foreign Ministry also argued that the allegations mirror Russian propaganda narratives aimed at damaging Ukraine’s international reputation and weakening its partnerships across the Middle East.

Additionally, the statement suggested that the incident could have resulted from external information influence or formed part of a coordinated information campaign intended to disrupt Iraqi-Ukrainian relations.

Ukraine called on Iraqi authorities to address what it described as unfounded allegations and to prevent state institutions from promoting misinformation that could serve the interests of third parties.

The Ukrainian response follows remarks made on Monday by National Security Adviser Qasim Al-Aboudi during an interview on Dijlah TV. Al-Aboudi said Iraqi intelligence had identified what he described as Ukrainian interference inside Iraq and claimed security forces had arrested several individuals who allegedly carried out attacks on Iraqi territory.

He further stated that those detained confessed during questioning to working on behalf of Ukraine. However, Al-Aboudi did not identify the facilities allegedly targeted or specify whether the alleged operations extended beyond Iraq’s borders.

He also acknowledged that investigations into attacks carried out inside Iraq remain complex and require further examination before responsibility can be definitively assigned.

World.title: Iraqi PM expands powers as political deadlock delays cabinet completion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A dispute over Iraq’s remaining vacant cabinet positions has expanded beyond the selection of ministers, with political factions now focusing on the growing authority of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, according to a report published by Al-Mada newspaper.

The debate follows the leak of an official document indicating that Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi has reactivated and expanded the powers of the Commander-in-Chief Office, placing several key security institutions under its supervision while the Ministries of Interior and Defense remain without permanent ministers.

According to Al-Mada, several political sources believe the expanded office significantly increases the prime minister’s direct oversight of Iraq’s security apparatus.

The report says the office now oversees the Ministries of Interior and Defense, the Counter-Terrorism Service, the National Intelligence Service, the National Security Service, the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), border crossings, military industries, and other security-related institutions.

Consequently, some political figures have described the move as a “quiet coup” against Iraq’s post-2003 political framework, arguing that it centralizes authority within the prime minister’s office while reducing the practical influence of future ministers.

Meanwhile, Iraq’s cabinet remains incomplete, with only 14 ministries currently filled while nine ministerial portfolios remain vacant. According to the report, political negotiations have become increasingly complicated, as disagreements now extend beyond candidate names to broader questions of political influence and institutional control.

Sources cited by Al-Mada said the State of Law Coalition has proposed rotating senior security positions as part of efforts to break the deadlock, particularly regarding the Interior Ministry, which traditionally falls under the Shiite political share, while the Defense Ministry is typically allocated to Sunni representatives.

However, negotiations have yet to produce a breakthrough.

At the same time, Al-Mada reported that U.S. objections have become one of the main obstacles preventing completion of the cabinet. Political sources quoted in the report claim Washington opposes appointing individuals affiliated with armed factions to ministerial positions or senior executive offices.

The report says these objections have complicated negotiations among members of the Coordination Framework, with some factions insisting that if their nominees are rejected, similar restrictions should apply to other political parties. As a result, discussions over the remaining cabinet positions have largely stalled.

Political analysts interviewed by Al-Mada argue that the continued delay in appointing ministers has allowed Prime Minister Al-Zaidi greater flexibility in managing state institutions through acting officials and appointments within his office.

According to the report, some political parties fear that prolonging the vacancies could further strengthen the prime minister’s influence over Iraq’s security establishment, making future ministerial appointments less significant.

The report also notes that recent anti-corruption campaigns and shifting political alliances have altered the balance of power within the Coordination Framework, adding another layer of complexity to negotiations.

Supporters of the government, however, argue that the current arrangements are necessary to maintain continuity while negotiations continue.

Officials quoted by Al-Mada said acting appointments and the reactivation of the Commander-in-Chief Office ensure that security institutions continue functioning despite the absence of permanent ministers.

They also expressed confidence that political forces will eventually reach an agreement to complete the cabinet, stressing that Iraq faces significant challenges, including anti-corruption efforts, security reforms, weapons control, and economic pressures linked to oil exports.

Nevertheless, the report suggests that political parties continue to use the vacant ministries as leverage in negotiations with the prime minister, making the timeline for completing the government uncertain.

World.title: US drone shot down in western Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – An unknown drone, first claimed by Iranian official media IRIB as a US surveillance one, crashed within a residential complex near the Haditha Dam in the western Iraqi province of Anbar.

Iraqi police and security agencies later indicated that the drone’s origin remains unknown, according to Al-Jazeera.

The debris was discovered blazing in a residential compound near the Haditha Dam in Anbar.

Local police stated that there were no recorded injuries or civilian deaths as a result of the collision.

Iranian state media swiftly released images of the smoking debris, claiming it was a US drone shot down amid broader regional activity.

The incident took place during a night of broad military conflict in Iraq, which included many drone attacks and defensive responses.

At least four Iranian drones attacked targets northeast of the capital of Iraqi Kurdistan, Erbil, sparking a huge defensive reaction, including over ten US jets and drones sent to inspect the skies.

Air defense systems were activated at Anbar’s Ain al-Asad Air Base in response to a drone strike.

Explosions, alleged suicide drones, and radar interruptions were also reported at Camp Taji, Balad Air Base, and Imam Ali Base in southern Iraq.

The US military has not publicly verified the loss of any aircraft in Anbar. Investigations into the model and operator of the crashed drone are still underway.

World.title: Al Zaidi: Iraq and Turkey can build a regional success story through economic integration
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al Zaidi said on Tuesday that the Middle East needs new success stories built on economic integration rather than conflict, arguing that Iraq and Turkey have the potential to create a model regional partnership through joint investment, infrastructure, and trade.

The remarks came in an article published by Turkey’s Anadolu Agency ahead of Al Zaidi’s official visit to Ankara, where he is expected to meet Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and senior officials.

Al Zaidi said relations between Iraq and Turkey have traditionally focused on managing issues such as security, water resources, trade, and border crossings. However, he argued that regional changes require a more ambitious vision centered on economic cooperation.

He said Iraq has chosen a path of stability, reform, and development, prioritizing a stronger economy, an effective state, and balanced foreign relations that make regional cooperation a pillar of growth.

According to Al Zaidi, Turkey’s industrial base, strategic location, and expertise in infrastructure, energy, and transportation complement Iraq’s geographic position, creating an opportunity to establish one of the region’s most significant economic partnerships.

The prime minister highlighted the Development Road Project, describing it as more than an Iraqi initiative. He said the corridor could redefine economic connectivity in the Middle East by linking Gulf ports with Asian and European markets.

He added that the project would not only reduce shipping times but also create new cities, industrial zones, investment opportunities, and thousands of jobs, while establishing a new economic artery connecting ports to global markets.

Al Zaidi also stressed that security cooperation remains essential, saying Iraq’s and Turkey’s security are closely linked and require mutual respect for sovereignty as well as joint efforts to combat terrorism and organized crime.

On water issues, he said water is no longer simply a technical matter but a development challenge affecting millions of people. He called for a shared approach based on mutual interests, scientific cooperation, and investment in modern technologies to strengthen water and food security.

“The Middle East needs new success stories,” Al Zaidi wrote, adding that Iraq and Turkey can provide one if they move beyond traditional cooperation toward genuine economic integration.

He said every joint investment, factory, transport route, and energy project represents an investment in regional stability, arguing that lasting stability is built through shared projects rather than conflict.

Later on Tuesday, Al Zaidi departed for Ankara at the head of a high-level government delegation. According to the Prime Minister’s Office, the visit will focus on strengthening bilateral cooperation in the fields of economy, water, security, investment, and regional affairs.

The two sides are also expected to review the implementation of existing agreements and memoranda of understanding, while discussing progress on joint infrastructure projects, including the Development Road initiative.

World.title: Drone attack targets Khor Mor gas field in northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Drone attacks targeted the Khor Mor gas field in the northern Iraqi province of Sulaymaniyah in the early hours of Tuesday.

The attack on the field, which is Iraq’s largest gas field with reserves estimated at 8.2 trillion cubic feet, was part of a coordinated wave of suspected Iranian drone attacks against the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

Iranian official media reported an attack on the gas field, which is operated by the UAE-based Pearl Consortium that includes Dana Gas and Crescent Petroleum.

The gas field supplies the majority of the electricity in Iraqi Kurdistan.

According to reports, the strikes were carried out by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), which targets Iranian Kurdish resistance groups and US interests in the region.

A few days ago, Iraqi Kurdistan’s Prime Minister Masoud Barzani stated that repeated security threats and drone attacks had caused energy companies to cut domestic output, seriously affecting the region’s electrical infrastructure.

The escalation takes place amid significant geopolitical challenges. On Monday, US President Donald Trump said he was ready to resume military action against Iran if diplomatic efforts to reach a nuclear deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz failed.

Trump stated that he has temporarily stopped military strikes against Iran to give negotiations a chance to work.

World.title: Iraq, Australia cooperate to sentence alleged drug trafficker to life imprisonment
World.content:
An Iraqi court has sentenced convicted drug trafficker Kazem Hamad to life imprisonment after finding him guilty of drug trafficking and links to transnational organized crime, in a case that involved close cooperation between Iraqi and Australian authorities.

The ruling marks a significant development in Iraq’s ongoing campaign against organized crime and narcotics trafficking.

In a statement issued on Monday, Iraq’s judiciary described Hamad as “one of the most wanted individuals by Iraqi and international courts.” According to the judiciary, Hamad was responsible for smuggling large quantities of heroin into both Iraq and Australia.

The statement also accused him of involvement with transnational criminal networks engaged in drug trafficking, money laundering, murder, kidnapping, extortion, and organized violence.

Australian authorities have identified Hamad as a key figure in Melbourne’s so-called “tobacco wars,” a violent conflict between organized crime groups competing for control of the illicit tobacco and vape market.

The turf war has been linked to more than 200 arson attacks, firebombings, and extortion incidents across the Australian city. Hamad was deported from Australia in 2023 and was arrested in Iraq in January 2026, where prosecutors charged him with smuggling narcotics into both countries.

The Australian Federal Police (AFP) confirmed earlier this year that it had provided operational information to support Iraq’s investigation. AFP Commissioner Krissy Barrett said in February that the agency would continue cooperating with Iraqi authorities while pursuing its own investigation into Hamad and his alleged criminal network under Operation Carmen.

Australian investigators have also linked Hamad to several serious crimes, including allegations that he played a role in the December 2024 firebombing of Melbourne’s Adass Israel Synagogue, according to Australian media reports.

The life sentence comes as Iraq continues to intensify its fight against drug trafficking and organized crime. Despite imposing some of the region’s toughest penalties, including life imprisonment and the death penalty for major narcotics offenses, Iraq has experienced a sharp rise in drug trafficking and addiction since 2003.

Officials say authorities have arrested thousands of suspects in recent years as part of nationwide anti-drug operations. Iraq was recently ranked third globally in combating narcotics at the World Police Summit in the United Arab Emirates, reflecting the country’s expanding efforts to dismantle trafficking networks.

World.title: Iraq’s trade exchange with Saudi Arabia hits $1.7 billion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Saudi General Authority for Statistics revealed on Monday that the volume of trade exchange between Iraq and Saudi Arabia reached approximately $1.7 billion during 2025.

The volume reflects the continued growth of trade relations between the two countries, with Saudi Arabia achieving a considerable trade surplus, local news outlet Shafaq News reported.

The authority said in a statement that the Saudi exports to Iraq totaled around $1.66 billion, with cereal- or flour-based products accounting for $237 million, electrical appliances and equipment standing at $221 million, and aluminum and its products totaling $160 million.

Iraqi exports to Saudi Arabia were around $18 million, with aluminum and related products ranking first, followed by antiquities and relics, and finally gums and herbal extracts.

Trade exchange between the two countries has increased by 35 percent due to non-oil exports and logistics at the Arar border crossing.

Saudi Arabia has a significant trade surplus, with exports mostly consisting of building materials, food, dairy products, and packaging.

The Arar border crossing has facilitated the movement of commercial vehicles and trade exhibitions.

Over 30 Saudi companies are operational in Iraq, and about 46 Iraqi companies are present in Saudi Arabia.

World.title: Evening news wrap: Govt, oppn clash as Lok Sabha discusses new anti-paper leak law; India rejects PoK legislative polls, and more
World.content:
The Lok Sabha witnessed a clash between the government and the opposition as the House took up the Centre's proposed amendments to the anti-paper leak law amid nationwide demands for stricter safeguards after the NEET (UG) paper leak.

A powerful 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck Japan's southern Kyushu region, triggering tsunami warnings and emergency alerts.

The ministry of external affairs described the legislative assembly elections being held in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoK) as a "cosmetic" attempt by Islamabad to legitimise its "illegal occupation" of the region.

(PoK) as a "cosmetic" attempt by Islamabad to legitimise its "illegal occupation" of the region. France appointed football legend Zinedine Zidane as their new head coach, ending months of speculation after Didier Deschamps stepped down following the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

The Delhi Police Retired Officers' Association has sought permission to hold a dharna at Jantar Mantar on July 31 in solidarity with security personnel injured during the Parliament protests in central Delhi on July 20.

Here are top news stories of the day

'Milestone legislation' vs 'Pradhan saved Pradhan Mantri': Centre, Oppn clash as Lok Sabha debates new anti-paper leak bill



Union minister Jitendra Singh introduced the Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, on Monday after the first week of Parliament's Monsoon session, which began on July 20, was washed out amid large-scale student protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP).

Parts of Japan's Kumamoto Castle walls collapse after 7.1-magnitude quake

According to the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA), the earthquake struck Kumamoto Prefecture at around 12:57 pm IST. The agency said the quake occurred at a shallow depth beneath the seabed.Videos circulating on social media showed sections of Kumamoto Castle's centuries-old stone walls collapsing, with large dust clouds rising near the castle's moat.

'Cosmetic exercise to camouflage illegal occupation': MEA rejects Pak-organised polls in PoK

Retired Delhi Police officers to hold dharna on July 31 over attacks on cops during âSansad Chaloâ



In a letter addressed to the Commissioner of Police, the association requested permission to stage a peaceful demonstration from 11 am to 5 pm at the designated protest site. The association also demanded the identification, arrest, and strict legal action against those responsible for assaulting police personnel and inciting violence during the 'Sansad Chalo' protest.





France's greatest icon returns! Zinedine Zidane appointed head coach



FFF president Philippe Diallo announced Zidane's arrival at the federation's headquarters in Paris, describing the appointment as a landmark moment for French football. "This is an exceptional moment, exceptional because of the person sat next to me," Diallo said. "Zidane is one of the legends of French soccer."

World.title: 'His personal thoughts': RSS distances itself from Kerala right-wing activist over Delhi student protest remarks
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

(RSS) on Tuesday distanced itself from right-wing political commentator TG Mohandas over his remarks on the recent student protests in Delhi, clarifying that he does not hold any position in the organisation.

Senior RSS functionary KB Sreekumar said Mohandas was not an office-bearer of the RSS at any level and described his remarks as "personal thoughts", adding that the comments deserved to be condemned.

"TG Mohandas's comments on the recent protest are his personal thoughts. He is not an RSS official at any level. RSS doesn't agree with his views and they should be condemned in every highest possible manner," Sreekumar told PTI.

The clarification came a day after Mohandas's remarks triggered widespread protests in Kerala and sparked outrage on social media, prompting the CPI-backed All India Students' Federation (AISF) to file a police complaint against him.

In its complaint to the Kerala DGP, the AISF alleged that Mohandas had called for student protesters to be "shot dead", amounting to an appeal for violence and mass killing.

According to the complaint, publicly advocating the use of state force to open fire on protesting students, with the possibility of deaths and grievous injuries, was an extremely dangerous statement that promoted violence, undermined the value of human life and had the potential to create fear and social unrest.





The student outfit sought registration of a criminal case against Mohandas under all applicable legal provisions and urged an investigation into the YouTube channel that carried the remarks, the source of the video, related digital records and its circulation across social media platforms.

The controversy stems from the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led student protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar over the NEET (UG) paper leak and broader education reforms.

The satirical online platform launched its indefinite agitation on June 21 and called it off on July 25 after then-Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned and the Centre accepted all three of its demands, one of which was Pradhan's resignation or ouster.

The RSS, which has now distanced itself from Mohandas's remarks, is the ideological mentor of the

, the party leading the government at the Centre.

World.title: 'Even her own party doesn't take her seriously, why should we?' CJP hits back at Kangana Ranaut
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has dismissed

's attack on young protesters, saying even her own party colleagues do not take her seriously so why should they.

"Even members of her own party don't pay much heed to Kangana Ranaut or take her seriously, so why should we?" CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das said.

"I don't think anyone in Gen Z, Gen Alpha, or any younger generation takes her seriously or listens to what she says.

"

Das pointed to Ranaut's own remarks from her Himachal Pradesh constituency, where she had said she expected the job to require very little work, only to realise being an MP involves massive labour. "That speaks volumes about her own seriousness," he added.

The BJP MP had launched a scathing attack on the young demonstrators who protested against the NEET paper leak, questioning their conduct while defending Prime Minister Narendra Modi against what she called "filthy abuse."

Ranaut specifically targeted the language used against PM Modi during the protests. "Our 75-year-old Prime Minister was targeted, and filthy abuse was hurled at his late mother," she said. She questioned whether such conduct befits students, adding, "We, too, have participated in student protests. But what kind of students are these, and what kind of obscene language are they using?"

The actor-politician drew a contrast between the protesters and her own journey, pointing out that she has been self-reliant since age 16.





"If these individuals need Supreme Court lawyers or legal counsel in the future, will their parents be able to afford it?" she asked. "They do not have the means to afford it themselves. We have been building our own careers since the age of sixteen. We have never been a burden on our parents.

"

Earlier on her Instagram stories, Ranaut had earlier called the protest reels "puke inducing" and used the term "Generation Gutter".

She dubbed Gen Z women as "so-called westernised Indian women" who are "not good at studies" and "so ugly and corrupt that they cannot be homemakers either."

"If you try to live independently without accountability, you are just a distorted entity. Gutter chap," she added.

The Mandi MP's remarks came as the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) wound up its 36-day agitation after the government conceded to its demands. Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Union education minister and Pralhad Joshi was given additional charge of the ministry, paving the way for the protest's withdrawal.

World.title: 'Garlanded as if he won a war': Opposition attacks BJP over Dharmendra Pradhan's felicitation after resignation
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A political row erupted in Parliament on Tuesday after the BJP's public felicitation of former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, who resigned over the NEET-UG paper leak controversy, drew sharp criticism from the Opposition.

Congress leaders accused the ruling party of celebrating a minister who resigned amid one of the country's biggest examination crises, saying he was welcomed "as if he were a superstar" and "had returned from a war against Pakistan".

The controversy stems from Monday's scenes at the Parliament complex, where BJP and NDA MPs welcomed Pradhan with chants of "Dharmendra Pradhan zindabad", draped him in a traditional stole and cap, and escorted him into the House in a show of solidarity just two days after his resignation.

What opposition said



Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra led the opposition's attack, calling it "shameful" that BJP MPs welcomed Pradhan in Parliament despite his resignation over the alleged NEET paper leak controversy.

"Don't you think it is shameful? Everyone saw the circumstances under which Dharmendra Pradhan resigned, but yesterday in the Parliament premises, he was welcomed as if he were a superstar!" she said.





She also accused the government of continuing to target students despite the controversy.

"No one can trust the Modi government, because even today, students are being harassed. I saw some Instagram handles with photographs of women alleging that they did such and such thing...Do you want to engage in talks to resolve this matter or you are still after the students, wanting to suppress them? This is wrong," Priyanka Gandhi said.

Speaking during the debate on the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 in the Lok Sabha, Congress MP Gaurav Gogoi echoed the criticism, saying Pradhan had been welcomed "as if he had returned from a war against Pakistan."

"...21 children lost their lives; they committed suicide. The minister under whose watch 21 children lost their lives, when he resigned from his post and returned to the House yesterday, you garlanded him as if he had returned from a war against Pakistan," Gogoi said.

The BJP's show of solidarity came after Pradhan resigned on Saturday following sustained protests over the alleged NEET paper leak. He has since been replaced by Union minister Prahlad Joshi.

Meanwhile, the government has announced a series of measures to overhaul the examination system, including a high-powered task force headed by Nandan Nilekani, proposed amendments to the anti-paper leak law, and fast-track courts to deal with examination fraud cases.

World.title: ITC Hotels signs Welcomhotel by ITC Hotels, Rajgir; strengthens presence in Bihar
World.content: NEW DELHI: Hospitality major ITC Hotels Ltd Tuesday announced the signing of a management agreement for a new Welcomhotel by ITC Hotels in Rajgir in the presence of Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary. The hotel will be developed under a long-term arrangement between the Bihar State Tourism Development Corporation and Kalsi Buildcon Pvt Ltd to promote Bihar as a tourist destination. Spread across 2.67 acres, the proposed hotel will have 107 keys.ITC Hotels MD Anil Chadha said: âBihar is home to some of India's most significant cultural & spiritual destinations, and we see immense long-term potential for hospitality-led tourism in the state. The signing of Welcomhotel Rajgir reinforces our promise to build a larger presence in Bihar. As domestic travel continues to evolve, travellers are increasingly seeking destinations that offer authentic experiences alongside branded hospitality. We look forward to this long-term association with Kalsi Buildcon Private Limited and to playing a meaningful role in elevating Bihar's tourism vision by bringing world-class experiences to one of India's most compelling travel destinations.âKalsi Buildcon Pvt Ltd director Sumeet Singh Kalsi said: âWe are delighted to collaborate with ITC Hotels to introduce the Welcomhotel brand in Rajgir, Bihar. With its deep historical significance and enduring appeal among visitors from across India and around the world, Rajgir presents a compelling opportunity for the development of a world-class hotel. Our vision is to create a landmark offering that reflects the essence of this region while catering to the evolving preferences of today's travellers. Combined with ITC Hotelsâ recognised service excellence, we are confident that this property will emerge as a distinguished addition to the state's growing travel landscape."âThis signing coupled with the recent signing of a new ITC Patna hotel and the opening of Welcomhotel Bodhgaya Hotel & Convention Centre, further strengthens ITC Hotelsâ presence in Bihar,â the hospitality major said in a statement.

World.title: 'Cosmetic exercise to camouflage illegal occupation': MEA rejects Pak-organised polls in PoK
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Tuesday dismissed the legislative assembly elections being held in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoK), calling the exercise a "cosmetic" attempt by Islamabad to legitimise its "illegal occupation" of the region.

Responding to reports on the polls, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal reiterated that the entire Union territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, including areas currently under Pakistan's control, are an integral part of India.

"We have seen reports regarding the so-called legislative assembly elections being conducted in the Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir... The entire union territories of Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh, including the areas currently under illegal and forcible occupation of Pakistan, are integral parts of India," he said.

"The current cosmetic electoral exercise is nothing but an attempt by Pakistan to camouflage its illegal occupation and hide its grave

in the region. The ongoing mass protest in the Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir is the direct consequence of its economic exploitation, its denial of fundamental rights to the people and its administrative oppression," he added.

PoK has been gripped by sustained protests for nearly two months, with demonstrators accusing the Pakistani authorities of political repression, economic exploitation and denying basic rights.





The unrest has now begun to overshadow the region's legislative assembly elections, prompting the postponement of polling in two constituencies and drawing criticism from international rights groups.

The latest escalation came on Monday when thousands of protesters marched towards Muzaffarabad after talks between the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) and the authorities collapsed, marking the 52nd day of the agitation.

The protest movement is being spearheaded by the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), which says it is fighting for greater political freedoms, economic relief and an end to what it describes as administrative oppression by Pakistani authorities.

World.title: 'Not an in-house probe ': AAIB explains to SC why AI171 crash report is getting delayed, to submit dossier in October
World.content:
The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) on Tuesday informed the Supreme Court that its investigation into the June 12, 2025 Air India Flight AI-171 crash, which claimed 260 lives, is not an "in-house" exercise limited to officials of the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), but also involves experts and officials from countries whose nationals were among the victims.

The submission was made during the hearing of petitions filed by the father of Captain Sumit Sabharwal and the Federation of Indian Pilots, who have sought a court-monitored investigation, alleging discrepancies in the ongoing probe.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant heard submissions from both the petitioners and the AAIB.

Final report to be submitted in October

During the hearing, the AAIB informed the court that the investigation includes simulation exercises and detailed technical analysis to reconstruct the sequence of events and determine the cause of the crash.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the AAIB, also assured the Bench that the draft final investigation report would be submitted to the Supreme Court in a sealed cover by October.

Probe delayed due to overseas examination

Explaining the revised timeline, Mehta said the investigation had taken longer than initially expected because several aircraft components had to be sent abroad for specialised forensic and technical examination before being returned to India.





He told the court that these examinations were essential for a comprehensive investigation, making the process more time-consuming than originally anticipated.

The matter came up as the petitioners sought greater judicial oversight over the probe into one of India's deadliest aviation disasters.

Air India's Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner, operating Flight AI-171 from Ahmedabad to London Gatwick, crashed shortly after take-off on June 12, 2025, killing 260 people. The aircraft was piloted by Captain Sumeet Sabharwal and First Officer Clive Kunder. Former Gujarat Chief Minister Vijay Rupani was among those killed.

World.title: 'Modiji clocked it': BJP MP's Gen Z-style praise for PM during anti-paper leak Bill debate
World.content:
BJP MP's Gen Z-style praise for PM during anti-paper leak Bill debate

NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party Lok Sabha member Bansuri Swaraj on Tuesday used a Gen Z term to praise the steps taken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi against the paper leak. She said that the PM had "clocked it" with the anti-paper leak Bill, a term used by the younger generation to recognize a fact.Speaking in favour of the Bill during the debate, she said, "Borrowing Gen Z's language, I would have to say that Modiji clocked it at providing this legislative solution"."I am standing in support of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026. This is a transformative amendment. Its necessity is not only evident, but it is also the demand of the present time. Bringing this amendment is proof of the sensitivity of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his committed government. Speaker Sir, when a competitive examination is compromised, its impact is not limited to the candidate whose future is put at stake," she added.The government has proposed amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act to ensure time-bound investigations, speedy trials and tougher penalties for paper leaks and organised exam fraud.Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced on Sunday the formation of a high-powered task force, headed by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani, to overhaul India's examination system and make it more transparent, reliable and technology-driven.Addressing students through a video message, PM Modi said the Centre had already taken steps to curb exam malpractice by jailing those involved, setting up fast-track courts and proposing stricter legal provisions, but stressed that broader systemic reforms were now needed.He said the task force would recommend measures to strengthen the credibility of public examinations, with the government acting on its report at the earliest. The Nilekani-led panel will study the use of technology and suggest reforms to improve transparency, efficiency and trust in the conduct of public examinations.The move comes in the wake of recent controversies surrounding competitive examinations, including the NEET row, as the Centre seeks to restore confidence in the system.

World.title: Zelenskyy will visit Trump at the White House before Lindsey Graham’s funeral
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy will meet Tuesday (July 28, 2026) ahead of Sen. Lindsey Graham’s funeral, their second sit-down this month and after a far-right activist with the U.S. president’s ear had a widely publicized change of heart on Russia’s war against Ukraine.

Mr. Trump is set to welcome Mr. Zelenskyy to the White House as the Ukrainian leader travels to Washington to honour Graham, whose final act as a public official was visiting Kyiv and securing an agreement on a package of sanctions that seek to punish countries that purchase Russian oil, gas and other exports.

Mr. Zelenskyy posted on X early on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) that he had arrived in the U.S. and listed the goals for his visit.

“Our schedule includes meetings with President Trump, his team, and those who can support our defense,” the Ukrainian leader said. “Our number one priority is anti-ballistic defense and strategic cooperation with America. Peace needs to be brought closer.”

Mr. Zelenskyy is now being bolstered by an unusual source: Laura Loomer, known primarily for her incendiary social media posts and her influence with the president. Traveling through Ukraine, Ms. Loomer has witnessed Moscow’s barrage firsthand and interviewed Mr. Zelenskyy while admitting she was “bamboozled by Russian propaganda.”

Ms. Loomer said she spoke to Mr. Trump after she met with Mr. Zelenskyy in Ukraine last week, and she also expects to meet with the U.S. president once she returns from her trip.

“It’s looking good for Ukraine, right?” Ms. Loomer said during an interview with The Associated Press. “Going into this meeting next week at the Oval Office is looking pretty good.”

Russia’s support for Iran

Ahead of the meeting, Mr. Zelenskyy has also warned that Russia has been aiding Iran as the war persists by capturing satellite imagery of U.S. bases in the Gulf region that later appear in Iran. The Ukrainian president also asserted that there was a “clear correlation” between Russia’s images and subsequent Iranian strikes.

“The purpose is clear,” Mr. Zelenskyy said earlier this month. “None of us in the world should turn a blind eye to one very simple fact: Evil always seeks ways to make things worse and spread further.”

On Monday (July 27m, 2026), Mr. Trump downplayed any impact of potential Russian assistance for Iran.

“I don’t think they’ve been doing it, certainly not at a high level,” Mr. Trump told reporters on Air Force One as he travelled to Michigan. “And if they have, it has been very un-impactful.”

Still, he said he would raise the issue with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Mr. Zelenskyy has a busy itinerary during his latest visit to Washington. In addition to his White House meeting, Mr. Zelenskyy will head to the Capitol to meet with senators on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) evening after Graham’s funeral at Washington National Cathedral, according to a person with knowledge of the meeting who was not authorised to discuss it publicly and spoke on condition of anonymity.

Republican leadership is hoping to advance Graham’s sanctions legislation this week, although the Senate is juggling several other priorities before lawmakers leave Washington for the August recess.

The bill has dozens of backers from both parties and is seen as the main policy tribute to Graham, who died unexpectedly this month from a tear in his aorta. It imposes tariffs on goods from the world’s top five purchasers of Russia oil or natural gas, including China and India.

The legislation also includes sanctions against Mr. Putin, senior Russian political and military leaders, and Russian financial institutions and energy projects.

Mr. Trump met with Mr. Zelenskyy on the sidelines of the NATO summit earlier this month in Ankara, Turkiye, and announced that the U.S. will give Ukraine a license to make Patriot air defense systems, a long-running request from Kyiv in order to counter Russian missile attacks.

The air defence systems are expensive to make and are in high demand. Noting that he and Mr. Zelenskyy have “actually developed a good relationship,” Mr. Trump said the U.S. will help Ukraine produce the Patriots and that the country would be able to produce them “pretty quickly.”

World.title: Top news of the day: Supreme Court moots independent probe into police excesses in CJP protest; major quake hits Japan, and more
World.content:
Supreme Court moots independent probe into police excesses, orders release of detained minors

The Supreme Court on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) observed that it would consider constituting a high-powered investigating team to conduct a “thorough, fair and independent” inquiry into allegations of police excesses during the recent student protests in Delhi and several other States, while ordering the immediate release of all minors arrested in connection with the demonstrations and restraining the police from taking coercive action against protesting students unless they had criminal antecedents.

Japan earthquake: ‘Considerable’ number of people reported dead in Kumamoto mall after earthquake

A “considerable number” of people have died in a shopping mall damaged by a major earthquake on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) in southwestern Japan, broadcaster TBS said. Police told AFP that they could not confirm whether there were any fatalities at the mall in the town of Kashima. Emergency services earlier said “many people” were trapped inside the building after a floor collapsed.

Rajya Sabha MP moves Supreme Court against use of facial recognition technology at NEET protests

Rajya Sabha Member of Parliament A.A. Rahim moved the Supreme Court on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) against the deployment of facial recognition technology and allied mass surveillance measures by the Delhi Police against students and persons who participated in the Cockroach Janta Party-linked protests over the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test-Undergraduate (NEET-UG) exam paper leaks.

Tamil Nadu CM Vijay seeks PM Modi’s intervention in Mekedatu issue

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, on Tuesday (July 28, 2026), wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi seeking his intervention to ensure no statutory or administrative approval is granted to the Mekedatu project unless it is demonstrably consistent with the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal (CWDT) Award and the judgment of the Supreme Court.

Cauvery Water Regulation Committee orders Karnataka to release 3,500 cusecs of water a day for 15 days to Tamil Nadu

The Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC), which met in Delhi on Tuesday (July 28, 2026), has directed Karnataka to release 4 tmcft of water to Tamil Nadu at a rate of 3,500 cusecs a day for 15 days. Expressing concern over the CWRC order that has come when the State is gripped by serious drought, Karnataka Water Resources Minister K. Ramalinga Reddy has said the State would examine the possibility of filing an appeal before the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA), which is the apex body that monitors implementation of Cauvery water release, against the CWRC order.

Cockroaches spreading their filth, who is birthing them?: Kangana Ranaut on CJP-led protests

Actor and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut has kicked up a row with her social media tirade against those who took part in the Cockroach Janata Party-led protests, calling Gen Z as “generation gutter” and their videos from the agitation “puke inducing”.

PM Modi cancelled Bihar tour realising BJP will lose Bankipur bypoll: Tejashwi

RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) claimed that Prime Minister Narendra Modi “cancelled his tour of Bihar” upon realising that the student unrest and the “growing unpopularity” of his government would lead to BJP’s defeat in the Bankipur Assembly bypoll. There has been no word from the BJP government in the State on the PM’s tour.

Welcomed him as if he were a superstar: Priyanka slams BJP MPs for felicitating Pradhan

Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) said it was “shameful” that BJP MPs welcomed Dharmendra Pradhan, who recently resigned as the Education Minister, at the Parliament premises “as if he were a superstar”. Two days after his resignation following large-scale student protests, Mr. Pradhan was welcomed by some party colleagues in the Parliament complex with a traditional cap and stole, and shouting “Pradhan Zindabad”.

Instamart CEO Amitesh Kumar Jha resigns, Nandita Sinha to replace him

Amitesh Kumar Jha, CEO of Swiggy-owned quick commerce platform Instamart, has resigned to pursue other opportunities, a regulatory filing said on Tuesday (July 28, 2026). Nandita Sinha has been appointed as CEO — Instamart with effect from August 3, 2026, Swiggy informed in the filing. Nandita joins from Myntra, where she served as Chief Executive Officer (CEO).

Zelenskyy will visit Trump at the White House before Lindsey Graham’s funeral

U.S. President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy will meet Tuesday (July 28, 2026) ahead of Sen. Lindsey Graham’s funeral, their second sit-down this month and after a far-right activist with the U.S. president’s ear had a widely publicised change of heart on Russia’s war against Ukraine.

No non-veg at eateries along Kanwar Yatra route in Muzaffarnagar; owners need to display paper work

Hotels and roadside eateries on the Kanwar Yatra route are banned from cooking and serving non-vegetarian food, and they have been directed to put up owners’ paperwork, including licences, on display, officials said on Tuesday (July 28, 2026). Ahead of the Kanwar Yatra, which begins July 30, the Food Safety Department has also started a drive to check shops and eateries across the yatra route in Muzaffarnagar, saying this is done every year.

World.title: Japan earthquake LIVE updates: Govt. sets up task force to assess possible damage, prepare rescue operations, says PM Takaichi
World.content:
An earthquake registering a magnitude of 7.1 shook Kumamoto on Japan’s southern main island of Kyushu late Tuesday (July 28, 2026) afternoon, causing damage and injuries, officials said. A tsunami advisory was temporarily issued but was lifted within two hours, the Japan Meteorological Agency said.

Also read | Japan earthquake: ‘Considerable’ number of people reported dead in Kumamoto mall after earthquake

Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, in a message posted on X, said her government has set up a task force to gather information, assess possible damage and prepare for rescue operations if needed.

Ms. Takaichi later told reporters that there have been reports of a number of injuries and damages to roads, bridges and buildings, as well as blackouts and fire, though details are still unclear. Ms. Takaichi warned people cooking to be careful with fire and with shards of broken glass.

In “Kashima town, a shopping complex’s second floor collapsed, leaving many people trapped inside,” the fire department said in a statement.

Police said earlier they had received reports of what sounded like an explosion at the Aeon Mall outlet in Kumamoto, with no information on damage or any casualties.

World.title: Davangere University to introduce skill-based programmes from current academic year
World.content:
With an aim to enhance the skills of the students, Davangere University plans to introduce various postgraduate diploma and certificate courses alongside undergraduate and postgraduate programmes from the current academic year.

Addressing reporters in Davangere on Tuesday, Vice-Chancellor B.E. Rangaswamy said that the focus was on skill-based education. “Emphasis is being placed on multidisciplinary education, with the objective of offering vocational, skill-oriented, and employment-generating degree programmes,” he said.

Mr. Rangaswamy said that these courses were aimed at equipping students with specialised knowledge in their chosen fields and prepare them for employment or self-employment.

“We already have introduced Postgraduate Diploma in Cyber Security, financial services, data analysis, food processing, safety and quality management and diploma and certificate courses in Yoga. In addition, the university is preparing to launch skill-based practical education through certificate and PG Diploma courses across undergraduate and postgraduate programmes in the faculties of commerce, science, social sciences, and education from the current academic year,” he said.

Emphasising that the focus was on producing entrepreneurs rather than job seekers, Mr. Rangaswamy said that students should develop the ability to create employment opportunities for others. “The university has already entered into collaborations with several national and international organisations and companies in this regard,” he said.

Elaborating on the importance given to research, the Vice-Chancellor said that the university had signed agreements on research collaboration with multiple institutions and would continue utilising all available resources to further strengthen the research ecosystem and elevate the institution to higher standards.

Deadline extended

Mr. Rangaswamy also announced that the deadline for submitting applications for admission to postgraduate courses for the current academic year had been extended from July 31 to August 10.

The decision has been taken in the wake of requests from scores of students and college principals. Admissions are open for MA, MCom, MSc, MEd, MFA, MSW, and MCA programmes.

Replying to a query, Mr. Rangaswamy said that the university currently had 129 full-time experienced faculty members, well-equipped laboratories, digital library facilities, student hostels, and career guidance services. Also, 30 postgraduate programmes are offered on the Shivagangotri campus in Davangere and the Postgraduate Centre at Guddada Rangavvanahalli in Chitradurga district.

Finance officer R. Shashidhar, dean of social sciences M.U. Lokesh, dean of commerce and business administration K.T. Srinivasa, principal of the College of Visual Arts Satish Vallepure and head of the Department of Journalism Shivakumar Kanasogi were present.

World.title: Instamart CEO Amitesh Kumar Jha resigns, Nandita Sinha to replace him

World.title: No non-veg at eateries along Kanwar Yatra route in Muzaffarnagar; owners need to display paper work
World.content:
Hotels and roadside eateries on the Kanwar Yatra route are banned from cooking and serving non-vegetarian food and they have been directed to put up owners' paper work, including licence, on display, officials said on Tuesday (July 28, 2026).

Ahead of the Kanwar Yatra which begins July 30, the Food Safety Department has also started a drive to check shops and eateries across the yatra route in Muzaffarnagar, saying this is done every year.

"Cooking and serving non-vegetarian foods in hotels and dhabas have been banned on the Kanwar Yatra route. The hotel and dhaba owners have also been told not to use onions and garlic in cooking and serving food," Assistant Commissioner Food [Muzaffarnagar] Archana Dheeran on Tuesday (July 28, 2026), told PTI.

"Hotels and dhabas have been following this norm every year. Any new hotel or dhaba, which comes up, is informed about this by the department," she said.

Six teams of the officials have been formed for checking food items. "Stale food will not be allowed in these dhabas," Ms. Dheeran said.

She added that steps have been taken for food safety measures and eateries have been directed to display owners' details, licence and food safety connect app QR codes.

The District authorities have set a standard rate for 21 essential items to prevent over-charging. The Food Safety Department has directed that cooks must wear gloves, and artificial colours are strictly prohibited in food items.

World.title: Ashada Fridays: No recommendation letters allowed for vehicle entry to Chamundi hill
World.content:
The Mysuru district administration has ruled out considering recommendation letters for vehicle entry to Chamundi Hills during Ashada Fridays, stating that no passes will be issued based on such requests, to ensure the smooth movement of devotees.

Deputy Commissioner G. Lakshmikanth Reddy said that except for vehicles covered under the prescribed security protocol, no other vehicles will be permitted to enter Chamundi Hills during Ashada Fridays. The restrictions have been imposed in view of the heavy influx of devotees visiting the Chamundeshwari Temple from across Karnataka and neighbouring States.

Clarifying the restrictions, the Deputy Commissioner, in a press release, said entry permissions for private vehicles have been withdrawn and that any recommendation letters seeking vehicle entry will not be entertained. “No vehicle passes will be issued on the basis of such recommendations,” he added.

The release said special traffic management and security arrangements have been put in place to facilitate safe, peaceful and hassle-free darshan while ensuring devotees are provided with the necessary basic amenities. The safety and convenience of pilgrims remains the administration’s top priority, it added.

The district administration has appealed to the public and devotees to cooperate in the strict implementation of the restrictions to ensure orderly traffic management and smooth darshan of Goddess Chamundeshwari during Ashada Fridays.

World.title: Cockroaches spreading their filth, who is birthing them?: Kangana Ranaut on CJP-led protests
World.content:
Actor and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut has kicked up a row with her social media tirade against those who took part in the Cockroach Janata Party-led protests, calling Gen Z as "generation gutter" and their videos from the agitation "puke inducing".

Her remarks came days after the 36-day agitation, led by the CJP along with students and civil society groups, ended on July 25 after the government accepted the protesters' key demands, including the resignation of then Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

In a post on Instagram on Monday (July 27, 2026), the BJP MP from Himachal Pradesh's Mandi described videos of protestors at Jantar Mantar a display of "filth, garbage and ugliness".

"Never in my life I have seen so much ugliness in one place, these reels from GenZ protests are puke inducing, the way they speak and the kind of language they are using, never in my life I have seen everything in each and every frame so jarring and so crass all at ones, ewwww who is birthing and raising them?" Ms. Ranaut said.

"India is a place of diversely beautiful people, draped in elegance and rooted in cultural sophistication, you call yourself cockroaches and look/ behave like them as well there is no paradox or juxtaposition there, just simply subjecting the world to your filth, garbage and ugliness. I am scarred from these reels, need some healing, digital detox," she added.

In another post, the actor took aim at young women participating in the protests, saying their behaviour during the agitation was "most appalling".

"Women who are truly independent they make rebellious choices, bold opinions, unconventional career moves and they take accountability for their actions. They have to cos they are on their own. They don't do this at the cost of their parents or families," she added.

"Here is a new generation of so called westernised Indian women. I call them Generation gutter," she said.

Ms. Ranaut said some of the women protestors were "so ugly and corrupt that they can't be home makers either".

"They proudly flaunt their freedom to have drugs, drinks or endless body counts and shamelessly live off their patents earnings and constantly fight to live independent lives without actually being independent.

"Gentle reminder independent life needs to be earned. If you try to live independently without accountability, you are just a distorted entity, gutter chaap," she added.

In her latest post on Tuesday (July 28, 2026), Ms. Ranaut defended those who have confronted protesters over their social media content, saying criticism and backlash were inevitable consequences of their actions.

"Protesters who are getting beaten and abused on the roads by ordinary people because of their filthy and abusive reels must understand that if you speak, you also have to be prepared to listen. If you damage public property, then the public will damage you too.

"If you have a problem with the country and its leadership and have publicly hurled filthy abuses at them, then now listen to those who love this country and brought this government to power through their votes. Because they also have the right to speak," she wrote.

Quoting Newton's third law of motion, the actor added, "Every action has equal and opposite reaction. If studying hasn't helped you understand cause and effect, now you will understand it very well."

Ms. Ranaut's statements went viral on social media with many criticising the actor for her "crass comments".

Congress leaders Renuka Chowdhury and Imran Pratapgarhi slammed the language she used to describe the young.

"It is unfortunate that a woman writes such things for getting praise from the government. When as an MP, you write such things, then I can only say that they are learning all this from you only. I think she will have to face consequences soon enough," Ms. Chowdhury told a television channel.

Congress MP Imran Pratapgarhi told reporters, "I think its reply will be given to her by the country's Gen Z..."

One social media user referred to Ms. Ranaut's past statements about Shaheen Bagh protests and actor Urmila Matondkar to point out that she had used derogatory language in the past.

"Kangana Ranaut posted this story, criticizing the language used in student protests. This is the same person who branded Urmila Matondkar a ‘soft porn star’ and mocked elderly women at the Farmers’ and Shaheen Bagh protests by claiming they were available to join for 100," the user said.

Another X user called her a hypocrite. "For someone who talks a whole lot of nothing and picks a non issue every other month to bully others… She sure has a lot of opinions on young students taking a stand for their own rights. The kind of language BJP/RSS use on the daily… I think she’d find the Gen Z’s terminology very tame as opposed to the party she belongs to," the person posted.

A user said Ms. Ranaut's comments were "weapons-grade cringe".

"How do you go from being a woman in power to using your platform to spew bitter 14 yr old incel level toxicity at women online? Bricks for brains, honestly," she said.
